Dear Sir/ Ma’am, 
 
1. 
This is to inform you that the Board of Directors of Mahindra & Mahindra Limited (“the Company”), at its 
Meeting held on 5th November 2026, has inter-alia approved the Unaudited Standalone and Consolidated 
Financial Results of the Company for the Second Quarter and Half year ended 30th September 2026. 
 
We are enclosing the Unaudited Standalone and Consolidated Financial Results of the Company for the 
Second Quarter and Half year ended 30th September 2026, along with the Limited Review Report thereon, 
issued by the Statutory Auditors, B S R & Co. LLP, Chartered Accountants as Annexure-1. 
 
2. 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI LODR Regulations, we also hereby inform you that Ms. Shuchi Suri, 
Executive Vice-President, Mahindra Experiences, Senior Management Personnel of the Company shall 
transition to the role of the Chief Sales & Marketing Officer - Automotive Business of the Company with effect 
from 1st April 2027. Consequent to this transition, she will cease to be a Senior Management Personnel of the 
Company. The details as required under Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR Regulations read with SEBI Master 
Circular are given hereunder as Annexure-2. 
 
The aforesaid meeting commenced at 11:00 a.m. and concluded at 12:47 p.m.

Outcome of Board Meeting of Mahindra & Mahindra Limited held on 5th November 2026 
 
Ref: 
▪ Regulations 30 (read with schedule III Part A & B), 33, 51 and 52 of the Securities and Exchange Board 
of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI LODR 
Regulations”) 
▪ SEBI Master Circular No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFDPOD2/I/3762/2026 dated 30th January 2026 (“SEBI 
Master Circular”) 
▪ Intimation of Board Meeting dated 24th September 2026 
 
 
Dear Sir/ Ma’am, 
 
1. 
This is to inform you that the Board of Directors of Mahindra & Mahindra Limited (“the Company”), at its 
Meeting held on 5th November 2026, has inter-alia approved the Unaudited Standalone and Consolidated 
Financial Results of the Company for the Second Quarter and Half year ended 30th September 2026. 
 
We are enclosing the Unaudited Standalone and Consolidated Financial Results of the Company for the 
Second Quarter and Half year ended 30th September 2026, along with the Limited Review Report thereon, 
issued by the Statutory Auditors, B S R & Co. LLP, Chartered Accountants as Annexure-1. 
 
2. 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI LODR Regulations, we also hereby inform you that Ms. Shuchi Suri, 
Executive Vice-President, Mahindra Experiences, Senior Management Personnel of the Company shall 
transition to the role of the Chief Sales & Marketing Officer - Automotive Business of the Company with effect 
from 1st April 2027. Consequent to this transition, she will cease to be a Senior Management Personnel of the 
Company. The details as required under Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR Regulations read with SEBI Master 
Circular are given hereunder as Annexure-2. 
 
The aforesaid meeting commenced at 11:00 a.m. and concluded at 12:47 p.m.  
 
This intimation is also being uploaded on the Company’s website at https://www.mahindra.com  
 
Yours sincerely, 
 
For Mahindra & Mahindra Limited

Dear Sir/ Ma’am, 
 
1. 
This is to inform you that the Board of Directors of Mahindra & Mahindra Limited (“the Company”), at its 
Meeting held on 5th November 2026, has inter-alia approved the Unaudited Standalone and Consolidated 
Financial Results of the Company for the Second Quarter and Half year ended 30th September 2026. 
 
We are enclosing the Unaudited Standalone and Consolidated Financial Results of the Company for the 
Second Quarter and Half year ended 30th September 2026, along with the Limited Review Report thereon, 
issued by the Statutory Auditors, B S R & Co. LLP, Chartered Accountants as Annexure-1. 
 
2. 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI LODR Regulations, we also hereby inform you that Ms. Shuchi Suri, 
Executive Vice-President, Mahindra Experiences, Senior Management Personnel of the Company shall 
transition to the role of the Chief Sales & Marketing Officer - Automotive Business of the Company with effect 
from 1st April 2027. Consequent to this transition, she will cease to be a Senior Management Personnel of the 
Company. The details as required under Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR Regulations read with SEBI Master 
Circular are given hereunder as Annexure-2.

Outcome of Board Meeting of Mahindra & Mahindra Limited held on 5th November 2026 
 
Ref: 
▪ Regulations 30 (read with schedule III Part A & B), 33, 51 and 52 of the Securities and Exchange Board 
of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI LODR 
Regulations”) 
▪ SEBI Master Circular No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFDPOD2/I/3762/2026 dated 30th January 2026 (“SEBI 
Master Circular”) 
▪ Intimation of Board Meeting dated 24th September 2026 
 
 
Dear Sir/ Ma’am, 
 
1. 
This is to inform you that the Board of Directors of Mahindra & Mahindra Limited (“the Company”), at its 
Meeting held on 5th November 2026, has inter-alia approved the Unaudited Standalone and Consolidated 
Financial Results of the Company for the Second Quarter and Half year ended 30th September 2026. 
 
We are enclosing the Unaudited Standalone and Consolidated Financial Results of the Company for the 
Second Quarter and Half year ended 30th September 2026, along with the Limited Review Report thereon, 
issued by the Statutory Auditors, B S R & Co. LLP, Chartered Accountants as Annexure-1. 
 
2. 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI LODR Regulations, we also hereby inform you that Ms. Shuchi Suri, 
Executive Vice-President, Mahindra Experiences, Senior Management Personnel of the Company shall 
transition to the role of the Chief Sales & Marketing Officer - Automotive Business of the Company with effect 
from 1st April 2027. Consequent to this transition, she will cease to be a Senior Management Personnel of the 
Company. The details as required under Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR Regulations read with SEBI Master 
Circular are given hereunder as Annexure-2. 
 
The aforesaid meeting commenced at 11:00 a.m. and concluded at 12:47 p.m.  
 
This intimation is also being uploaded on the Company’s website at https://www.mahindra.com  
 
Yours sincerely, 
 
For Mahindra & Mahindra Limited

1 
Media release  
APSEZ agrees to acquire 100% of Evos B.V., Europe’s 2nd largest independent liquid storage 
operator, at an enterprise value of €2.56 bn 
• Transaction establishes a major European liquids platform for APSEZ, comprising eight port 
terminals in five countries. Evos is valued at 11.7x CY25 EV/EBITDA  
 
• Evos delivered CY25 revenue and EBITDA at €392 mn & €219 mn respectively (56% EBITDA 
margin)  
 
• Evos has 6.3 mn cubic meters of storage capacity and handled 37 MMT of throughput during 
CY25. Evos adds a high-margin, cash-generative liquids business to APSEZ’s portfolio with 
average commercial occupancy at 99% and substantial part of revenue under take-or-pay 
contracts and CPI-linked contract base  
 
• The transaction will strengthen APSEZ’s business risk profile by increasing the scale, 
geographic diversity, and cash flow of the combined platform  
 
• APSEZ’s global footprint now expands to 28 ports and terminals across 10 countries  
 
• The regulatory approval processes and works council consultation process will start 
immediately 
 
5 November 2026, Ahmedabad: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited (APSEZ), India’s 
largest and one of the world’s fastest growing Integrated Transport Operator, agrees to acquire 
100% stake in Netherlands-headquartered Evos B.V. (Evos) from Igneo Infrastructure Partners. The 
proposed transaction is an all-cash deal at an enterprise value of €2.56 bn. The transaction values 
Evos at an equity value of €1.18 bn, implying an acquisition multiple of 11.7x CY25 EV/EBITDA. For 
CY25, Evos delivered revenue and EBITDA at €392 mn & €219 mn respectively (56% EBITDA margin). 
Pro forma net debt-to-EBITDA for the combined entity stands at 2.76x (based on APSEZ FY26 and 
Evos CY25 financials) and is expected to be around 2.5x by FY27. The transaction will be funded via 
debt and is subject to regulatory and other approvals and works council consultation.  
“Evos marks an important milestone in APSEZ’s trajectory towards handling 1 billion tons of cargo 
and building a truly global, integrated transport platform. We are delighted to welcome Evos into 
our portfolio, giving us significant presence across key global liquid storage and energy hubs. We 
look forward to partnering with Europe, supporting its sustainable energy transition and creating 
enduring value while maintaining the financial prudence that underpins our growth,” said Mr. Karan 
Adani, Managing Director, APSEZ. 
Evos is Europe’s second-largest independent liquid storage operator with 6.3 mn cubic meters of 
storage capacity at eight strategically located port-based terminals across the Netherlands, 
Germany, Spain, Belgium and Malta. Evos’ terminals are positioned in Europe’s most important 
energy and industrial hubs, including the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) region, Hamburg 
and the Mediterranean. The platform comprises 452 tanks, 63 vessels and barge berths, and has 
several integrated pipeline connectivities (including Schiphol airport and Central Europe Pipeline 
System). Evos handled 37 MMT of throughput in CY25. Evos operates a diversified liquids platform 
spanning both conventional and transition fuels. Its product mix includes gasoline, gasoil, marine 
fuels and jet fuel, alongside transition fuels such as sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), biofuels, 
methanol and bioethanol, positioning the business to participate in Europe’s evolving energy mix. 
Evos is an investment-grade rated issuer. 

BSE: 532921 | NSE: ADANIPORTS | Bloomberg: ADSEZ:IN | Reuters: APSE.NS 
                        
 
2 
Evos has a diversified roster of Tier-1 customers, including global energy majors, leading industrial 
and chemical companies, and commodity traders. Its business model provides high revenue and 
cash flow visibility, underpinned by tenured customer relationships, average 99% commercial 
occupancy, and substantial part of revenue under take-or-pay contracts and CPI-linked contract 
base.  
Evos is a strong strategic fit with APSEZ’s ambition to build a globally diversified integrated 
transport platform. The acquisition establishes a sizeable European foothold, materially scales and 
diversifies APSEZ’s liquids portfolio, and provides exposure to the long-term transition toward new-
age fuels. Importantly, Evos adds high-margin, predictable hard-currency cash flows backed by high 
take-or-pay revenues and CPI-linked contract base, strengthening the quality, resilience and 
geographic diversification of APSEZ’s earnings. Evos’ 56% EBITDA margin is above APSEZ’s H1 FY27 
International Ports margin of 44.8%, underscoring the margin-accretive nature of the business. 
As of Q2 FY27, ended 30 September 2026, APSEZ had a cash balance of ₹12,502 Cr. APSEZ’s 
International Ports portfolio sustained its strong momentum, delivering record revenue and EBITDA 
of ₹3,586 Cr and ₹1,608 Cr respectively, with the EBITDA margin reaching a record 44.8% in H1FY27. 
Volumes increased to 47 MMT from 17 MMT in H1 FY26. The performance was led by the continued 
ramp-up of Colombo West International Terminal (CWIT) and Tanzania operations and contribution 
from NQXT Australia.  
MUFG is the sole underwriter and has provided financing commitments for up to €2.8 billion for the 
proposed transaction. Linklaters and Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas have acted as international and 
domestic legal counsel for APSEZ.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

BSE: 532921 | NSE: ADANIPORTS | Bloomberg: ADSEZ:IN | Reuters: APSE.NS 
                        
 
3 
About APSEZ 
 
APSEZ, part of the globally diversified Adani Group, a leading Integrated Transport Operator--across cargo 
origination (International Freight Network) through port handling, rail transport, multi-modal logistics parks, 
warehousing, and final delivery via road transport to customer gates.   
 
This comprehensive "shore-to-door" capability, supported by cutting-edge digital infrastructure and AI-driven 
optimization, positions APSEZ as India's preeminent integrated logistics solutions provider. The company 
operates a comprehensive ecosystem of 16 strategically located ports and terminals across India's west, south, 
and east coasts, combined with a diversified marine fleet of 138 vessels, integrated logistics capabilities 
including 12 multi-modal logistics parks, 3.1 million sq. ft. of warehouses, and 40,000+ trucks operating on its 
proprietary platform, thus providing capabilities to handle vast amounts of cargo from both coastal areas and 
the hinterland. APSEZ also operates 4 international ports across Australia, Colombo, Israel and Tanzania.  With 
a current cargo handling capacity of 671 million tonnes per annum, APSEZ commands approximately 27% of 
India's total port volumes, targeting 1 billion tonnes throughput by FY31.  
 
Recognized among the Top 5% of global transportation and transportation infrastructure firms in the 2025 
S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment (95th percentile globally), with five ports featuring in the 
World Bank's Container Port Performance Index 2024, APSEZ combines scale, operational excellence, and 
integrated capabilities to enable seamless global trade.

Media release  
APSEZ agrees to acquire 100% of Evos B.V., Europe’s 2nd largest independent liquid storage 
operator, at an enterprise value of €2.56 bn 
• Transaction establishes a major European liquids platform for APSEZ, comprising eight port 
terminals in five countries. Evos is valued at 11.7x CY25 EV/EBITDA  
 
• Evos delivered CY25 revenue and EBITDA at €392 mn & €219 mn respectively (56% EBITDA 
margin)  
 
• Evos has 6.3 mn cubic meters of storage capacity and handled 37 MMT of throughput during 
CY25. Evos adds a high-margin, cash-generative liquids business to APSEZ’s portfolio with 
average commercial occupancy at 99% and substantial part of revenue under take-or-pay 
contracts and CPI-linked contract base  
 
• The transaction will strengthen APSEZ’s business risk profile by increasing the scale, 
geographic diversity, and cash flow of the combined platform  
 
• APSEZ’s global footprint now expands to 28 ports and terminals across 10 countries  
 
• The regulatory approval processes and works council consultation process will start 
immediately 
 
5 November 2026, Ahmedabad: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited (APSEZ), India’s 
largest and one of the world’s fastest growing Integrated Transport Operator, agrees to acquire 
100% stake in Netherlands-headquartered Evos B.V. (Evos) from Igneo Infrastructure Partners. The 
proposed transaction is an all-cash deal at an enterprise value of €2.56 bn. The transaction values 
Evos at an equity value of €1.18 bn, implying an acquisition multiple of 11.7x CY25 EV/EBITDA. For 
CY25, Evos delivered revenue and EBITDA at €392 mn & €219 mn respectively (56% EBITDA margin). 
Pro forma net debt-to-EBITDA for the combined entity stands at 2.76x (based on APSEZ FY26 and 
Evos CY25 financials) and is expected to be around 2.5x by FY27. The transaction will be funded via 
debt and is subject to regulatory and other approvals and works council consultation.  
“Evos marks an important milestone in APSEZ’s trajectory towards handling 1 billion tons of cargo 
and building a truly global, integrated transport platform. We are delighted to welcome Evos into 
our portfolio, giving us significant presence across key global liquid storage and energy hubs. We 
look forward to partnering with Europe, supporting its sustainable energy transition and creating 
enduring value while maintaining the financial prudence that underpins our growth,” said Mr. Karan 
Adani, Managing Director, APSEZ. 
Evos is Europe’s second-largest independent liquid storage operator with 6.3 mn cubic meters of 
storage capacity at eight strategically located port-based terminals across the Netherlands, 
Germany, Spain, Belgium and Malta. Evos’ terminals are positioned in Europe’s most important 
energy and industrial hubs, including the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) region, Hamburg 
and the Mediterranean. The platform comprises 452 tanks, 63 vessels and barge berths, and has 
several integrated pipeline connectivities (including Schiphol airport and Central Europe Pipeline 
System). Evos handled 37 MMT of throughput in CY25. Evos operates a diversified liquids platform 
spanning both conventional and transition fuels. Its product mix includes gasoline, gasoil, marine 
fuels and jet fuel, alongside transition fuels such as sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), biofuels, 
methanol and bioethanol, positioning the business to participate in Europe’s evolving energy mix. 
Evos is an investment-grade rated issuer. 

BSE: 532921 | NSE: ADANIPORTS | Bloomberg: ADSEZ:IN | Reuters: APSE.NS 
                        
 
2 
Evos has a diversified roster of Tier-1 customers, including global energy majors, leading industrial 
and chemical companies, and commodity traders. Its business model provides high revenue and 
cash flow visibility, underpinned by tenured customer relationships, average 99% commercial 
occupancy, and substantial part of revenue under take-or-pay contracts and CPI-linked contract 
base.  
Evos is a strong strategic fit with APSEZ’s ambition to build a globally diversified integrated 
transport platform. The acquisition establishes a sizeable European foothold, materially scales and 
diversifies APSEZ’s liquids portfolio, and provides exposure to the long-term transition toward new-

Dr. Reddy’s receives marketing authorization for generic semaglutide injection 
in Brazil 
• 
ANVISA grants marketing authorization for generic semaglutide injection for the treatment of adults with 
insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus, as an adjunct to diet and exercise 
 
• 
The approval expands Dr. Reddy’s semaglutide presence to Brazil, one of the key markets in Latin 
America 
Hyderabad, India; November 5, 2026: Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories Ltd. (BSE: 500124, NSE: DRREDDY, NYSE: RDY, 
NSEIFSC: DRREDDY), along with its subsidiaries together referred to as “Dr. Reddy’s”, today announced that Brazil’s 
National Health Surveillance Agency (ANVISA) has granted marketing authorization for generic semaglutide injection 
for the treatment of adults with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus, as an adjunct to diet and exercise, either 
as monotherapy when metformin is considered inappropriate due to intolerance or contraindications, or in addition to 
other medicinal products for the treatment of diabetes. The product will be available as a pre-filled, multi-dose injectable 
pen in two presentations, 2 mg/1.5 mL and 4 mg/3 mL, for once-weekly dosing. 
Brazil has 16.6 million adults aged 20–79 living with diabetes and ranks sixth globally in terms of the number of adults 
living with diabetes.1 Reflecting the significant treatment need in the country, the semaglutide market for diabetes is 
estimated at approximately USD 244.6 million.2 
Commenting on the approval, MV Ramana, Chief Executive Officer, Global Generics, Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories, 
said, “Our focus with semaglutide is to expand access to this treatment option across markets where the patient need 
is significant. Brazil, with its substantial burden of diabetes, is an important part of that journey. This approval builds on 
our broader semaglutide strategy and brings us another step closer to making semaglutide available to more patients. 
We plan to launch semaglutide in Brazil with Aché.” 
About Dr. Reddy’s: Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories Ltd. (BSE: 500124, NSE: DRREDDY, NYSE: RDY, NSEIFSC: DRREDDY) is a global pharmaceutical 
company headquartered in Hyderabad, India. Established in 1984, we are committed to providing access to affordable and innovative medicines. 
Driven by our purpose of ‘Good Health Can’t Wait’, we offer a portfolio of products and services including APIs, generics, branded generics, biosimilars 
and OTC. Our major therapeutic areas of focus are gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, diabetology, oncology, pain management and dermatology. Our 
major markets include – USA, India, Russia & CIS countries, China, Brazil and Europe. As a company with a history of deep science that has led to 
several industry firsts, we continue to plan ahead and invest in businesses of the future. As an early adopter of sustainability and ESG actions, we 
released our first Sustainability Report in 2004. Our current ESG goals aim to set the bar high in environmental stewardship; access and affordability 
for patients; diversity; and governance. For more information, log on to: www.drreddys.com.  
 
1 Source: IDF Diabetes Atlas 2025, 11th edition. 
 
2 Source: IQVIA, MAT September 2026.

SAMIL Reports Highest Ever Quarterly and Half Yearly Revenues.   
Booked Business at all time high of USD 106 Billion. 
 
India (5th November 2026) – Samvardhana Motherson International Limited (SAMIL) today announced its financial results for the second quarter 
and half year of fiscal 2026-27, which ended on 30th September 2026. 
 
Commenting on the results, Mr. Vivek Chaand Sehgal, Chairman, Motherson, said, 
“We are pleased to report a resilient performance, which reflects the continued trust of our customers and 
the efforts of our teams across the world. We are grateful for their support to Motherson. We achieved our 
highest-ever quarterly revenues, underscoring our strong execution and continued focus on operational 
excellence. As we continue to integrate our newly acquired businesses, we are actively working on identifying 
and realising synergies across the Group. These efforts are expected to create new opportunities for growth 
and further strengthen our capabilities. With a strong booked business of USD 106 Bn and a healthy balance 
sheet, reflected in a leverage ratio at 0.8x, we remain well positioned to support our customers and pursue 
sustainable growth opportunities to create long term value for our stakeholders.” 
 
Key Highlights 
 
1) Record quarterly revenue of Rs. 38,280 Cr (+27% YoY); H1FY27 revenue of Rs. 73,524 Cr (+22% YoY). 
2) Booked business at an all-time high of USD 106 billion. 
3) Capex of Rs. 3,585 Cr in H1FY27 (56% of EBITDA). FY27 capex outlay of Rs. 6,000 Crores +/- 10%. 
4) 01 plant operationalised during the quarter; 5 expansions announced. Total 17 facilities at different stages of 
completion. 
5) Leverage ratio at 0.8x, well within the 2.5x financial policy. 
6) Acquisition of Rotary Connectors (India) announced during the quarter. 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
Samvardhana Motherson International Limited (SAMIL) 
Samvardhana Motherson International Limited (SAMIL) is a global *Design, Engineering, Manufacturing, Assembly and Logistics (D.E.M.A.L.) specialist. 
The company was listed on the BSE and NSE in India in 1993. The company is focused, dynamic, and progressive, providing customers with innovative and 
value-added products, services, and solutions. With a diverse global customer base that includes nearly all leading automobile manufacturers worldwide, 
the company supports its customers from over 475 facilities across 47 countries on six continents. The company has diversified to support customers in 
non-automotive businesses, including technology and industrial solutions, health & medical, aerospace, consumer electronics and logistics. SAMIL is 
currently the largest auto ancillary in India and is ranked among the top 10 automotive suppliers worldwide. The company was selected as one of the Best 
Companies for 2024 by TIME. For more details, please visit www.motherson.com  (CIN – L35106MH1986PLC284510). Note –All numbers in the press 
statement are on consolidated basis unless stated otherwise. For more details on the results of SAMIL, please contact.

Independent Auditor’s Review Report on the Quarterly Unaudited Consolidated Financial Results of the
Company Pursuant to the Regulation 33 and 52 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended
Review Report to
The Board of Directors
Samvardhana Motherson International Limited
1.
We have reviewed the accompanying Statement of Unaudited Consolidated Financial Results of
Samvardhana Motherson International Limited (the “Holding Company”) and its subsidiaries (the Holding
Company and its subsidiaries together referred to as “the Group”), its associates and joint ventures for the
quarter ended September 30, 2026 and year to date from April 01, 2026 to September 30, 2026 (the
“Statement”) attached herewith, being submitted by the Holding Company pursuant to the requirements of
Regulation 33 and 52 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as
amended (the “Listing Regulations”).
2.
The Holding Company’s Management is responsible for the preparation of the Statement in accordance with
the recognition and measurement principles laid down in Indian Accounting Standard 34, (Ind AS 34)
“Interim Financial Reporting” prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 as amended, read
with relevant rules issued thereunder and other accounting principles generally accepted in India and in
compliance with Regulation 33 and 52 of the Listing Regulations. The Statement has been approved by the
Holding Company’s Board of Directors. Our responsibility is to express a conclusion on the Statement based
on our review.
3.
We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagements (SRE)
2410, “Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the Entity” issued
by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. This standard requires that we plan and perform the review
to obtain moderate assurance as to whether the Statement is free of material misstatement. A review of interim
financial information consists of making inquiries, primarily of persons responsible for financial and
accounting matters, and applying analytical and other review procedures. A review is substantially less in
scope than an audit conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing and consequently does not enable
us to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant matters that might be identified in an
audit. Accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion.
We also performed procedures in accordance with the Master Circular No. CIR/CFD/CMD1/44/2019 dated
March 29, 2019 issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India under Regulation 33(8) of the Listing
Regulations, to the extent applicable.
4.
The Statement includes the results of the entities mentioned in Annexure I.
5.
Based on our review conducted and procedures performed as stated in paragraph 3 above and based on the
consideration of the review reports of other auditors referred to in paragraph 6 below, nothing has come to
our attention that causes us to believe that the accompanying Statement, prepared in accordance with
recognition and measurement principles laid down in the aforesaid Indian Accounting Standards (‘Ind AS’)
specified under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013, as amended, read with relevant rules issued
thereunder and other accounting principles generally accepted in India, has not disclosed the information
required to be disclosed in terms of the Listing Regulations, including the manner in which it is to be
disclosed, or that it contains any material misstatement.
6.
The accompanying Statement includes the unaudited interim financial results and other financial information
in respect of:
x
84 subsidiaries and one Employee Stock Option Trust, whose unaudited interim financial results
include total assets of Rs. 82,969 Crores as at September 30, 2026, total revenues of Rs. 18,128 Crores
and Rs. 36,584 Crores, total net profit after tax of Rs. 82 Crores and Rs. 975 Crores, total comprehensive
income of Rs. 88 Crores and Rs. 998 Crores for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and for the
period ended on that date respectively, and net cash outflow of Rs. 174 Crores for the period from April

1, 2026 to September 30, 2026 as considered in the Statement which have been reviewed by their
respective independent auditors.
x
5 joint ventures, whose unaudited interim financial results include Group’s share net profit after tax of
Rs. 20 Crores and Rs. 66 Crores, total comprehensive income of Rs. 20 Crores and Rs. 66 Crores, for
the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and for the period ended on that date respectively, as considered
in the Statement whose financial results, other financial information have been reviewed by their
respective independent auditors.
The independent auditor’s reports on interim financial results of these entities have been furnished to us by
the Management and our conclusion on the Statement, in so far as it relates to the amounts and disclosures in
respect of these subsidiaries and joint ventures is based solely on the report of such auditors and procedures
performed by us as stated in paragraph 3 above.
7.
The accompanying Statement includes unaudited interim financial results and other unaudited financial
information in respect of:
x
80 subsidiaries, whose interim financial results and other financial information reflect total assets of Rs.
7,946 Crores as at September 30, 2026, and total revenues of Rs. 1,129 Crores and Rs. 1,963 Crores,
total net loss after tax of Rs. 19 Crores and Rs. 29 Crores, total comprehensive expense of Rs. 45 Crores
and Rs. 55 Crores, for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and for the period ended on that date
respectively and net cash inflows of Rs. 196 Crores for the period from April 1, 2026 to September 30,
2026.
x
2 associates and 3 joint ventures, whose interim financial results includes the Group’s share of net profit
after tax of Rs. 20 Crores and Rs. 21 Crores and Group’s share of total comprehensive income of Rs. 17
Crores and Rs. 19 Crores for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and for the period ended on that date
respectively.
The unaudited interim financial results and other unaudited financial information of the these subsidiaries,
joint ventures and associates have not been reviewed by their auditors and have been approved and furnished
to us by the Management and our conclusion on the Statement, in so far as it relates to the affairs of these
subsidiaries, joint ventures and associate, is based solely on such unaudited interim financial results and other

efficient utilisation of the project site and enhances renewable power generation.

across its renewable energy operations. Around 16 women professionals, accounting for nearly

participation highlights the growing role of women in technical and leadership positions within 
India’s renewable energy sector.

renewable energy projects and reinforces its commitment to supporting India’s transition 
towards a low-carbon energy future through technology-led solutions, strong execution 
capabilities and responsible project development.

signed 2.8 GW of pumped hydro storage projects, and expanded its EV charging network to over 7,000 public charging points

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to conference call hosted by GE Vernova T&D 
India Limited for Quarter 2 of financial year 2026-'27. As a reminder, all participant lines will 
be in the listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the 
presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an 
operator by pressing star then zero on your touch-tone phone. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Ms. Megha Gupta from GE Vernova T&D India Limited. 
Thank you, and over to you. 
Megha Gupta: 
Good evening, everyone. Welcome to the earnings call of GE Vernova T&D India Limited. I'm 
Megha Gupta from Investor Relations team, and I'm joined by Mr. Sandeep Zanzaria, CEO and 
MD of the company; Mr. Sushil Kumar, Whole-Time Director and CFO of the company; Mr. 
Abhishek Srivastava, Head Business Operations; and other members of the leadership team. 
 
Before we begin, I would like to highlight that today's discussion may contain a few forward-
looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. These statements are based on 
our current expectations, and actual results may differ materially from those expressed or 
implied. 
 
Now I hand over the conference to Mr. Sandeep Zanzaria to open up the discussion. 
Sandeep Zanzaria: 
Thank you, Megha. Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining the second quarter 
earnings call. The Indian power transmission sector is at its historic inflection point moving from 
a centralized grid towards a more dynamic digitalized and decarbonized architecture. Three key 
pillars are defining the industry. 
 
First is unprecedented grid expansion and modernization. India's energy demand is scaling at a 
pace that requires aggressive expansion of transmission infrastructure. The integration of large-
scale renewable energy often far from consumption centers requires robust long-distance high-
voltage direct current and alternating current corridors. 
 
Second is the digital transformation of the grid. The grid has grown more complex, making 
advanced automation, real-time smart substations and predictive maintenance essential to reduce 
AT&C losses and improve the reliability. GE Vernova is focused on providing the software and 
digital infrastructure required to manage this complexity. 
 
Third, the T&D sector is the backbone of India's energy transition and net zero ambition. The 
greener grid requires not only solar and wind capacity, but also the hardware and intelligence to 
balance the intermittent power sources. Systems such as flexible AC transmission solutions and 
energy storage integration are therefore becoming essential for grid resilience. 
 
Coming to the financial performance, during the second quarter, we saw an order book of 
INR24.4 billion, up 52% year-on-year compared to INR16.1 billion in quarter ended September 
'25. Our Q2 revenue stood at INR20.3 billion versus INR15.4 billion in Q2 FY25-'26, up by 32% 
year-on-year. 
• 
GEVERNOVA 

 
 
 
 
GE Vernova T&D India Limited 
October 30, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 21 
 
 
Order backlog stands at INR214.4 billion as of September '26, versus INR214.6 billion as of 
March '26. The order backlog stands at more than 3 years of revenue for FY25-'26. Our profit 
before tax and exceptional items for the quarter ended September 26 was at INR5.8 billion 
compared to around INR4 billion in the corresponding quarter of the last financial year, growing 
by 1.4x. Cash generation of INR10.1 billion during H1. With this cash, our balance stands at the 
end of September at INR32.5 billion. 
 
Looking ahead, our priorities are consistent. First, execution excellence on mega projects, 
especially our HVDC; Second, deeper localization, expanding our manufacturing footprint in 
India, reducing exposure to global supply chain risk and supporting the vision of self-reliant 
energy sector. 
 
Third, growing our services and software business, particularly grid automation and asset 
performance management, where predictive maintenance and software optimization help 
utilities get more from the assets they already have. A heartful thanks to our colleagues at the 
project sites and in our factories. As the volumes grow, they continue to deliver with rigor and 
never compromise on safety. 
 
Now I turn to Abhishek to walk through the specific operational highlights for the quarter. 
Abhishek Srivastava: 
Thanks, Sandeep. Good evening to all of you. So, I will take you through the key network 
augmentations that we achieved in the last quarter. So first of the notable mentions is 400 kV 
substation for NEA in Nepal. So, this is for the backbone of 400 kV grid network that Nepal is 
trying to develop. So earlier, we had commissioned Khimti, and this is the second in the league. 
After that, 400 kV GIS station was commissioned for GETCO at Babarzar. 
 
In addition to that, we have been strengthening the transformation capacities at various existing 
and new substations. And in that, we commissioned 765 kV reactors for our customers PGCIL 
at Bidar, Resonia at Beawar and then 765 kV generator transformer for NUPPL at Ghatampur. 
 
In addition to that, we had GIS commissioning done at Narela in Delhi and some export jobs, 
one in Spain and another one in Senegal. All these commissionings are a testament of our focus 
in terms of network augmentation and our commitment towards operational excellence and 
continuously delivering on our promises to our customers. 
 
So, I hand over to Sushil now to take us forward. 
Sushil Kumar: 
Thank you, Abhishek. Good afternoon and good evening, everyone. First, I will talk about the 
order booking highlights for the quarter. During quarter 2, we secured an order intake of INR24.4 
billion, bringing our cumulative H1 order intake to approximately INR35.8 billion. This 
represents an 11% growth year-on-year. 
 
Key wins during the quarter reflect our strong technical capabilities and diverse market reach, 
including a major package for 400 kV generator transformer and 420 kV GIS for a 1,500-
megawatt pumped storage hydro project in Maharashtra, 800 kV and 420 kV GIS packages for 
transmission projects in Andhra Pradesh, supply of 400 kV reactors and 420/220 kV GIS 
package for a TBCB transmission project in the state of Himachal Pradesh. 
• 
GEVERNOVA 

 
 
 
 
GE Vernova T&D India Limited 
October 30, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 21 
 
 
Supply of 765 kV shunt reactor for a TBCB transmission project in the state of Andhra Pradesh, 
and continued export momentum with multiple equipment orders for GIS/AIS across North 
America, Europe, Middle East, Africa alongside steady grid automation packages. 
 
Our order backlog closed strong at INR214.4 billion, reflecting a healthy baseline as we 
efficiently convert our backlog into revenue.  
Turning now to the financial performance for the quarter and some highlights of the first half. 
Revenue for the quarter, stood at INR20.3 billion, up 32% year-on-year with H1 revenue 
reaching about INR38.6 billion, up 35%. 
 
Gross margin for the quarter stood at 44.5%. Disciplined cost management across operations 
enabled us to deliver an EBITDA of INR5.5 billion, approximately 27.1% of revenue. This 
EBITDA is at the higher end of our mid-20 guidance band that we had been communicating to 
the stakeholders in the past. 
 
Profit before tax for the quarter rose to INR5.8 billion and profit after tax is at INR4.3 billion, 
representing 21.3% of revenue. Finance costs remain negligible with our continued net zero debt 
position. 
 On the balance sheet side, we generated INR10.1 billion of cash during first half, taking our 
total available cash and cash equivalents, including funds lent to the cash pool to approximately 
INR32.5 billion. 
 
Regarding our capital expenditure, as previously announced, the company is progressing with 
the capacity expansion program of approximately INR10 billion, out of which roughly 20% has 
been already incurred. Management continues to evaluate various options for the utilization of 
balance cash to optimize returns to the shareholders. 
 
I would also like to highlight the contract quality and segmentation of our orders and revenue. 
For the quarter, our order and revenue mix reflects a strong balance with export orders sitting at 
21% and export revenues at 32%. Looking at our order and revenue split for the half year, orders 
stood at 29% export and revenue stood at 31% of exports. 
 
Further, our ongoing counterparty derisking strategy ensures that private customers and central 
utilities & PSUs continue to form an overwhelming majority of our order backlog, maintaining 
a robust and secure risk profile. 
 
In the presentation, we have also given the status of material related party approvals. So we had 
secured an approval of roughly INR31 billion in the AGM of 2025. This was for export of 
various high-voltage switchgear components to 2 related parties in Middle East and France. This 
lapsed in AGM of 2026 because the shareholder approval for the related party is valid for a 
period of 1 year. And the reason is that the order is on hold from the customer side due to the 
operational planning delays from their side. 
 
We had also secured another approval for a related party from a U.S. entity, largely for export 
of goods from India for approximately $151 million. This approval is valid till 15th of May 
• 
GEVERNOVA 

 
 
 
 
GE Vernova T&D India Limited 
October 30, 2026 
 
Page 5 of 21 
 
2027, and the order is in discussion stage with the customers. We hope that in H2 of this financial 
year, we should be able to conclude this order. 
 
So, summarizing before I hand back for the questions, order intake grew steadily. Revenue 
growth, execution pace, cash generation and backlog quality all remained strong and consistent 
with our full year expectation. And we are confident of converting our INR214 billion backlog 
profitably over the coming years. 
 
With that, I'll hand over for the question and answers. 
Moderator: 
Thank you very much, sir. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. First question 
is from the line of Sameer Thakur from Ambit Capital. 
Sameer Thakur: 
My first question is that GE Vernova Global, they announced acquisition of Trench. They also 
said that they are evaluating expanding the manufacturing of Trench products in India. So is 
there any view on that, whether that will be part of GE Vernova India? Or is it too early to say? 
Just wanted your comments on that. That's the first question. 
Sandeep Zanzaria: 
Thank you, Sameer. The acquisition has been announced only 2 days back. The whole 
acquisition process is expected to end in the later part of FY27. So, it's too early to comment on 
that. 
Sameer Thakur: 
Okay. And the second question is what is the revenue contribution from services and software 
at the moment? And is there any target which you have in mind or any ambitions regarding this? 
Sushil Kumar: 
Good evening, Sameer. So, software and services business, we don't give a breakup as such 
because we operate as one segment, which is the high-voltage products on transmission side. 
 
But I can give an overall color that we off late have been booking lot of equipment orders because 
our order booking, including the HVDC order has been very strong in the last few years. So as 
a ratio of the total revenue, the share of software and services may have dropped, while every 
business is growing year-over-year. 
Moderator: 
Next question is from the line of Mohit Kumar from ICICI Securities. 
Mohit Kumar: 
Congratulations on a super quarter. My first question is on the GE Vernova Global is talking 
about $900 million order, which they have booked for, for giving the orders to global factories. 
My question is, are we in contention for those? And how many factories globally GE has for 
producing transformers, especially in Asia? 
Sandeep Zanzaria: 
Mohit, In Asia, we have two transformer factories. One is in Indonesia, but that's a much smaller 
factory because, they build up till 245 kV only. And the higher rating transformers are all built 
in Vadodara. In the $900 billion orders, yes, there will be some orders which are going to flow 
for which we have taken a related party approval for INR1,300 crores and the finalization 
process is on. 
Mohit Kumar: 
My second question is, I think you mentioned in the PPT that is hold up on the 2 related party 
approval orders. One is, I think, GE Middle East and one is, I think, France, right? In your 
• 
GEVERNOVA 

 
 
 
 
GE Vernova T&D India Limited 
October 30, 2026 
 
Page 6 of 21 
 
opinion, do you think in the next 6 to 12 months that hold up will get clear and there is an 
opportunity to participate in those orders? 
Sandeep Zanzaria: 
That project actually is of a much bigger size and the hold has been put by the customer. So, we 
are not very sure whether the hold is going to get lifted in 6 months, 8 months or a year. So, it 
will be too early to speculate on that. 
Mohit Kumar: 
Understood. My last question is, how are you seeing the new opportunities for HVDC 
developing over the next 12 months? And is there a need to invest still more from our side to 
improve the indigenization content for HVDC as we go forward, yes. 
Sandeep Zanzaria: 
We have a very strong pipeline of HVDC going forward. We expect minimum 2 to 3 projects to 
come next year. And HVDC is going to remain our key focus area as well. If you look at HVDC 
practically, most of the things have been localized. So today, we are manufacturing transformers 
in India, valves in India, controls in India. 
 
So, at one point of time, a large part of the transformers and 100% of valves and controls are 
coming from outside. But with whatever capex we have done or whatever capex is under 
progress, all these things have been localized. 
 
However, there are components still which come from outside, not manufactured by GE 
Vernova, but manufactured by our subcontractors or sub-vendors. So as a long-term strategy, 
we will be working in the next phase, on localization of that as well. 
Moderator: 
Next question is from the line of Parikshit Kandpal from HDFC Securities. 
Parikshit Kandpal: 
Congratulations on a great quarter. So, in this quarter, we have seen a very significant pickup in 
the domestic orders. So last quarter was subdued. So how do you see rest of the financial year 
in terms of domestic market? And was there any one-off in this quarter, any large orders in the 
domestic markets, which would have contributed significantly to the overall order inflows? 
Sandeep Zanzaria: 
We see order intake for the year as a positive story only. There was no one-offs. It was all regular 
orders which have come in. Also, we have already declared that we are the lowest bidder in 
power grid for Barmer, and Barmer has already been acquired by Power Grid. So we expect that 
this quarter will also be significant in terms of booking that order as well. On the order side, we 
are pretty confident that this year is going to be a much stronger year than what we delivered 
last year. 
Parikshit Kandpal: 
Any color on the domestic ordering, sir, how is it panning out for the second half  
Sandeep Zanzaria: 
It is strong because in last 3 to 4 months, there was a substantial strong pipeline of TBCB projects 
and still the opportunities are coming in. So, I look at least in the next 4, 5 months, the pipeline 
to remain strong. 
Parikshit Kandpal: 
On the RPT side now, so we have seen a fallback of 2 orders. I mean they've got an indefinite 
suspension as of now and may take time to come back. So, in terms of RPT opportunities, so 
how does one look at it from here on, given even the U.S. data center order has been, kind of, 
• 
GEVERNOVA 

 
 
 
 
GE Vernova T&D India Limited 
October 30, 2026 
 
Page 7 of 21 
 
slightly delayed and may come up, as we said, later part of the year. But as an overall pipeline 
from Asia, Europe, Americas, so how does one look at RPT from here on? Are there significant 
orders which can replace the lost opportunity which we had faced from these 2 orders? 
Sandeep Zanzaria: 
For larger opportunities, definitely, yes, they are like really one-off, but we are seeing a strong 
pipeline for the smaller orders, which don't fall under the category of material RPTs, but then 
the order inflow for the normal product business is much stronger this year as compared to last 
year. 
Sushil Kumar: 
I'll just add on, Parikshit. This year, in the first half, we have booked INR10.4 billion of export 
orders and most of, like, a significant part of these orders booking are from related parties, 
compared to INR11.8 billion in the entire financial year '25-'26. So, on a like-to-like basis, you 
can see that there is a significant growth in the normal order flow, excluding the large one. And 
if we are able to close the material RPT, the U.S. one in the second half, then the entire year 
from the export perspective will be also very significant growth. 
Parikshit Kandpal: 
So, what is driving the smaller inflows, sir, from the related parties? I mean, is it broad-based? 
Or is it from some specific geographies? How would be the geographies? 
Sandeep Zanzaria: 
It's all broad-based, Parikshit. 
Parikshit Kandpal: 
Is it the effort of the certification, which we have done for our factories in new countries and 
that's yielding this, kind of, performance? So, what is driving the sudden change, I mean, from 
the small orders. 
Sandeep Zanzaria: 
Everything, many geographies are now seeing a lot of investment coming in and supply chain 
also getting stretched. So that's creating an additional opportunity. And definitely, in many cases, 
it is the certification, which we are working for last 1 year, are also yielding results. 
Parikshit Kandpal: 
Sir, the last question, sir, on the competitive intensity. We are now seeing Chinese players 
coming in, some of the other domestic players are tying up with some foreign partners and 
planning to enter into HVDC and below 400kv, we are seeing huge competition now. So how 
do you see the competitive intensity panning out from here? Are you seeing the pricing now 
cracking down? So, any color on that will be helpful for the future orders. 
Sandeep Zanzaria: 
So, after we have won Barmer, there has been no HVDC tender, so we don't know that. So 
whatever strategy you are talking about, Chinese tying up, that is not yet seen in the market. 
There has been no tender subsequently. So we cannot talk about competitive intensity as of now. 
Parikshit Kandpal: 
But regular transformers, sir, I mean, your regular stuff with high-voltage transformers beyond 
HVDC, excluding HVDC. So how is the competitive intensity? 
Sandeep Zanzaria: 
There's some slight pressure on the prices, yes, but very little, not significant. 
Moderator: 
Next question is from the line of Umesh Raut from Nomura. 
Umesh Raut: 
Congrats on a very good set of numbers again. My first question is again pertaining to acquisition 
done by parent for Trench Group. So just wanted to have your view on two comments which are 
• 
GEVERNOVA 

 
 
 
 
GE Vernova T&D India Limited 
October 30, 2026 
 
Page 8 of 21 
 
made by parent. One is basically expanding Trench Group's reach in select regions, including

“Lodha Developers Limited  
Q2 FY 2027 Post Results Conference Call” 
November 2, 2026 
 
 
 
       
 
 
 
   
 
 
 
Management: 
Mr. Abhishek Lodha: Managing Director  
 
 
Mr. Sushil Kumar Modi: Whole-time Director, Group Finance Director 
 
 
 
Mr. Sanjay Chauhan: Chief Financial Officer    
                                      
                                       Mr. Rajendra Joshi – Regional Chief Executive Officer, Bangalore 
 
 
Mr. Anand Kumar: Head of Investor Relations  
 
Mr. Chintan Parikh:  Co-Head of Investor Relations  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
2 
 
Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Lodha Developers Limited Q2 FY27 
Analyst Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and 
there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should 
you need assistance during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then 
zero on your touchtone phone. Please note that this conference has been recorded. I now hand 
the conference over to Mr. Chintan Parikh from Lodha Developers Limited. Thank you, and over 
to you, sir. 
Chintan Parikh: 
Thank you, Swapnali. Welcome to Lodha Developers Q2 FY27 Conference Call. Today, we have 
with us Mr. Abhishek Lodha, Managing Director; Mr. Sushil Kumar Modi, Group Finance 
Director; Mr. Sanjay Chauhan, Chief Financial Officer; Mr. Rajendra Joshi, CEO of Bangalore. I 
would now like to invite Abhishek to make his opening remarks. Over to you, Abhishek. 
Abhishek Lodha: 
Thank you, Chintan. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Wishing all of you 
and your families a very Happy Diwali and a prosperous new year. The first half of fiscal '27 has 
been the strongest in Lodha's history. We've delivered profit after tax of INR 2,386 crores, 
which is up 63%. 
 
Our revenue at INR 9,460 crores is up 30%. Our pre-sales of INR 96 billion are up by 7%; all 3 
being the highest ever in our history. We have achieved this while moderately reducing our net 
debt, which now stands at about INR 52 billion, about 0.2x equity. As we had told you at the 
start of the year, our H1 pre-sales would be about 40% to 42% in the first half and the balance 
in the second half.  
This came in at about 40.3%. The numbers for the second half of the year are likely to be coming 
with a mix of about INR 6000 crores to INR 7,000 crores of development company pre-sales in 
both Q3 as well as Q4 and 1 data center land transaction of about INR 1,500 crores in the fourth 
quarter for the full year number at about INR 24,000 crores of pre-sales. 
 
Having said that, we expect to easily beat our profit guidance of 20% growth which would have 
taken us to just over INR 4,000 crores. And in the first half, having already touched INR 2,400 
crores, we feel very confident of being able to beat this guidance quite comfortably. Over the 
medium term, we believe that the underlying profitability of the business is getting better. 
And therefore, will support an improvement in our return on equity further and will also aid 
our DevCo to become net debt-free over the next 2 to 3 years, which is in line with our previous 
guidance. In terms of where we stand now, at the start of the second half, we've had a strong 
start to the third quarter. October, the festive season has been strong. 
 
 
 

 
 
 
3 
 
 
We expect that the momentum in the market will continue through this year, and this is in 
spite of the fact that the adverse effects, if any, of the rising interest rates have already started. 
Having said that, we believe that the segments that we serve are not really affected by the 
change in interest rates, and hence, we feel that there will be no adverse effect of any 
moderate further increase in interest rates from this point onwards. 
 
I would like to highlight in terms of our Q2 performance that our new launch in Bangalore 
delivered significant success and therefore, Bangalore's pre-sales for the second quarter was 
over INR 1,800 crores. This tells you about the significance of the fact that we've delivered INR 
96 billion of sales in the first half with only INR 4,000 crores of GDV of new launches.  
In the second half of the year, we have a further almost just under INR 20,000 crores of new 
launches planned. And while 1 or 2 launches may move by a month or 2, overall, the program 
is a very solid and dispersed across different geographies, which will enable us to deliver on 
our guidance for the year. 
 
I would also like to update you that we just entered and have started the pre-sales for our first 
project in Gurugram NCR and the start has been quite constructive; We believe that this will 
be the start of the for city, which will over time contribute to our growth and our profitability.  
In terms of other updates, the Mulund-Airoli-Palava Freeway is now clinically complete. And 
we think that it will open in the next few weeks. And with that, Airoli will be just 20 minutes 
from Palava and Mulund will be only a 25-minute travel from Palava. Both of these will make a 
big difference to allow our attractiveness. 
 
We expect that calendar year 2027 will lead to a significant uptick in pre-sales at Palava on 
account of this infrastructure improvement. Obviously, the opening of the bullet train, which 
is scheduled for 2029, will be a significant step further in the direction of Palava moving from 
a secondary suburb to becoming a primary suburb. 
 
In terms of our collections and cash flows. The first half collections were at about INR 76 billion, 
up 19% year-on-year, and the operating cash flow was about INR 27 billion. Q2 collections were 
about INR 35 billion following the usual pattern, whereas the Q1 collections obviously had the 
land transaction as a part of it and hence, were higher. 
 
In the second half, we expect that our operating cash flow as it was in last fiscal, will significantly 
crank up, and we expect full year that our operating cash flow will be put around INR 85 billion 
or thereabouts. In terms of our data center platform, we are seeing good progress both in the 
land demand as well as in the BTS boxes.  
 
 

 
 
 
4 
 
We expect to have the definitive documents executed for the first BTS box of in this fiscal year 
and to start construction for the boxes also in this fiscal year with a view to delivering those 
boxes to the end tenant in fiscal '29, and therefore, starting the rental earnings from our data 
center BTS program in fiscal '29 itself. 
 
In addition to this, we expect the land sales to be an ongoing and continuous and predictable 
pattern with 1 transaction happening every 6 months or thereabout. And this will lead to a 
significant not only cash flow but also positive impact on profitability.  
Speaking of profitability, I would like to point out that the numbers that you see for Q2 are 
really the underlying profitability of our solid development business because there were no 
land sales in this quarter. Both the embedded EBITDA as well as the PAT are a real reflection 
of the strength of profitability of the business, driven by the strength of our brand.  
In terms of the industry, there are a few questions which often come up, and I would like to 
share our views about these. The first 1 is the war in the Middle East and how it is affecting 
housing demand. In our opinion, the direct demand effect is limited to the NRI demand from 
the Gulf which is about 4% to 5% of the sales. The broader effects due to the effective 
management of the fuel availability as well as prices by the government have been largely 
absorbed and that is reflected in India's June quarter GDP growth at about 7.8% and 
industrial production growing by over 6.7% in September. 
 
We are hopeful that as and when the Middle East situation stabilizes, there will be a positive 
momentum to Indian growth with oil prices coming down and as a consequence, is being 
supportive of both the Indian rupee as well as domestic growth.  
                                                    In terms of the 25 basis points increase in the repo rate by the RBI in October. We would like to 
point out that about 50% of our sales by value come in the segment between INR 1 crores to 
INR 5 crores value of the unit and the balance comes from the segment above INR 5 crores. 
Impact of mortgages on the segment above INR 5 crores is negligible. And hence, we do not 
expect any impact of interest rate increases in that segment. 
 
In the segment between INR 1 crores to INR 5 crores, we see an average LTV of high 40s, low 
50s. And while there will be some moderate impact of the increase in interest rates on this 
segment, we see no change in our outlook which is really driven by the significant gap in high-
quality supply in the marketplace.  
The related point I would like to speak about is that is there an oversupply building up? And 
whether there is a likelihood of that impacting the market going forward? We've been speaking 
about the redevelopment phenomena in Mumbai for 3 years now. And as you can notice, us 
as well as other large developers continue to scale up their pre-sales.  
 

 
 
 
5 
 
This really is a reflection of the fact that the market is getting increasingly tuned towards large 
organized and branded developers. And the supply from these Grade A+ and Grade A 
developers is seen and dealt with by the market in a very different manner from the rest of the 
supply. 
 
India, in the first 9 months of 2026 has seen about 60 million square feet of office absorption 
with about 40% of it by the global capability centers. We also see that AI is reorganizing 
workflows, but we also see that it is not all negative for India and on the contrary, as we saw 
in the example of PwC where PwC U.S. and PwC India have come together to set up a large-
scale consulting venture to serve U.S. clients in India. 
We believe that AI given the high level of technology and the high level of need for execution, 
implementation support will be a positive for Indian jobs and therefore, as by extension in 
housing. Our performance in Bangalore in the last quarter is an indication of our belief that for 
the strong brands, the demand continues to remain robust, and there is a significant supply-
demand gap. 
 
I would also like to highlight that Newsweek has again named Lodha amongst the World’s 1,000 
most trustworthy companies, the only Indian real estate company on the list for the second 
year running. We believe that this is a recognition of the way that our business is conducted 
and about how society at large as well as our direct sale stakeholders like employees and 
customers are perceiving our company.  
Through the Lodha Foundation, the Lodha Mathematical Sciences Institute hosted 55 
researchers this quarter with more than 90 from 15 countries expected in the coming 
semester. The team comprising of 6 Students from Lodha Genius Program placed second at the 
Eking 2026 in Switzerland.  
And we continue to support the communities that we work in by direct cash transfers as well 
as health insurance for a large number of families. With this, I would like to hand over and call 
in Mr. Rajendra Joshi, the CEO of our Bangalore business to speak about the Q2 launch that we 
had and what we're seeing on the ground in Bangalore. 
Rajendra Joshi: 
Thank you, sir. Good afternoon to everyone. I will speak in brief about the Bangalore market 
and our journey in Bangalore. The Bangalore residential real estate market is now over      INR 
1 lakh crores as of FY '26, nearly tripling in size over the last 4-to-5-year period, driven by both 
volume and price.  
The market has continued to premiumize with homes priced over INR 2 crores, increasing their 
contribution from 40% in FY '24 to 50% in FY '26 over the last 2 years, while the aggregate 
volume in square feet terms have largely remained steady, premium housing has continued to 
grow. 

 
 
 
6 
 
 
Pricing growth has been healthy at about 10% in most locations during this period with some 
pockets witnessing stronger price growth on account of improving connectivity and new job 
hub creation. Supply continues to be on the healthy side with an average inventory position of 
about 18 months in the last 2 years.  
The market continues to remain robust in FY '27 with the first half of this year, recording an 
absorption of about INR 52,500 crores, up 10% over the same period of last year. Pricing 
momentum continues to be steady as well with an average increase of about 6% compared to 
first half of FY '26. 
 
The INR 2 crores and above segment in which we operate continues to perform strongly, as 
we've mentioned, contributes about 50% of the overall market demand. Demand continues to 
be strong across the key growth corridors of North, East and Southeast Bangalore, supported 
by cities growing base of white-collar professionals across GCC technology companies. 
And the start-up ecosystem with majority of these buyers belonging to mid - to senior 
managers in these organizations. Office absorption being a lead indicator of residential demand 
remains at record levels. Bangalore recorded nearly 17 million square feet of net office 
absorption in calendar year '25, the highest ever for the city.  
This is followed by 8.3 million square feet in first half of this calendar year. GCC is continuing 
to be an important driver of this demand and Bangalore remains a major GCC hub. Global giants 
such as Google, Microsoft, JPMorgan continue to have significant GCC presence in Bangalore, 
and many of these centers have moved beyond just being back-office work locations to 
strategic hub for digital engineering and core product development.  
This, I think, is something that is really driving the recent demand in the Bangalore City. The 
city's Cyber ecosystem is another source of demand, spanning late-stage and well-funded 
early-stage companies. Consumer tech in particular, has boomed over the last 3 to 4 years with 
names such as Swiggy, Razorpay, Meesho, Zepto contributing to a growing uniform base and 
the wave of IPOs.  
Looking ahead, strong job creation, sustained investor confidence in the start-up ecosystem 
and ongoing infrastructure development, such as the upcoming North Bangalore Metro line 
and the Satellite Town Ring Road are expected to be key catalysts for the continued residential 
growth. 
Coming to our journey in Bangalore. We entered Bangalore with the launch of Lodha Mirabelle 
next to Manyata's Business Park in North Bangalore in November. Our first couple of years 
were focused on establishing Lodha as a premium brand in the city, building a strong local 
organization and demonstrating our ability to deliver a differentiated product and a customer 
experience. Having successfully completed this initial phase, we are now firmly in the growth 
phase of our Bangalore journey. 

 
 
 
7 
 
 
From two projects in FY '25 and about INR 700 crores in pre-sales. We have now grown through 
4 operating projects in FY '26, and we achieved about INR 2,300 crores in sales. In this year, in 
the second quarter, as Lodha mentioned, we have launched a project and are ready to launch 
another project in the second half of this year.  
With this, we would have six operating projects by the end of FY27 and we are likely to cross 
about INR 3,000 crores in pre-sales from Bangalore in this financial year. Over this period, we've 
also established presence across key group corridor for Bangalore and as we have scaled our 
strategic focus; has remained consistent; build, premium and luxury developments in locations 
where we believe the depth of end user demand; and to differentiate ourselves through the 
quality of our product and customer experience.  
I would like to talk a little about the launch of Lodha Beaumont Estate, as Mr. Lodha mentioned, 
the significant milestones in this year for us. This is a 70-acre development in North Bangalore. 
We have reported sales of about INR 1,500 crores plus in the first 3 months since launch. 
Response to Beaumont estate has been particularly encouraging for us for a few reasons.  
First, the product differentiation. We introduced large-format premium homes in a micro 
market where much of the existing supply was at a relatively smaller typologies and lower 
ticket sizes. Beaumont estate were priced above INR 3 crores with a few units going up to as 
high as INR 13 crores to INR 14 crores compared to the fact that most of the competition supply 
was at around INR 2 crores. Importantly, larger premium homes have much greater demand 
by our customers.  
Second, the premium lifestyle proposition. The project has been designed as a premium garden 
estate with a strong emphasis on open spaces, landscaping and high-quality amenities, 
including a large signature club house. We believe this differentiates proposition has related 
strongly with customers in the macro market. 
 
Third, an expensive customer experience. As we have done in our previous projects in 
Bangalore, we place significant emphasis on the quality of customer journey at Beaumont 
estate. It included a pointed customer engagement, consultative sales and high hospitality 
standards including curated F&B experiences. We believe the customer experience during the 
purchase journey gives buyers an early indication of the service standards and leading 
experience we aim to provide after possession as well.  
Fourthly and most importantly, the success also allays some concerns over AI-led job 
disruptions in Bangalore. The disruption, we believe, is more a phenomenon at the entry-level 
jobs, which pays around INR 500,000 to INR 600,000 per annum salaries, a segment which is 
not our customers. Most of our target segments in this project are those who have household 
income of above INR 50 lakhs and are probably net gainers of the AI net productivity gains and 
are actually very, very confident cohort.  

 
 
 
8 
 
The success of Beaumont estate gives us further confidence in the premium positioning that 
we've been building in Bangalore over the last few years. More importantly, the depth of 
demand across ticket sizes, including at the upper end of the project, reinforces I believe that 
there is a meaningful and growing customer base for differentiated premium and luxury 
housing in the city of Bangalore. 
 
Looking over the past few years, we have re-established Lodha as an aspirational premium 
development in Bangalore and Beaumont estate launch reflects this. As we scale, we will keep 
our focus on premium luxury projects and on delivering exemplary customer experience and 
product across all our projects. 
 
We continue to actively evaluate land parcels, which align with these criteria, build a healthy 
project pipeline. The high growth North-east and South-east Bangalore corridors remain a 
priority, and we continue to explore opportunities closer to the city as well. Over the longer 
period, we want to become a meaningful player in the city and see ourselves having a mid-teen 
market share. 
 
From a people's point, we have scaled significantly from starting up in 2023 to about 350 plus 
employees across all functions. We expect this number to grow significantly over the next year, 
especially in operations, in line with our growth ambitions. As always, we will continue to 
leverage support from our head office, which has a strong employee base who support us in 
every functions, while depending on a strong core team in Bangalore to lead and deliver. Thank 
you. 
Abhishek Lodha: 
We can open the floor for Q&A. 
Moderator: 
Sure, sir. Thank you very much. We will now begin with the question-and-answer session. We 
will take the first question from the line of Karan Khanna from Ambit Capital. 
Karan Khanna: 
Congrats on the strong operating profit growth for the quarter and also the Bangalore success. 
My first question to you, Abhishek, and while you did briefly talk about this during your opening 
remarks. We've had two quarters since the start of the West Asia war. Based on the trends that 
you're seeing, which segment has been impacted the most in terms of footfalls because of the 
crisis?  
And as a follow-up for your portfolio, South and Central Mumbai accounted for about INR 8,000 
crores of sales in FY '26. So how is the luxury segment trending overall since the start of the 
war and of the 5.6 million sq. ft slated for launch in MMR, what's the share of South and Central 
in the launch pipeline? 
 
 

 
 
 
9 
 
Abhishek Lodha: 
Karan, thank you for your questions. In terms of the impact on the footfall from the Gulf war, 
as I mentioned in my opening remarks, the only impact we've seen so far in terms of sales is 
from the NRI sales in the Middle East, which make up about 4% to 5% of our sales. And these 
tend to be more focused entry level, which are homes between INR 1 crores to INR 3 crores.  
So that's where sort of the impact has been seen. We haven't seen any other meaningful 
change in terms of our footfalls on account of the Middle East situation. In terms of the strength 
of the market in a Central Mumbai or what you refer to as a luxury buyer, we continue to see 
strong demand. We see that the consumer for that segment is constructive.  
They're making their sales decisions. And they are clearly differentiating between the options 
that they have on the basis of the credibility of the brand and the location. So, we find that all 
these factors are supportive of our continued scale up in this segment. In terms of the launch 
pipeline, we have about INR 100 billion GDV in the MMR of which about South-Central Mumbai 
launches will be approximately INR 40 billion. 
Karan Khanna: 
Sure. This is helpful, Abhishek. Secondly, can you talk a bit about the office opportunity in NCR, 
while it is too early, how is the initial response for your commercial project that was launched 
on Golf Course Road? And is this part of the strategy for NCR where you build brand visibility 
with commercial followed by our Q4 launch at Sohna Road? As a follow-up, when you're 
looking at future opportunities, are you evaluating both commercial as well as residential or 
will the focus largely remain on adding more residential projects in this region? 
Abhishek Lodha: 
Development business focuses on for sale product across office as well as residential with 
residential obviously being by far the dominant component of that strategy. In terms of the 
launch that we've recently started this festive season in NCR. The response so far has been 
quite encouraging. Obviously, these are early days. So, we will have a more detailed update for 
you in the next quarter's analyst call. 
 
In terms of our strategy, whether again, residential or office in the NCR. NCR, as you know, we 
are in pilot phase. We will do a very modest number of projects in the early days. And we have 
currently this launch project, 1 more, which we have visibility of, and we'll perhaps add a third 
site soon and then take it from there. So, as it stands right now, this is the first of our office 
projects, and we expect to have 2 more residential projects in our pilot phase and then 
evaluate. 
Karan Khanna: 
Sure. And then last question, if I look at Slides 14 and 15, the launch guidance for FY '27 in July 
was about INR 25,000 crores, but now that stands reduced to INR 23,100 crores and yet you 
maintained the pre-sales guidance of INR 24,000 crores. So, is it safe to assume that sustaining 
sales should continue remaining stronger?  
 

 
 
 
10 
 
And as a follow-up, while sustaining sales have been very strong this quarter as well as in first 
half. How should one think about the sustenance sales from completed unsold inventory? If I 
look at Slide 17 of the presentation and the number 3.9 million square feet on completed 
unsold inventory, that remains unchanged this quarter versus last quarter. So, are you seeing 
a trend where completed inventory is still taking longer to sell versus launched, but have we 
completed the inventory? 
Abhishek Lodha: 
Karan, I think that question on completed inventory, almost no completed inventory actually 
stays. Completed inventory is the fastest moving when you imagine that we have deliveries of 
10 million, 11 million, 12 million square feet depending on the year. We will obviously have 
each quarter a significant amount completing and that gets added.  
It's just a coincidence that last quarter and this quarter, the math has just added up to 3.9 
million. It's not the same 3.9 million feet, which is remaining unsold. And in terms of the launch 
pipeline. See launches move around, there'll always be a month here or on there. It doesn't 
change our outlook.  
You've seen that even in previous years, we never really on a full year basis, been explaining 
the fact that just because the launch moved from 1 year to the start of the next year, that 
should not affect the expectation from us in terms of our delivery on our KPIs. So yes, while 1 
project seems to have moved from Q4 into Q1 of the next fiscal, that doesn't change our 
outlook in terms of our pre-sale’s performance. And it also tells you that overall, the underlying 
momentum is good, which is what really sustainable sales is all about. 
Karan Khanna: 
That is helpful Abhishek. Greetings to you and to the entire team for the festive season. 
Abhishek Lodha: 
Thank you. To you, too.  
Moderator: 
Thank you. Will take the next question from the line of Abhinav Sinha from Jefferies. 
Abhinav Sinha: 
A couple of questions. So firstly, on the data center a bit where you've seen the availability now 
being increased to 5 gigawatts from 3. So, can you talk a bit about what is driving this higher 
visibility? And also, how do you see that transmission and distribution aspect of this panning 
out in the next couple of years? 
Abhishek Lodha: 
Abhinav, in terms of the power, the update is really reflective of the approvals that we've 
received from the concerned authorities. So, we've updated it in line with those approvals. This 
5 gigawatts is an outcome of the available transmission ecosystem in and around the site, and 
it doesn't require a significant upgradation of the existing transmission network. 
 
We obviously are carrying out the tapping of that network by building the substations at our 
own cost, for which work is underway, but that is being done by us at our cost. So, we see that 
with this scale of availability, the fact that we have 3 marquee tenants already building on the 
site, AWS, STT and digital edge.  

 
 
 
11 
 
With these tenants what they are building, a lot of it is getting taken up quite quickly by the 
world's largest companies. And as a whole, there is a good bounce when it comes, like I said, 
to our own progress as well as additional land requirements from existing as well as new 
companies to start within the campus. It's important to note that with this campus of about 5 
gigawatts of input power, which will translate into a little over 4 gigawatts of IT output. 
 
The level of investment that India will get will be in the range of $150 billion or more. And this 
will become 1 of the largest, if not the very largest locations for FDI in the country. So, what 
we're building is not just about 1 more project, but we are building a nationally strategic piece 
of infrastructure, which we think will be critical for India's long-term ambitions and we are 
receiving strong support from the government because they recognize how important this is 
for India's future strength. 
Abhinav Sinha: 
Second question is on pre-sales for the first half of the year. Can you detail a bit on the trends 
that you have seen in Mumbai, which segments or geographies are doing better? 
Abhishek Lodha: 
We Abhinav saw that we ended up with good sales across the different price points. So, there 
isn't anything specifically to report in terms of 1 geography, Mumbai performing stronger or 
weaker than the other? The monsoon quarter typically is quite soft. So, we were very pleased 
with the overall sales for this quarter. Especially, since there was no land contribution to it.  
                                                     The mid-income segment contribution went up modestly in this quarter compared to the last 
quarter. But there's nothing really in terms of a larger trend that we are seeing. Sales across 
the different price points continue to remain quite positive. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. We will take the next question from the line of Biplab Debbarma from Emkay 
Global. 
Biplab Debbarma: 
Sir, I missed the part on data center… 
Moderator: 
Sorry to interrupt in between, Biplab, could you please with your handset mode as you are not 
audible?
