Further to our letter dated 26th October 2026, we write to inform that at the meeting held today (5th November
2026), the Board of Directors of the Company has approved the following:
1. Unaudited Standalone and Consolidated Financial Results of the Company for the quarter and half
year ended 30th September 2026:
The Unaudited Standalone and Consolidated Financial Results of the Company for the quarter and half year
ended 30th September 2026, in the format specified under the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 ('SEBI Listing Regulations"), together with a copy of the Limited Review
Reports of M/s. Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP, Statutory Auditors of the Company are
enclosed for your records. The aforesaid Unaudited Financial Results are also being uploaded on the
Company's website at https://tiindia.com. An extract of the aforesaid Unaudited Financial Results, in the
manner prescribed under the SEBI Listing Regulations, along with a Quick Response (QR) code will be
published in English and Tamil newspapers within the time stipulated.
A copy of the press release made with regard to the said unaudited financial results for the quarter and half
year ended 30th September 2026 is enclosed.
2. Capacity Enhancement in Engineering division:
The Board has approved a capital expenditure proposal not exceeding Rs. 83 Cr. towards the capacity
enhancement in the existing manufacturing facility of Cold Rolled Steel Strips (CRSS) at Avadi to meet
increase in demand. The project will be primarily funded through internal accrual and is expected to be
completed in FY 2027-28. Since actual enhancement in the capacity depends on different product mix, the
exact enhancement in manufacturing capacity cannot be determined at this stage.

returns, supported by reputed promoters with rich experience and backed by

ABOUT UNO MINDA
Uno Minda Limited is one of the leading manufacturers and suppliers of auto 
components and systems with leadership across key product segments. 
The company has a well diversified product portfolio with marquee clientele, 
both globally and domestically
Diversified across product divisions (Acoustics, Switches, Castings, 
Lighting and others), segments (4Ws & 2Ws) and geographies 
(International & Domestic) and channels (replacement & OEM)
Product portfolio is well insulated from any foreseeable market 
disruptions, with an ICE-EV agnostic product portfolio and constantly 
increasing kit value, leading to higher wallet share with OEMs
The company has been steadily growing its global presence through 
sustained capacity additions and channel expansions
Strong R&D focus and infrastructure helps in in-house product development 
and localization of products 
Track record of robust financial performance and delivering strong shareholder 
returns, supported by reputed promoters with rich experience and backed by 
professional management team

Pursuant to Regulation 30, 33, 51 and 52 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosures Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015 (the "SEBI Listing Regulations"), as applicable, we wish to inform that the Board of Directors 
("Board") of the Company, at its meeting held today i.e. Thursday, November OS, 2026, has, inter-alia, 
considered and approved the following matters: 
1) Un-audited Financial Results (Standalone & Consolidated) for the Quarter and Half Year ended on 
September 30, 2026 
We are enclosing herewith the following as Annexure I: -
a) 
Un-audited Standalone Financial Results for the quarter and half year ended on September 30, 2026 
along with the Limited Review Report thereon; 
b) 
Un-audited Consolidated Financial Results for the quarter and half year ended on September 30, 
2026 along with the Limited Review Report thereon; 
2) Detailed Project Report ("DPR"l of Sunroof Division of the Company 
The Board has approved an additional capital investment of approximately Rs. 85.00 Cr. towards expanding 
its Sunroof manufacturing capacity at Bawal, Haryana. The proposed expansion is aimed at catering to 
incremental customer orders secured by the Company and the growing demand for advanced sunroof 
systems in the Indian passenger vehicle market. The additional capacity is expected to be commissioned by 
Q2 FY28. 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 of SEBI Listing Regulations, read with Circular No. SEBI/HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-
POD2/l/3762/2026 dated January 30, 2026, the requisite details against this matter(s) is enclosed as 
Annexure- II to this letter. 
3) Changes in Senior Managerial Personnel ("SMP"l 
• 
Mr. Nitesh Minda will transition into a new role as Chief Executive officer-SCS Domain of the Company 
As part of the planned leadership succession of the SCS Domain of the company and in view of upcoming 
retirement of Mr. A.G. Giridharan, CEO-SCS Domain (SMP) of the Company, the Board of Directors of the 
Company, on the recommendation of Nomination and Remuneration Committee, has appointed Mr. Nitesh 
Minda as Chief Executive officer (Designate)-SCS Domain of the Company effective from November 05, 2026. 
Further, Mr. Minda will take over as CEO - SCS Domain upon retirement of Mr. Giridharan.

handover and continuity of domain leadership. 
•
Elevation of Mr. Kartikeya Joshi to the role of Chief Marketing Officer (CMO) of the Company
The Board has approved the elevation of Mr. Kartikeya Joshi for taking over charge as Chief Marketing Officer 
effective from November 05, 2026. In this role, Mr. Kartikeya Joshi will lead the Group's marketing function. 
•
Additional charge to Mr. Amit Jain. re-designated as Group Chief Growth and Technology Officer
(CGTO)
The Board has approved the transition of Mr. Amit Jain, from currently serving as Group CTO and CEO - 4W 
Powertrain, into the newly created role of Group Chief Growth and Technology Officer (CGTO). 
In this expanded role, he will continue to lead the Group's Technology, R&D strategy, 4W EV business and 
will additionally oversee the Corporate Manufacturing Excellence, Digital and Strategy functions.

Sub: - Outcome of the Board Meeting held on Thursday, November 05, 2026 
Dear Sir(s)/ Madam, 
[MINDA] 
--c;;:,.IVING THE Nl!W--
Pursuant to Regulation 30, 33, 51 and 52 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosures Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015 (the "SEBI Listing Regulations"), as applicable, we wish to inform that the Board of Directors 
("Board") of the Company, at its meeting held today i.e. Thursday, November OS, 2026, has, inter-alia, 
considered and approved the following matters: 
1) Un-audited Financial Results (Standalone & Consolidated) for the Quarter and Half Year ended on 
September 30, 2026 
We are enclosing herewith the following as Annexure I: -
a) 
Un-audited Standalone Financial Results for the quarter and half year ended on September 30, 2026 
along with the Limited Review Report thereon; 
b) 
Un-audited Consolidated Financial Results for the quarter and half year ended on September 30, 
2026 along with the Limited Review Report thereon; 
2) Detailed Project Report ("DPR"l of Sunroof Division of the Company 
The Board has approved an additional capital investment of approximately Rs. 85.00 Cr. towards expanding 
its Sunroof manufacturing capacity at Bawal, Haryana. The proposed expansion is aimed at catering to 
incremental customer orders secured by the Company and the growing demand for advanced sunroof 
systems in the Indian passenger vehicle market. The additional capacity is expected to be commissioned by 
Q2 FY28. 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 of SEBI Listing Regulations, read with Circular No. SEBI/HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-
POD2/l/3762/2026 dated January 30, 2026, the requisite details against this matter(s) is enclosed as 
Annexure- II to this letter. 
3) Changes in Senior Managerial Personnel ("SMP"l 
• 
Mr. Nitesh Minda will transition into a new role as Chief Executive officer-SCS Domain of the Company 
As part of the planned leadership succession of the SCS Domain of the company and in view of upcoming 
retirement of Mr. A.G. Giridharan, CEO-SCS Domain (SMP) of the Company, the Board of Directors of the 
Company, on the recommendation of Nomination and Remuneration Committee, has appointed Mr. Nitesh 
Minda as Chief Executive officer (Designate)-SCS Domain of the Company effective from November 05, 2026. 
Further, Mr. Minda will take over as CEO - SCS Domain upon retirement of Mr. Giridharan.

Mr. Nitesh Minda will work closely with Mr. Giridharan during the transition period to ensure a smooth 
handover and continuity of domain leadership. 
•
Elevation of Mr. Kartikeya Joshi to the role of Chief Marketing Officer (CMO) of the Company
The Board has approved the elevation of Mr. Kartikeya Joshi for taking over charge as Chief Marketing Officer 
effective from November 05, 2026. In this role, Mr. Kartikeya Joshi will lead the Group's marketing function. 
•
Additional charge to Mr. Amit Jain. re-designated as Group Chief Growth and Technology Officer
(CGTO)
The Board has approved the transition of Mr. Amit Jain, from currently serving as Group CTO and CEO - 4W 
Powertrain, into the newly created role of Group Chief Growth and Technology Officer (CGTO). 
In this expanded role, he will continue to lead the Group's Technology, R&D strategy, 4W EV business and 
will additionally oversee the Corporate Manufacturing Excellence, Digital and Strategy functions.

Q2`FY27 Earnings Release
EBIT margin delivered strong growth of 28.4% YoY, driven by richer premium product mix & scale 
benefits from robust volume growth offsetting elevated commodity prices particularly in copper, 
aluminum and Plastic (Polypropylene).
Segment’s delivered highest growth since listing, supported by strong double-digit momentum
across major categories with Washing Machines, Refrigerators & RAC led the charge, while 
Dishwashers delivered breakout growth. Our two-track strategy delivered growth across mass and
premium segments, while the expanding LG Essential range & newly launched Chest Freezers 
further widened our reach, strengthening market leadership across key categories.
We are well-positioned to capitalize on festive demand, with Go-to-Market investments made 
during the quarter ensuring channel readiness across key markets. Premium categories such as 
French Door Refrigerator, Dishwashers are expected to sustain their momentum, while exports and 
the upcoming Sri City plant compressor facility will power the next phase of growth 
The festive and wedding season is expected to drive strong consumption across categories, with 
consumer preference increasingly shifting toward premium, energy-efficient and larger-capacity 
appliances. While commodity and currency trends remain key monitorable overall industry sentiment 
remains positive heading into the peak demand season.

8

Home Entertainment
EBIT margin increased 19.9% YoY despite commodity inflation, FX headwinds, and strategic Go-to-
Market investments ahead of the festive season. Growth was supported by operating leverage from 
higher volumes and improved profitability in the B2B business, which continues to strengthen as a 
second profit engine alongside Television.
Profit
Revenue grew 17.2% YoY on a high base, marking the segment’s third consecutive quarter of double-
digit growth. Televisions led the momentum, with value growth outpacing volumes as consumer 
upgrades to larger screens and offline market share scaling to all time high widening our lead in the 
category. Our B2B business (Information Display) delivered strong growth, adding further depth to the 
segment’s growth engines.
Revenue
With TV market share at a record high, the addition of Mini LED TVs expands our offering to a wider 
consumer base, complementing our strong large-screen lineup and advanced QNED and OLED 
technologies. Festive go-to-market investments during Q2 ensure strong channel readiness to 
maximize sell-out. B2B business is expected to sustain its improved profitability, adding further 
resilience to segment margins.
LGEIL
The festive season is expected to be the key demand driver for the television category, as consumer 
preference continues to shift toward larger screen sizes and advanced display technologies, 
supporting value growth across the industry. Institutional demand for information displays is also 
expected to remain healthy.

LG Electronics India Continues Strong Momentum – 
Delivers Highest Growth Post Listing in Q2 FY27 
 
Delivers second consecutive quarter of double-digit growth: Revenue up 19.5%, 
EBITDA up 28.0% and PAT up 25.7%  
 
 
Key Highlights: 
• 
Robust revenue growth from operations for Q2 FY27, grew 19.5% YoY to ₹73.80 billion 
• 
EBITDA at ₹7.01 billion, up 28.0% YoY, with margin expanding 63 bps to 9.5% despite 
commodity and currency headwinds 
• 
Strong growth in Profit after tax (PAT) at ₹4.89 billion, up 25.7% YoY 
• 
Balanced growth across volume and value, mass and premium segments, with record-
high offline television market share  
• 
Home Appliances & Air Solution Segment: Highest growth since listing, with revenue 
up by 20.9% driven by strong double-digit growth across key categories 
• 
Home Entertainment Segment: Third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with 
revenue up 17.2% on a high base  
• 
Continues exports momentum, adding 20 new countries since the IPO, along with 
expansion of its product export portfolio 
• 
Diversifying into the high-growth automotive market with advanced Vehicle 
Solutions, creating new growth opportunities and strengthening our presence in the 
growing B2B sector 
 
New Delhi, November 5, 2026 - LG Electronics India Limited (LGE India), India's leading 
consumer electronics brand, today announced results for the second quarter of FY27, delivering its 
highest year-on-year growth since listing and a second consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.

LGE India continues its growth momentum by delivering strong revenue from operations of ₹73.80 
billion in Q2 FY27, up 19.5% over ₹61.74 billion in Q2 FY26. EBITDA rose 28.0% to ₹7.01 
billion, with margin expanding 63 basis points to 9.5%, while profit after tax (PAT) grew 25.7% 
to ₹4.89 billion. Increased profitability was achieved despite elevated commodity prices, rupee 
depreciation and go-to-market investments to capture the upcoming festive season demand.  
 
Looking at H1FY27, revenue grew 17.5% to ₹146.13 billion, PAT rose 26.5% to ₹11.42 billion, 
EBITDA grew 27.9% to ₹16.16 billion with EBITDA margin of 11.1% (up 0.9% YoY).  

 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
What distinguished the quarter was the quality of the growth. It was balanced across volume and 
value, and across both mass and premium segments. Both businesses contributed strongly - Home 
Appliances & Air Solution recorded its highest growth since listing, while Home Entertainment 
extended its run of double-digit growth to a third consecutive quarter on a high base. Television 
value market share reached a record high, and a fast-scaling export business complemented healthy 
domestic demand, reflecting growth that is broad-based and built to last. 
 
LGE India also announced its entry into a new B2B segment – Vehicle Solutions, In-Vehicle 
Infotainment (IVI). This initiative will bring LG Korea's key global B2B automotive business, 
including automotive infotainment and telematics solutions, to India. These products will be 
manufactured and supplied from LGE India’s 3rd plant at Sri City, Andhra Pradesh. 
 
Highlighting the results, Mr. Hong Ju Jeon, Managing Director, LGE India Limited, said, “We 
are proud to announce our second consecutive strong quarter results, culminating in a robust 
H1FY27. This performance reflects the broader strength of India’s consumer durables industry, 
which continues to benefit from rising disposable incomes, growing aspiration for premium 
products and deepening penetration across metro and emerging markets. As LGE India completes 
its first year as a listed company, this performance reflects the trust our shareholders have placed 
in us and our commitment to creating long-term value for them. Moving beyond consumer 
electronics, we are expanding our footprint in the rapidly evolving B2B sector, by entering a new 
B2B vertical, Vehicle Solutions. Our foundational three-pillar strategy—Make-in-India, Make-for-
India, and Make-India-Global—will continue driving our ambitious growth trajectory across 
domestic and export markets.” 
 
Category Performance  
 
Home Appliances & Air Solution (H&A) delivered its highest quarterly growth since listing, 
with revenue of ₹47.72 billion, up 20.9% YoY. Strong double-digit momentum ran across major 
categories, with washing machines, refrigerators and room air conditioners leading the charge, 
while dishwashers delivered breakout growth. The company's two-track strategy delivered growth 
across both mass and premium segments, and the expanding LG Essential Series range, together 
with the newly launched Chest Freezers and French Door Refrigerators further widened its reach, 
strengthening market leadership across key categories. 
 
Segment EBIT grew 28.4% YoY to ₹4.16 billion, with EBIT margin improving to 8.7% from 8.2% 
in Q2 FY26. Operating leverage on strong volume growth more than offset elevated commodity 
prices, currency impact on imports and go-to-market investments made ahead of the festive season. 
 
Home Entertainment (HE) delivered revenue of ₹26.08 billion, up 17.2% YoY on a high base, 
marking the segment's third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. Televisions led the 
momentum as consumers upgraded to larger screens and offline market share scaled to an all-time 
high, widening LG's lead in the category. The B2B Information Display business delivered strong 
growth, adding further depth to the segment's growth engines. 
 
Segment EBIT rose 19.9% to ₹3.37 billion, with EBIT margin improving to 12.9% from 12.6% in 
Q2 FY26. Elevated panel costs, currency impact on imports and incremental festive go-to-market 
investments were offset by operating leverage from strong revenue growth and improved 
profitability in the B2B business, which has emerged as a second profit engine alongside 
televisions. 

 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
FY27 Outlook 
• 
Strong festive and wedding season positioning, with go-to-market investments made in Q2 
ensuring channel readiness across key markets  
• 
Expanded television line-up: Mini LED TVs join the large-screen, QNED and OLED 
range, building on record-high television market share 
• 
Energy-efficient ACs to continue driving growth momentum 
• 
Premium momentum: French Door refrigerators and dishwashers expected to sustain 
growth as consumers shift towards premium, energy-efficient and larger-capacity 
appliances, while B2B continues to add resilience to margins 
• 
Export scale-up: India positioned as LG's preferred export hub, with over 20 new countries 
entered since the IPO 
• 
Sri City plant expected to commence operations in Q3 FY27 with compressor 
manufacturing, enhancing localisation and set to increase existing capacity for domestic 
and export demand 
 
Backed by a strong H1 FY27 performance, LGE India reaffirms its FY27 targets of mid-teen 
revenue growth and an early double-digit EBITDA margin. While commodity and currency trends 
remain key monitorables, these are being actively managed through localisation, calibrated pric-
ing and operational efficiency, and overall industry sentiment remains positive heading into the 
peak demand season.

risks, uncertainties and other factors, which may cause the actual results, financial condition, performance, or achievements of LGE 
India or industry results, to differ materially from the results, financial condition, performance or achievements expressed or implied 
by such forward-looking statements. LGE India disclaims any obligation to update these forward-looking statements to reflect future 
events or developments. 
 
# # # 
About LG Electronics India Ltd                
LG Electronics India Limited was established in January 1997 in India. It is focused on various consumer electronics 
and B2B businesses, from home appliances and media entertainment to HVAC and commercial displays. LGE India’s 
manufacturing units at Greater Noida and Ranjangaon, Pune have the capacity to manufacture LED TVs, air condition-
ers, commercial air conditioning systems, washing machines, refrigerators, monitors, water purifiers, microwave owens, 
etc.

LG Electronics India Continues Strong Momentum – 
Delivers Highest Growth Post Listing in Q2 FY27 
 
Delivers second consecutive quarter of double-digit growth: Revenue up 19.5%, 
EBITDA up 28.0% and PAT up 25.7%  
 
 
Key Highlights: 
• 
Robust revenue growth from operations for Q2 FY27, grew 19.5% YoY to ₹73.80 billion 
• 
EBITDA at ₹7.01 billion, up 28.0% YoY, with margin expanding 63 bps to 9.5% despite 
commodity and currency headwinds 
• 
Strong growth in Profit after tax (PAT) at ₹4.89 billion, up 25.7% YoY 
• 
Balanced growth across volume and value, mass and premium segments, with record-
high offline television market share  
• 
Home Appliances & Air Solution Segment: Highest growth since listing, with revenue 
up by 20.9% driven by strong double-digit growth across key categories 
• 
Home Entertainment Segment: Third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with 
revenue up 17.2% on a high base  
• 
Continues exports momentum, adding 20 new countries since the IPO, along with 
expansion of its product export portfolio 
• 
Diversifying into the high-growth automotive market with advanced Vehicle 
Solutions, creating new growth opportunities and strengthening our presence in the 
growing B2B sector 
 
New Delhi, November 5, 2026 - LG Electronics India Limited (LGE India), India's leading 
consumer electronics brand, today announced results for the second quarter of FY27, delivering its 
highest year-on-year growth since listing and a second consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.

LGE India continues its growth momentum by delivering strong revenue from operations of ₹73.80 
billion in Q2 FY27, up 19.5% over ₹61.74 billion in Q2 FY26. EBITDA rose 28.0% to ₹7.01 
billion, with margin expanding 63 basis points to 9.5%, while profit after tax (PAT) grew 25.7% 
to ₹4.89 billion. Increased profitability was achieved despite elevated commodity prices, rupee 
depreciation and go-to-market investments to capture the upcoming festive season demand.  
 
Looking at H1FY27, revenue grew 17.5% to ₹146.13 billion, PAT rose 26.5% to ₹11.42 billion, 
EBITDA grew 27.9% to ₹16.16 billion with EBITDA margin of 11.1% (up 0.9% YoY).  

 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
What distinguished the quarter was the quality of the growth. It was balanced across volume and 
value, and across both mass and premium segments. Both businesses contributed strongly - Home 
Appliances & Air Solution recorded its highest growth since listing, while Home Entertainment 
extended its run of double-digit growth to a third consecutive quarter on a high base. Television 
value market share reached a record high, and a fast-scaling export business complemented healthy 
domestic demand, reflecting growth that is broad-based and built to last. 
 
LGE India also announced its entry into a new B2B segment – Vehicle Solutions, In-Vehicle 
Infotainment (IVI). This initiative will bring LG Korea's key global B2B automotive business, 
including automotive infotainment and telematics solutions, to India. These products will be 
manufactured and supplied from LGE India’s 3rd plant at Sri City, Andhra Pradesh. 
 
Highlighting the results, Mr. Hong Ju Jeon, Managing Director, LGE India Limited, said, “We 
are proud to announce our second consecutive strong quarter results, culminating in a robust 
H1FY27. This performance reflects the broader strength of India’s consumer durables industry, 
which continues to benefit from rising disposable incomes, growing aspiration for premium 
products and deepening penetration across metro and emerging markets. As LGE India completes 
its first year as a listed company, this performance reflects the trust our shareholders have placed 
in us and our commitment to creating long-term value for them. Moving beyond consumer 
electronics, we are expanding our footprint in the rapidly evolving B2B sector, by entering a new 
B2B vertical, Vehicle Solutions. Our foundational three-pillar strategy—Make-in-India, Make-for-
India, and Make-India-Global—will continue driving our ambitious growth trajectory across 
domestic and export markets.” 
 
Category Performance  
 
Home Appliances & Air Solution (H&A) delivered its highest quarterly growth since listing, 
with revenue of ₹47.72 billion, up 20.9% YoY. Strong double-digit momentum ran across major 
categories, with washing machines, refrigerators and room air conditioners leading the charge, 
while dishwashers delivered breakout growth. The company's two-track strategy delivered growth 
across both mass and premium segments, and the expanding LG Essential Series range, together 
with the newly launched Chest Freezers and French Door Refrigerators further widened its reach, 
strengthening market leadership across key categories. 
 
Segment EBIT grew 28.4% YoY to ₹4.16 billion, with EBIT margin improving to 8.7% from 8.2% 
in Q2 FY26. Operating leverage on strong volume growth more than offset elevated commodity 
prices, currency impact on imports and go-to-market investments made ahead of the festive season. 
 
Home Entertainment (HE) delivered revenue of ₹26.08 billion, up 17.2% YoY on a high base, 
marking the segment's third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. Televisions led the 
momentum as consumers upgraded to larger screens and offline market share scaled to an all-time 
high, widening LG's lead in the category. The B2B Information Display business delivered strong 
growth, adding further depth to the segment's growth engines. 
 
Segment EBIT rose 19.9% to ₹3.37 billion, with EBIT margin improving to 12.9% from 12.6% in 
Q2 FY26. Elevated panel costs, currency impact on imports and incremental festive go-to-market 
investments were offset by operating leverage from strong revenue growth and improved 
profitability in the B2B business, which has emerged as a second profit engine alongside 
televisions. 

 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
FY27 Outlook 
• 
Strong festive and wedding season positioning, with go-to-market investments made in Q2 
ensuring channel readiness across key markets  
• 
Expanded television line-up: Mini LED TVs join the large-screen, QNED and OLED 
range, building on record-high television market share 
• 
Energy-efficient ACs to continue driving growth momentum 
• 
Premium momentum: French Door refrigerators and dishwashers expected to sustain 
growth as consumers shift towards premium, energy-efficient and larger-capacity 
appliances, while B2B continues to add resilience to margins 
• 
Export scale-up: India positioned as LG's preferred export hub, with over 20 new countries 
entered since the IPO 
• 
Sri City plant expected to commence operations in Q3 FY27 with compressor 
manufacturing, enhancing localisation and set to increase existing capacity for domestic 
and export demand 
 
Backed by a strong H1 FY27 performance, LGE India reaffirms its FY27 targets of mid-teen 
revenue growth and an early double-digit EBITDA margin. While commodity and currency trends 
remain key monitorables, these are being actively managed through localisation, calibrated pric-
ing and operational efficiency, and overall industry sentiment remains positive heading into the 
peak demand season.

risks, uncertainties and other factors, which may cause the actual results, financial condition, performance, or achievements of LGE 
India or industry results, to differ materially from the results, financial condition, performance or achievements expressed or implied 
by such forward-looking statements. LGE India disclaims any obligation to update these forward-looking statements to reflect future 
events or developments. 
 
# # # 
About LG Electronics India Ltd                
LG Electronics India Limited was established in January 1997 in India. It is focused on various consumer electronics 
and B2B businesses, from home appliances and media entertainment to HVAC and commercial displays. LGE India’s 
manufacturing units at Greater Noida and Ranjangaon, Pune have the capacity to manufacture LED TVs, air condition-
ers, commercial air conditioning systems, washing machines, refrigerators, monitors, water purifiers, microwave owens, 
etc.

automotive and mobility technologies, products, components, systems and software, as more

Company by insertion of a new Sub-clause 7 under the Main Objects of Clause III(A), to enable the

Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 and Regulation 33 read with Schedule III of the SEBI (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”), we hereby inform 
you that the Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held today i.e. Thursday,    
November 05, 2026, has inter-alia, considered and approved the following: 
 
(a) Unaudited Financial Results 
 
Approved the Unaudited Financial Results of the Company for the quarter and half year ended 
September 30, 2026. 
 
The said financial results have been limited reviewed by the Statutory Auditors of the Company and 
the Limited Review Report issued thereon is enclosed herewith. 
 
(b) Adoption of a new line of business – Vehicle Solutions Business 
 
Approved the proposal to enter into a new line of business, namely, the Vehicle Solutions Business, 
encompassing manufacturing, assembling, importing, exporting, distributing, trading, selling, 
supplying, installing, integrating, servicing, maintaining and providing solutions relating to 
automotive and mobility technologies, products, components, systems and software, as more 
particularly described in the proposed alteration to the Objects Clause of the Memorandum of 
Association of the Company. 
 
The details required under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations read with the applicable 
provisions of the SEBI Master Circular dated January 30, 2026, in respect of the adoption of the new 
line of business are enclosed herewith as Annexure-A. 
 
(c) Alteration of the Objects Clause of the Memorandum of Association (“MOA”) 
 
Approved the alteration of the Objects Clause of the Memorandum of Association (“MOA”) of the

Sub: Outcome of Board Meeting 
 
Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 and Regulation 33 read with Schedule III of the SEBI (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”), we hereby inform 
you that the Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held today i.e. Thursday,    
November 05, 2026, has inter-alia, considered and approved the following: 
 
(a) Unaudited Financial Results 
 
Approved the Unaudited Financial Results of the Company for the quarter and half year ended 
September 30, 2026. 
 
The said financial results have been limited reviewed by the Statutory Auditors of the Company and 
the Limited Review Report issued thereon is enclosed herewith. 
 
(b) Adoption of a new line of business – Vehicle Solutions Business 
 
Approved the proposal to enter into a new line of business, namely, the Vehicle Solutions Business, 
encompassing manufacturing, assembling, importing, exporting, distributing, trading, selling, 
supplying, installing, integrating, servicing, maintaining and providing solutions relating to 
automotive and mobility technologies, products, components, systems and software, as more 
particularly described in the proposed alteration to the Objects Clause of the Memorandum of 
Association of the Company. 
 
The details required under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations read with the applicable 
provisions of the SEBI Master Circular dated January 30, 2026, in respect of the adoption of the new 
line of business are enclosed herewith as Annexure-A. 
 
(c) Alteration of the Objects Clause of the Memorandum of Association (“MOA”) 
 
Approved the alteration of the Objects Clause of the Memorandum of Association (“MOA”) of the 
Company by insertion of a new Sub-clause 7 under the Main Objects of Clause III(A), to enable the 
Company to undertake the Vehicle Solutions Business, as detailed in the proposed Postal Ballot 
Notice, subject to the approval of the shareholders of the Company through Postal Ballot.

The proposed new line of business pertains to the Vehicle 
Solutions Business, which encompasses the manufacture, 
supply and service of advanced electronic and technology 
solutions for the automotive and mobility sectors.  
 
The business activities may include automotive infotainment 
systems, in-vehicle displays, head units, digital cockpit 
solutions, telematics and connectivity solutions, vehicle 
computing systems, cockpit domain controllers (CDCs),  
High-performance computing (HPC), Advanced Driver  
Assistance Systems (ADAS), human-machine interface 
(HMI), automotive software and other related automotive 
electronic components and technologies. 
 
The manufacturing of Vehicles Solutions products will take 
place at LGE India’s 3rd plant in Sri City, Andra Pradesh. 
 
2 
Expected benefits 
The proposed entry into the Vehicle Solutions business is 
expected to provide the following benefits to the Company: 
 
(i) 
Business 
Diversification: Expansion 
of 
the 
Company’s business portfolio beyond its existing product 
offerings and entry into the growing automotive electronics 
and mobility solutions sector.  
 
(ii) 
Growth 
Opportunities: Access 
to 
emerging 
opportunities arising from increasing demand for connected 
vehicles, digital cockpits, advanced infotainment systems and 
intelligent mobility solutions.   
 
(iii) 
 Enhanced 
Market 
Presence: Opportunity 
to 
establish and strengthen the Company’s presence in the 
automotive and mobility ecosystem in India. 
 
(iv) 
Long-term Business Growth: Creation of additional 
business opportunities, potential revenue streams and long-
term growth prospects for the Company. 
 
3 
Estimated amount to be 
invested 
The investments shall be undertaken in a phased manner, 
based on the scale of operations, technology and equipment 
requirements, regulatory requirements and prevailing market 
conditions.

Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, we wish to inform you that the Board of 
Directors in their meeting held on Thursday, November 05, 2026 have approved the alteration of 
object clause of the MOA of the company subject to the approval of shareholders of the company. 
Approval of the shareholders of the Company shall be taken through Postal Ballot. 
 
Further, the brief details of alteration in MOA as required under Regulation 30 read with Part A of the 
Schedule III of the SEBI Listing Regulations are as follows: 
 
Insertion of new Sub Clause 7 after Sub Clause 6 under the Main Object of Clause III (A), as set 
out below:- 
 
“7. To carry on the business of manufacturing, assembling, importing, exporting, distributing, 
trading, selling, supplying, installing, integrating, servicing, maintaining and providing solutions 
relating to automotive and mobility technologies, products, components, systems and software, 
including in-vehicle infotainment systems, head units, cockpit electronics, automotive displays, head-
up display (HUD), digital cockpits, central information displays (CIDs), audio video navigation 
(AV/AVN), cluster, telematics, telematics control units (TCUs), communication and networking 
systems, advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), automotive vision and sensing systems, 
wireless/5G connectivity, antennas, driver and occupant monitoring systems, adaptive cruise control, 
emergency braking and steering systems, traffic sign recognition systems, adaptive lighting and 
lighting assistance systems, in-cabin solutions, vehicle computing and electronic control systems, 
High-performance computing (HPC), Electronic control units (ECUs), central control units (CCUs), 
body control units (BCUs), domain control units (DCUs), cockpit domain controllers (CDCs), vehicle 
electrification and power electronics components, human-machine interface (HMI) solutions, 
automotive software, including vehicle operating systems, middleware, applications, software 
platforms, automotive contents platform, cloud-based solutions, software-defined vehicle (SDV) 
solutions, cybersecurity solutions and other electronic, electrical, digital and intelligent solutions for 
vehicles and mobility applications and to undertake related testing, technical support and other allied 
activities.”

the Limited Review Report issued thereon is enclosed herewith. 
 
(b) Adoption of a new line of business – Vehicle Solutions Business

encompassing manufacturing, assembling, importing, exporting, distributing, trading, selling, 
supplying, installing, integrating, servicing, maintaining and providing solutions relating to 
automotive and mobility technologies, products, components, systems and software, as more 
particularly described in the proposed alteration to the Objects Clause of the Memorandum of 
Association of the Company.

provisions of the SEBI Master Circular dated January 30, 2026, in respect of the adoption of the new 
line of business are enclosed herewith as Annexure-A.

Company by insertion of a new Sub-clause 7 under the Main Objects of Clause III(A), to enable the 
Company to undertake the Vehicle Solutions Business, as detailed in the proposed Postal Ballot 
Notice, subject to the approval of the shareholders of the Company through Postal Ballot.

Sub: Outcome of Board Meeting 
 
Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 and Regulation 33 read with Schedule III of the SEBI (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”), we hereby inform 
you that the Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held today i.e. Thursday,    
November 05, 2026, has inter-alia, considered and approved the following: 
 
(a) Unaudited Financial Results 
 
Approved the Unaudited Financial Results of the Company for the quarter and half year ended 
September 30, 2026. 
 
The said financial results have been limited reviewed by the Statutory Auditors of the Company and 
the Limited Review Report issued thereon is enclosed herewith. 
 
(b) Adoption of a new line of business – Vehicle Solutions Business 
 
Approved the proposal to enter into a new line of business, namely, the Vehicle Solutions Business, 
encompassing manufacturing, assembling, importing, exporting, distributing, trading, selling, 
supplying, installing, integrating, servicing, maintaining and providing solutions relating to 
automotive and mobility technologies, products, components, systems and software, as more 
particularly described in the proposed alteration to the Objects Clause of the Memorandum of 
Association of the Company. 
 
The details required under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations read with the applicable 
provisions of the SEBI Master Circular dated January 30, 2026, in respect of the adoption of the new 
line of business are enclosed herewith as Annexure-A. 
 
(c) Alteration of the Objects Clause of the Memorandum of Association (“MOA”) 
 
Approved the alteration of the Objects Clause of the Memorandum of Association (“MOA”) of the 
Company by insertion of a new Sub-clause 7 under the Main Objects of Clause III(A), to enable the 
Company to undertake the Vehicle Solutions Business, as detailed in the proposed Postal Ballot 
Notice, subject to the approval of the shareholders of the Company through Postal Ballot.

Adoption of a New Line of Business – Vehicle Solutions Business 
 
S. No. 
Particulars 
Details 
 
1 
Industry 
or 
area 
to 
which the new line of 
business belongs 
The proposed new line of business pertains to the Vehicle 
Solutions Business, which encompasses the manufacture, 
supply and service of advanced electronic and technology 
solutions for the automotive and mobility sectors.  
 
The business activities may include automotive infotainment 
systems, in-vehicle displays, head units, digital cockpit 
solutions, telematics and connectivity solutions, vehicle 
computing systems, cockpit domain controllers (CDCs),  
High-performance computing (HPC), Advanced Driver  
Assistance Systems (ADAS), human-machine interface 
(HMI), automotive software and other related automotive 
electronic components and technologies. 
 
The manufacturing of Vehicles Solutions products will take 
place at LGE India’s 3rd plant in Sri City, Andra Pradesh. 
 
2 
Expected benefits 
The proposed entry into the Vehicle Solutions business is 
expected to provide the following benefits to the Company: 
 
(i) 
Business 
Diversification: Expansion 
of 
the 
Company’s business portfolio beyond its existing product 
offerings and entry into the growing automotive electronics 
and mobility solutions sector.  
 
(ii) 
Growth 
Opportunities: Access 
to 
emerging 
opportunities arising from increasing demand for connected 
vehicles, digital cockpits, advanced infotainment systems and 
intelligent mobility solutions.   
 
(iii) 
 Enhanced 
Market 
Presence: Opportunity 
to 
establish and strengthen the Company’s presence in the 
automotive and mobility ecosystem in India. 
 
(iv) 
Long-term Business Growth: Creation of additional 
business opportunities, potential revenue streams and long-
term growth prospects for the Company. 
 
3 
Estimated amount to be 
invested 
The investments shall be undertaken in a phased manner, 
based on the scale of operations, technology and equipment 
requirements, regulatory requirements and prevailing market 
conditions.

Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, we wish to inform you that the Board of 
Directors in their meeting held on Thursday, November 05, 2026 have approved the alteration of 
object clause of the MOA of the company subject to the approval of shareholders of the company. 
Approval of the shareholders of the Company shall be taken through Postal Ballot. 
 
Further, the brief details of alteration in MOA as required under Regulation 30 read with Part A of the 
Schedule III of the SEBI Listing Regulations are as follows: 
 
Insertion of new Sub Clause 7 after Sub Clause 6 under the Main Object of Clause III (A), as set 
out below:- 
 
“7. To carry on the business of manufacturing, assembling, importing, exporting, distributing, 
trading, selling, supplying, installing, integrating, servicing, maintaining and providing solutions 
relating to automotive and mobility technologies, products, components, systems and software, 
including in-vehicle infotainment systems, head units, cockpit electronics, automotive displays, head-
up display (HUD), digital cockpits, central information displays (CIDs), audio video navigation 
(AV/AVN), cluster, telematics, telematics control units (TCUs), communication and networking 
systems, advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), automotive vision and sensing systems, 
wireless/5G connectivity, antennas, driver and occupant monitoring systems, adaptive cruise control, 
emergency braking and steering systems, traffic sign recognition systems, adaptive lighting and 
lighting assistance systems, in-cabin solutions, vehicle computing and electronic control systems, 
High-performance computing (HPC), Electronic control units (ECUs), central control units (CCUs), 
body control units (BCUs), domain control units (DCUs), cockpit domain controllers (CDCs), vehicle 
electrification and power electronics components, human-machine interface (HMI) solutions, 
automotive software, including vehicle operating systems, middleware, applications, software 
platforms, automotive contents platform, cloud-based solutions, software-defined vehicle (SDV) 
solutions, cybersecurity solutions and other electronic, electrical, digital and intelligent solutions for 
vehicles and mobility applications and to undertake related testing, technical support and other allied 
activities.”

Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 and Regulation 33 read with Schedule III of the SEBI (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”), we hereby inform 
you that the Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held today i.e. Thursday,    
November 05, 2026, has inter-alia, considered and approved the following: 
 
(a) Unaudited Financial Results 
 
Approved the Unaudited Financial Results of the Company for the quarter and half year ended 
September 30, 2026. 
 
The said financial results have been limited reviewed by the Statutory Auditors of the Company and 
the Limited Review Report issued thereon is enclosed herewith. 
 
(b) Adoption of a new line of business – Vehicle Solutions Business 
 
Approved the proposal to enter into a new line of business, namely, the Vehicle Solutions Business, 
encompassing manufacturing, assembling, importing, exporting, distributing, trading, selling, 
supplying, installing, integrating, servicing, maintaining and providing solutions relating to 
automotive and mobility technologies, products, components, systems and software, as more 
particularly described in the proposed alteration to the Objects Clause of the Memorandum of 
Association of the Company. 
 
The details required under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations read with the applicable 
provisions of the SEBI Master Circular dated January 30, 2026, in respect of the adoption of the new 
line of business are enclosed herewith as Annexure-A. 
 
(c) Alteration of the Objects Clause of the Memorandum of Association (“MOA”) 
 
Approved the alteration of the Objects Clause of the Memorandum of Association (“MOA”) of the 
Company by insertion of a new Sub-clause 7 under the Main Objects of Clause III(A), to enable the 
Company to undertake the Vehicle Solutions Business, as detailed in the proposed Postal Ballot 
Notice, subject to the approval of the shareholders of the Company through Postal Ballot.

Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
With reference to the captioned subject matter, we would like to inform you that the Board of Directors 
of the Company at its meeting held today i.e. November 5, 2026, has inter alia considered and approved 
following: 
 
1. 
The Unaudited (Standalone & Consolidated) Financial Results for the quarter and half year 
ended on September 30, 2026. The financial results along with Limited Review Reports are 
enclosed herewith. 
 
2. 
Interim Dividend for the financial year 2026-27 at the rate of Rs. 1.50/- per share of face value of 
Rs. 1/- each. The Record Date for determining the shareholders entitled for payment of the said 
Interim Divided has been fixed as Friday, November 13, 2026. 
 
3.  
Based on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, the following 
employees of the Company, have been designated as Senior Management Personnel in terms 
of Regulation 16(1)(d) of the SEBI Listing Regulations, with effect from November 5, 2026. 
 
a) Mr. Ritesh Patel, Associate Vice President – Technical Operations 
 
b) Mr. Pritesh Shah, Associate Vice President – Finance & Accounts

Master Circular No. SEBI/HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated January 30, 2026.

1. 
We have reviewed the accompanying statement of unaudited standalone financial results of Astral 
Limited (the "Company") for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and year to date from April 01, 
2026 to September 30, 2026 (the "Statement") attached herewith, being submitted by the Company 
pursuant to the requirements of Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended (the "Listing Regulations"). 
2. 
The Company's Management is responsible for the preparation of the Statement in accordance with 
the recognition and measurement principles laid down in Indian Accounting Standard 34, (Ind AS 
34) "Interim Financial Reporting" prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 as 
amended, read with relevant rules issued thereunder and other accounting principles generally 
accepted in India and in compliance with Regulation 33 of the Listing Regulations. The Statement 
has been approved by the Company's Board of Directors. Our responsibility is to express a 
conclusion on the Statement based on our review. 
3. 
We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagements 
(SRE) 2410, "Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of 
the Entity" issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. This standard requires that we 
plan and perform the review to obtain moderate assurance as to whether the Statement is free of 
material misstatement. A review of interim financial information consists of making inquiries, 
primarily of persons responsible for financial and accounting matters, and applying analytical and 
other review procedures. A review is substantially less in scope than an audit conducted in 
accordance with Standards on Auditing and consequently does not enable us to obtain assurance 
that we would become aware of all significant matters that might be identified in an audit. 
Accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion. 
4. 
Based on our review conducted as above, nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe 
that the accompanying Statement, prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement 
principles laid down in the aforesaid Indian Accounting Standards ('Ind AS') specified under 
Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 as amended, read with relevant rules issued thereunder and 
other accounting principles generally accepted in India, has not disclosed the information required 
to be disclosed in terms of the Listing Regulations, including the manner in which it is to be 
disclosed, or that it contains any material misstatement.

financial impact of the loss of inventory and certain fixed assets due to fire amounting to Rs.36.81 crores was recognised as "Exceptional item". The Company had filed an insurance 
claim for the aforesaid loss and accordingly, the Company had recorded an insurance claim receivable as at 31 March 2026 resulting in reversal of the recorded loss during the quarter

Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Rules, 2015, as amended. These results, as reviewed by the Audit Committee, were approved and taken on record by the Board of Directors

been completed and the related Report does not have any impact on the above 'Results and Notes' for the Quarter and Six Months ended September 30, 2026 which needs to be 
explained. 
2) The Company is primarily engaged in the business of 'Paints and Coatings'. There is no separate reportable segment as per Ind AS 108 -Operating Segments 
3) The exceptional items comprise the following: 
a. Impact of notification of Labour Codes 
On November 21, 2025, the Government of India notified four Labour Codes - the Code on Wages, 2019, the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, the Code on Social Security, 2020, and 
the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 consolidating 29 hitherto existing labour laws. The management had assessed and disclosed the incremental 
impact of these changes as an "Exceptional item" in the standalone statement of profit and loss for the year ended March 31,2026 
b. Fire incident at warehouse 
During the quarter ended June 30, 2025, there was a fire in a warehouse of the Company located in Barasat, West Bengal. There was no casualty reported due to the fire. The 
financial impact of the loss of inventory and certain fixed assets due to fire amounting to Rs.36.81 crores was recognised as "Exceptional item". The Company had filed an insurance 
claim for the aforesaid loss and accordingly, the Company had recorded an insurance claim receivable as at 31 March 2026 resulting in reversal of the recorded loss during the quarter 
ended 31 March 2026. The insurance claim proceeds were subsequently realised during the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

PRESS RELEASE – FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Premier Energies Reports Strong Q2 FY27 Results, Reinforces Leadership as India’s Largest
Integrated Solar Manufacturer
Hyderabad, 5 November 2026
Premier Energies Limited (NSE: PREMIERENE | BSE: 544238), India’s largest integrated solar
manufacturer, has announced its financial results for the quarter ended September 30,
2026. The Company reported total revenue of INR 26,560 million, registering a growth of
38.2% YOY. Quarterly EBITDA stood at INR 7,600 million, growing 17.8% YOY, with a margin
of 28.6%. Profit After Tax (PAT) reached INR 4,624 million, growing 30.8% YOY and translating
into a margin of 17.4%.
During the quarter, the Company produced 916 MW solar cells achieving a record 99%
capacity utilisation, 1,199 MW solar modules and 761 MVA transformers. These record
revenue and production numbers reflect strong operational performance driven by growing
scale and demand for high-efficiency products. With the commissioning of its 7 GW N-type
TOPCon solar cell facility at Naidupeta, Andhra Pradesh in September, the Company has
become the largest integrated manufacturer with total cell capacity of 10.6 GW and module
capacity of 11.1 GW.
Commenting on the results, Mr. Chiranjeev Saluja, Managing Director, Premier Energies
Limited, said: "Our steady performance in Q2 FY27 reflects disciplined execution and
operational excellence. The recent commissioning of our solar cell and module facilities
marks an important milestone in our growth journey and makes us well positioned to
capitalise on the growing demand for high-efficiency solar products. As these facilities ramp
up operations, they should help us in further enhancing production volumes, cutting down
costs and strengthening our technological capabilities."
About Premier Energies Limited
Premier Energies Limited is a publicly listed company and India's largest integrated solar
manufacturer, with 10.6 GW of solar cell and 11.1 GW of solar module manufacturing
capacity. With more than 30 years of solar manufacturing expertise, the Company is
recognised for its focus on technology innovation, sustainability and an employee-centric
culture.
The Company is undertaking a ₹12,500 crore capital expenditure programme to strengthen
its manufacturing capabilities, expand backward integration into ingots and wafers, and
diversify into inverters, transformers and battery energy storage systems. Premier Energies
has received Great Place to Work certification for five consecutive years.

Marketing & Communications
Premier Energies Limited

Management 
Commentary 
We delivered another strong quarter in 2QFY27, with revenue and EBITDA reaching their highest-
ever levels. Revenue grew ~45% YoY and EBITDA grew ~37% YoY, with margins remaining healthy 
at 28%. All three verticals contributed meaningfully to this performance, with our API segment 
delivering its highest-ever quarterly revenue, underscoring the breadth and resilience of our 
business.
Our novel FDF portfolio continues to make steady progress, with niche launches lined up through 
FY27 and beyond. We expect these launches to contribute meaningfully to our growth and to 
further strengthen the quality of our business over time.
At the core of our strategy is a deliberate focus on innovation-led differentiation, and it is 
increasingly translating into high-value partnerships with global companies. Our expanded 
partnership with Orion Corporation is a strong example, extending our relationship into immuno-
oncology through an exclusive arrangement for our Nivolumab biosimilar in Europe, with Shilpa as 
the development and supply partner. This partnership reinforces our position as a partner of choice 
for complex therapies.
These strategic choices are also reflected in our capital efficiency, with ROCE continuing its 
improving trend. Our progress on sustainability has also been recognized externally, with an 
improvement in our CRISIL ESG score, reflecting our commitment to responsible and well-governed 
growth. With strong first-half momentum, a maturing pipeline, and a sharpened strategic focus, we 
are well positioned to deliver a stronger FY27.

PRESS RELEASE 
FINANCIAL RESULTS OF NLCIL FOR THE QUARTER & HALF YEAR 
ENDED 30.09.2026 
Key Highlights - Standalone Physical and Finance Performance for the Half Vear 
Ended September 2026: 
• 
Achieved Coal production of 78.55 LT compared to 74.87 LT in H1 2025-26, 
registering a growth of 4.92%. 
• 
Achieved Coal Sales of 101 .23 LT compared to 88.37 LT In H1 2025-26, 
registering a growth of 14.55%. 
• 
Achieved NLCIL (Thermal) Power Gross Generation of 8,306.66 MU as against 
7,922.6 MU, registering a growth of 4.85%. 
• 
Total Revenue from operations for the Half Year ended 30th Sep 2026 is Rs. 
5,562.61 Cr against Rs. 5,060.51 Cr in the corresponding period of previous year, 
registering a growth of 9.92%. 
• 
Total 
Comprehensive 
Income (Comprising 
Profit or (Loss) and 
Other 
Comprehensive Income) for the period ended 30th Sep 2026 is Rs.1,623.41 Cr 
against Rs.842.25 Cr in the corresponding period of previous year, registering a 
growth of 92.75%. 
• 
The Net-worth as on 30.09.2026 stood at 20,858.73 Cr compared to 18,099.42 Cr 
in the previous year, registering a growth of 15.25%. 
• 
The Collection efficiency of Power debtors till 30.09.2026 stood at 104.58 % 
reflecting robust recovery measures and sustained improvement in receivables 
management. 
Key Highlights - Group Physical and Finance performance for the Half Vear 
Ended Sep 2026: 
• 
Achieved Gross Thermal Power Generation of 14,621.90 MU compared to 
12,249.34 MU in H1 2025-26, registering a growth of 19.37%. 
• 
Achieved Renewable Power Generation of 1,485.82 MU compared to 1,126.53 
MU in H1 2025-_26, registering a growth of 31.89%. 
• 
Achieved Coal production of 78.78 LT compared to 74.87 LT in H1 2025-26, 
registering a growth of 5.22%. 

• 
All time Highest Ever Revenue from operations for the Half Year Ended 30th Sep 
2026 of Rs.9,449.10 Cr as against Rs.8,004.02 Cr in the corresponding period of 
previous year, registering a growth of 18.05%. 
• 
All time Highest Ever Total Profit After tax (PAT) for the Half Year ended 30th Sep 
2026 of Rs. 1,764.34 Cr as against Rs. 1,564.01 Cr in the corresponding period 
of previous year, registering a growth of 12.81 %. 
• 
The Net-worth as on 30.09.2026 stood at 23,400.83 Cr compared to 19,965.62 
Cr in the previous year of H 1 2025-26 registering a growth of 17.21 %. 
• 
Interim dividend@ 15% is declared for the year 2026-27.

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Indian Energy Exchange Q2 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call hosted by Axis Capital Limited. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in 
the listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the 
presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during this conference call, please signal an 
operator by pressing star then zero on your touch-tone phone. Please note that this conference is 
being recorded. 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Rohan Gheewala from Axis Capital. Please go ahead. 
Rohan Gheewala: 
Thank you. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. On behalf of Axis Capital, I am pleased to 
welcome you all to the IEX Q2 FY27 earnings conference call. We have with us the management 
team of IEX, which is represented by Mr. Rohit Bajaj, Joint Managing Director, Mr. 
Satyanarayan Goel, Chairman and Managing Director, Mr. Vineet Harlalka, Chief Financial 
Officer, Mr. Amit Kumar, Head of Operations, New Product Initiatives and Exchange 
Technology, and Ms. Aparna Garg, Head Investor Relations and Corporate Communications. 
We will begin with the opening remarks from Mr. Rohit Bajaj, followed by an interactive Q&A 
session. Thank you, and over to you, Sir. 
Rohit Bajaj: 
Thank you. Good afternoon, friends. I welcome you all to the IEX earning call for Q2 FY 2027. 
With me today on this call are Mr. Satyanarayan Goel, CMD, IEX, Mr. Vineet Harlalka, CFO 
and Company Secretary, Mr. Amit Kumar, Head of Market Operations and Exchange 
Technology, Ms. Aparna Garg, Head of Investor Relations and Corporate Communications; and 
Mr. Aditya Wali. 
Friends, amid global uncertainty and inflationary pressures driven by oil supply volatility, India 
continues to remain the fastest growing major economy in the world, having recorded strong 
GDP growth of 7.8% in Q1 FY27. Reinforcing this outlook, the IMF recently revised its forecast 
upwards and projects India’s GDP to grow by 7% in each of the next 2 years. 
This growth trajectory is powered by strong domestic demand, robust services activity, and 
favourable demographic trends. Notably, this performance comes despite severe El Nino 
conditions, which led to the fourth lowest performing monsoon season this century, with rainfall 
at just 87% of the long-period average. 
Looking at the bigger picture, India is steadily progressing toward a USD5 trillion economy by 
FY30, driven by reforms like GST rationalization, new labor codes, and FTAs with the UK, 
Switzerland, New Zealand, and the forthcoming one with EU and some other countries. 
Together, they are advancing the vision of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. This growth story will be 
fueled by electricity at its core. 
The power sector witnessed sustained demand growth during the first half of the year supported 
by strong industrial activity and higher irrigation demand amid the weak monsoon. In the first 
half of FY27, power demand grew 10.2% Y-o-Y to touch 897 billion units. Elevated 
temperatures due to El Nino and deficient monsoon rainfall drove Q2 electricity demand to 502 
billion units, marking a record 11.5% year-on-year increase. 

 
Indian Energy Exchange Limited 
October 30, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 18 
 
While peak demand during the summer reached 271 gigawatt, it remained elevated at 269 
gigawatt in September. The demand and supply scenario remained volatile during the quarter. 
A weak monsoon increased buy bids in IEX day-ahead market by nearly 120% Y-o-Y in Q2, 
pushing up average DAM prices nearly 46% Y-o-Y to INR5.72 per unit and average RTM price 
higher by 49% Y-o-Y to INR5.24 per unit. 
With prices touching INR20 per unit in certain time blocks during the quarter, the high-priced 
day-ahead market, (HP DAM), played a critical role by enabling unmet demand bids to transition 
into the high-price segment, ensuring supply for buyers with urgent power requirements. 
However, cyclones and unseasonal rains during the later part of the quarter moderated demand 
in several regions, providing ample supply liquidity and driving RTM prices to near zero in 
multiple time blocks on a few days.  
In the first half of fiscal, prices during solar hour touched an average of INR2.3 per unit pushing 
up arbitrage opportunity to over INR6.5 per unit for both 2-hour, 2 cycles per day and 4-hour, 1 
cycle per day battery storage systems and providing further opportunity for addition of BESS 
capacity. 
On the fuel side, domestic coal production was largely flat at 445 million ton in H1 FY27 
compared with H1 FY26. Summer demand strained plant inventories and weather disruption 
tightened availability further. As of 22nd October 2026, coal inventory stood at nearly 8 days 
with stock at about 100 plants at a critical 3 days level. 
The Ministry of Power has been closely monitoring coal stocks and has taken various measures 
to improve coal availability, and some of these measures can be seen on the ground. Further, 
MoP has invoked Section 11 of the Electricity Act to direct over 100 captive coal-fired plants as 
well as Coastal Gujarat Power Limited, CGPL, imported coal-based plant to maximize 
generation till 31st December 2026. 
Let us now talk about few important regulatory updates and policy initiatives during the quarter.  
• 
Earlier this May, CERC issued a discussion paper on strengthening and scheduling 
timelines for real-time market. The paper proposes reduction of RTM auction window 
from 15 minutes to 5 minutes, and thereby reducing gate closure time from 75 minutes 
to 50 minutes. 
The objective is to enable better forecasting, more efficient management of 
renewables, and enhance liquidity on the exchange platform. The same has now been 
proposed in draft grid code, (IEGC), and public comments on the proposal were 
invited and closed last week. 
• 
The CERC issued amendments to the Sharing of Inter-State Transmission Charges and 
Losses Regulation 2020, providing ISGF charges waiver for up to 25 years for battery 
energy storage systems integrated with renewable or hybrid generating stations. 

 
Indian Energy Exchange Limited 
October 30, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 18 
 
This should expectedly reduce the cost of power trading for BESS players and increase 
liquidity on exchanges. 
• 
In other developments, CERC has identified the Green Day Ahead market as a source 
of green power for energy storage systems such as BESS and PSP to procure power 
and meet eligibility criteria to qualify as green storage. This classification should 
increase trading in G-DAM segment at exchanges.  
 
• 
The CEA made draft amendment to Technical Standards for Construction of Electric 
Plants and Electric Lines, Second Amendment 2026. The draft proposes that solar and 
onshore wind projects commissioned after July 1st, 2027 would have to be equipped 
with co-located energy storage system with a minimum 2-hour storage duration and 
capacity equivalent to at least 10% of the plant installed capacity. It further proposes 
an increase in storage duration for projects commissioned after July 1st, 2029, and up 
to July 30th, 2031. These solar and onshore wind projects would be required to install 
co-located ESS with a minimum 4-hour storage duration with storage capacity equal 
to at least 10% of the plant installed capacity. These measures would help in grid 
stability going forward as countrywide renewable capacity increases and provide 
liquidity on the exchanges. 
 
• 
With regards to the carbon market wherein carbon credit certificates are to be traded 
on power exchanges, Bureau of Energy Efficiency, (BEE), in consultation with Grid 
India, has issued draft procedures for trading of these certificates under the compliance 
mechanism. In conjunction, IEX has filed a petition with the CERC for approval of 
carbon credit certificate trading on the exchanges. 
On market coupling, in July 2025, CERC issued an order proposing implementation of market 
coupling in the Day-Ahead Market, pursuant to which IEX filed an appeal before APTEL and 
subsequently in the Supreme Court. Both forums observed that market coupling cannot be 
implemented by this order and it can only be implemented after the regulations are issued. And 
hence, IEX is not an aggrieved party yet, and they do not wish to interfere at this stage. 
If IEX is aggrieved by the final regulation, they can approach the appropriate forum, including 
the grounds raised in the appeal made. Meanwhile, CERC issued draft regulation for market 
coupling in the month of April, and proposed Grid India as the market coupling operator. 
Submission of comments by stakeholders and public hearing on draft regulation was completed 
in the month of June. There has been no further development on this during this particular 
quarter. 
 
CERC in its order of July 2025 had also mentioned that in case of Real-Time Market, since the 
timelines are very tight for bidding and the auction process, this would be considered 
subsequently. In light of the CERC discussion paper for shortening the scheduling in Real-Time 
Market, that is, reducing the gate closure time from 75 to 50 minutes, where RTM bidding will 
be reduced from 15 to 5 minutes, coupling is likely to become more challenging. 

 
Indian Energy Exchange Limited 
October 30, 2026

Further, over the last 3 years, we have undertaken several initiatives to strengthen our customer 
relationships and technology capabilities, including extensive customer interactions and 
feedback, providing API-based bidding tools, back-office integration through APIs, data 
analytics, enhanced web portal, customer-centric digital solutions, and reinforced cybersecurity 
safeguards. 
 
With our customer-centric initiative track record of trust and deep customer engagement, we 
shall be able to retain and strengthen our market position post coupling. 
 
Moving on to IEX performance in this quarter. During Q2 FY27, IEX recorded electricity 
trading volume of 39.7 billion units, a year-on-year growth of 12.7%. For H1 FY27, electricity 
traded volume reached 77 billion units, a growth of 14.2% over the first half of FY26. 
 
Revenue for the company grew by 10.7% year-on-year, increasing from INR 183.3 crores in Q2 
FY26 to INR 203 crores in Q2 FY27. Profit after tax increased by 12.9%, rising from INR 123 
crores in Q2 FY26 to INR 139 crores in Q2 FY27.  
In Q2 FY27, 15.3 lakhs Renewable Energy Certificates were traded, considerably lower than 44 
lakhs certificates traded over the same quarter in FY26. 
 
The RTM segment continued to demonstrate strong growth with nearly 42% share in electricity 
volume at IEX, surpassing the share of the DAM segment for the second quarter in succession. 
The segment witnessed the highest ever single day volume of 315 million units during the month 
of September. 
 
For Q2 FY27, RTM volumes at nearly 16.5 billion units were higher by 10.5% on a year-on-
year basis, highlighting the segment's critical role in helping distribution companies and open 
access consumers efficiently manage their short-term requirements. RTM's ability to offer 
flexibility and immediate responsiveness underlines the opportunity to efficiently integrate 
renewables with the grid and weather-related volatilities. 
 
With regard our product pipeline, we continue to await approval from the CERC on our petitions 
to extend the Term-Ahead Market contract from 3 months to 11 months; to introduce the Green 
RTM contract; and third, with regard to introduction of Peak DAM and Peak RTM segments. 
 
Moving on to IGX numbers. IGX traded gas volumes of 42 million MMBtu in Q2 FY27, a 
growth of 160% over Q2 FY26, led by volumes from domestic gas producers and heightened 
power demand being met by gas power plants during the month of August and September. In 
Q2 FY27, nearly 30% of the traded gas volumes were from the power sector. For the first half 
of the year, traded gas volume reached around 70 million MMBtu, higher by nearly 71% over 
H1 FY26.  
For Q2 FY27, IGX recorded a profit after tax of INR23.4 crores, which was higher by 144% 
compared with INR9.6 crores in Q2 FY26. PAT in H1 FY27 stood at INR39.7 crores, an increase 
of 67.4% over H1 FY26.

As you may be aware, we had filed a DRHP, (Draft Red Herring Prospectus), for an IPO of IGX 
earlier in July this financial year. As per PNGRB regulations, (Petroleum and Natural Gas 
Board), we have to lower our existing holding from 47.3% to 25% by end of December 2026, 
and the IPO process remains on track. 
 
Our other diversification initiatives are also gradually gathering momentum. For Q2 FY27, ICX 
Private Limited issued nearly 52 lakhs I-RECs, a growth of 38.4% Y-o-Y. Issuance in the first 
half of FY27 reached 94 lakhs, a growth of 15% over H1 FY26. Revenue for ICX in Q2 FY27 
stood at INR2.3 crores, higher by 20.8% on a year-on-year basis. I-REC is a globally recognized 
digital certificate that serves as a transferable proof of generation of 1 megawatt hour of energy 
from renewable sources. 
 
With regards our initiative to build a coal exchange in India, IEX has incorporated Indian Coal 
Exchange Limited as a wholly owned subsidiary for this purpose. Recently in September, Indian 
Coal Exchange Limited applied for a license with Coal Controller Organisation, CCO, the 
regulatory body for coal exchanges. 
 
Indian Coal Exchange aims to be a physical delivery-based coal trading exchange, providing an 
organized, transparent and technology-enabled marketplace for coal trading in accordance with 
the Coal Exchange Rules, 2026. The exchange will facilitate trades at designated delivery points, 
enabling efficient price discovery and wider market access. 
 
Further in line with the Government’s vision of bringing transparency in trades of all 
commodities, Ministry of Mines has also notified final regulations for a mineral exchange. This 
development is being explored and should provide us with another diversification opportunity. 
 
With the power consumption forecast to hit nearly 2,700 billion units going forward with peak 
demand of 388 gigawatt by 2032, we believe power demand growth will continue to drive 
exchange volume growth in the coming few years. In response to this expected demand growth, 
the MoP has been regularly monitoring the road map of thermal capacity addition, which has 
now been revised from an earlier 80 gigawatt by 2032 to 115 gigawatt by 2035. 
 
In addition, the Government and regulators continue to take policy measures to ease supply 
liquidity to rationalize power prices on exchange. India’s power sector continues to experience 
fast-paced transition. The government focus on green hydrogen, data centers, AI economy, 
electric vehicles, pump storage, battery energy storage, all this will lead to innovation of new 
products and market segment on the exchanges. 
 
Battery Energy Storage Systems and FDRE round-the-clock tenders are gaining traction. To 
further deepen the green markets, we have continued to advocate market-based options like 
CfDs, virtual PPAs and merchant models for RE capacity addition. 
 
And going forward, with large-scale rooftop solar, we see emergence of local energy markets 
and ecosystem where exchanges will play a central role. These developments are poised to 
become key enablers in expanding and deepening the country's power market to support a 
successful energy transition.

Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Indian Energy Exchange Q2 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call hosted by Axis Capital Limited. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in 
the listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the 
presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during this conference call, please signal an
