I now hand the conference over to Mr. Rohan Gheewala from Axis Capital. Please go ahead. 
Rohan Gheewala: 
Thank you. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. On behalf of Axis Capital, I am pleased to 
welcome you all to the IEX Q2 FY27 earnings conference call. We have with us the management 
team of IEX, which is represented by Mr. Rohit Bajaj, Joint Managing Director, Mr. 
Satyanarayan Goel, Chairman and Managing Director, Mr. Vineet Harlalka, Chief Financial 
Officer, Mr. Amit Kumar, Head of Operations, New Product Initiatives and Exchange 
Technology, and Ms. Aparna Garg, Head Investor Relations and Corporate Communications. 
We will begin with the opening remarks from Mr. Rohit Bajaj, followed by an interactive Q&A 
session. Thank you, and over to you, Sir. 
Rohit Bajaj: 
Thank you. Good afternoon, friends. I welcome you all to the IEX earning call for Q2 FY 2027. 
With me today on this call are Mr. Satyanarayan Goel, CMD, IEX, Mr. Vineet Harlalka, CFO 
and Company Secretary, Mr. Amit Kumar, Head of Market Operations and Exchange 
Technology, Ms. Aparna Garg, Head of Investor Relations and Corporate Communications; and 
Mr. Aditya Wali. 
Friends, amid global uncertainty and inflationary pressures driven by oil supply volatility, India 
continues to remain the fastest growing major economy in the world, having recorded strong 
GDP growth of 7.8% in Q1 FY27. Reinforcing this outlook, the IMF recently revised its forecast 
upwards and projects India’s GDP to grow by 7% in each of the next 2 years. 
This growth trajectory is powered by strong domestic demand, robust services activity, and 
favourable demographic trends. Notably, this performance comes despite severe El Nino 
conditions, which led to the fourth lowest performing monsoon season this century, with rainfall 
at just 87% of the long-period average. 
Looking at the bigger picture, India is steadily progressing toward a USD5 trillion economy by 
FY30, driven by reforms like GST rationalization, new labor codes, and FTAs with the UK, 
Switzerland, New Zealand, and the forthcoming one with EU and some other countries. 
Together, they are advancing the vision of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. This growth story will be 
fueled by electricity at its core. 
The power sector witnessed sustained demand growth during the first half of the year supported 
by strong industrial activity and higher irrigation demand amid the weak monsoon. In the first 
half of FY27, power demand grew 10.2% Y-o-Y to touch 897 billion units. Elevated 
temperatures due to El Nino and deficient monsoon rainfall drove Q2 electricity demand to 502 
billion units, marking a record 11.5% year-on-year increase. 

 
Indian Energy Exchange Limited 
October 30, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 18 
 
While peak demand during the summer reached 271 gigawatt, it remained elevated at 269 
gigawatt in September. The demand and supply scenario remained volatile during the quarter. 
A weak monsoon increased buy bids in IEX day-ahead market by nearly 120% Y-o-Y in Q2, 
pushing up average DAM prices nearly 46% Y-o-Y to INR5.72 per unit and average RTM price 
higher by 49% Y-o-Y to INR5.24 per unit. 
With prices touching INR20 per unit in certain time blocks during the quarter, the high-priced 
day-ahead market, (HP DAM), played a critical role by enabling unmet demand bids to transition 
into the high-price segment, ensuring supply for buyers with urgent power requirements. 
However, cyclones and unseasonal rains during the later part of the quarter moderated demand 
in several regions, providing ample supply liquidity and driving RTM prices to near zero in 
multiple time blocks on a few days.  
In the first half of fiscal, prices during solar hour touched an average of INR2.3 per unit pushing 
up arbitrage opportunity to over INR6.5 per unit for both 2-hour, 2 cycles per day and 4-hour, 1 
cycle per day battery storage systems and providing further opportunity for addition of BESS 
capacity. 
On the fuel side, domestic coal production was largely flat at 445 million ton in H1 FY27 
compared with H1 FY26. Summer demand strained plant inventories and weather disruption 
tightened availability further. As of 22nd October 2026, coal inventory stood at nearly 8 days 
with stock at about 100 plants at a critical 3 days level. 
The Ministry of Power has been closely monitoring coal stocks and has taken various measures 
to improve coal availability, and some of these measures can be seen on the ground. Further, 
MoP has invoked Section 11 of the Electricity Act to direct over 100 captive coal-fired plants as 
well as Coastal Gujarat Power Limited, CGPL, imported coal-based plant to maximize 
generation till 31st December 2026. 
Let us now talk about few important regulatory updates and policy initiatives during the quarter.  
• 
Earlier this May, CERC issued a discussion paper on strengthening and scheduling 
timelines for real-time market. The paper proposes reduction of RTM auction window 
from 15 minutes to 5 minutes, and thereby reducing gate closure time from 75 minutes 
to 50 minutes. 
The objective is to enable better forecasting, more efficient management of 
renewables, and enhance liquidity on the exchange platform. The same has now been 
proposed in draft grid code, (IEGC), and public comments on the proposal were 
invited and closed last week. 
• 
The CERC issued amendments to the Sharing of Inter-State Transmission Charges and 
Losses Regulation 2020, providing ISGF charges waiver for up to 25 years for battery 
energy storage systems integrated with renewable or hybrid generating stations. 

 
Indian Energy Exchange Limited 
October 30, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 18 
 
This should expectedly reduce the cost of power trading for BESS players and increase 
liquidity on exchanges. 
• 
In other developments, CERC has identified the Green Day Ahead market as a source 
of green power for energy storage systems such as BESS and PSP to procure power 
and meet eligibility criteria to qualify as green storage. This classification should 
increase trading in G-DAM segment at exchanges.  
 
• 
The CEA made draft amendment to Technical Standards for Construction of Electric 
Plants and Electric Lines, Second Amendment 2026. The draft proposes that solar and 
onshore wind projects commissioned after July 1st, 2027 would have to be equipped 
with co-located energy storage system with a minimum 2-hour storage duration and 
capacity equivalent to at least 10% of the plant installed capacity. It further proposes 
an increase in storage duration for projects commissioned after July 1st, 2029, and up 
to July 30th, 2031. These solar and onshore wind projects would be required to install 
co-located ESS with a minimum 4-hour storage duration with storage capacity equal 
to at least 10% of the plant installed capacity. These measures would help in grid 
stability going forward as countrywide renewable capacity increases and provide 
liquidity on the exchanges. 
 
• 
With regards to the carbon market wherein carbon credit certificates are to be traded 
on power exchanges, Bureau of Energy Efficiency, (BEE), in consultation with Grid 
India, has issued draft procedures for trading of these certificates under the compliance 
mechanism. In conjunction, IEX has filed a petition with the CERC for approval of 
carbon credit certificate trading on the exchanges. 
On market coupling, in July 2025, CERC issued an order proposing implementation of market 
coupling in the Day-Ahead Market, pursuant to which IEX filed an appeal before APTEL and 
subsequently in the Supreme Court. Both forums observed that market coupling cannot be 
implemented by this order and it can only be implemented after the regulations are issued. And 
hence, IEX is not an aggrieved party yet, and they do not wish to interfere at this stage. 
If IEX is aggrieved by the final regulation, they can approach the appropriate forum, including 
the grounds raised in the appeal made. Meanwhile, CERC issued draft regulation for market 
coupling in the month of April, and proposed Grid India as the market coupling operator. 
Submission of comments by stakeholders and public hearing on draft regulation was completed 
in the month of June. There has been no further development on this during this particular 
quarter. 
 
CERC in its order of July 2025 had also mentioned that in case of Real-Time Market, since the 
timelines are very tight for bidding and the auction process, this would be considered 
subsequently. In light of the CERC discussion paper for shortening the scheduling in Real-Time 
Market, that is, reducing the gate closure time from 75 to 50 minutes, where RTM bidding will 
be reduced from 15 to 5 minutes, coupling is likely to become more challenging.

Further, over the last 3 years, we have undertaken several initiatives to strengthen our customer 
relationships and technology capabilities, including extensive customer interactions and 
feedback, providing API-based bidding tools, back-office integration through APIs, data 
analytics, enhanced web portal, customer-centric digital solutions, and reinforced cybersecurity

With our customer-centric initiative track record of trust and deep customer engagement, we

Moving on to IEX performance in this quarter. During Q2 FY27, IEX recorded electricity

In Q2 FY27, 15.3 lakhs Renewable Energy Certificates were traded, considerably lower than 44

The RTM segment continued to demonstrate strong growth with nearly 42% share in electricity

For Q2 FY27, RTM volumes at nearly 16.5 billion units were higher by 10.5% on a year-on-
year basis, highlighting the segment's critical role in helping distribution companies and open

With regard our product pipeline, we continue to await approval from the CERC on our petitions 
to extend the Term-Ahead Market contract from 3 months to 11 months; to introduce the Green 
RTM contract; and third, with regard to introduction of Peak DAM and Peak RTM segments. 
 
Moving on to IGX numbers. IGX traded gas volumes of 42 million MMBtu in Q2 FY27, a 
growth of 160% over Q2 FY26, led by volumes from domestic gas producers and heightened 
power demand being met by gas power plants during the month of August and September. In 
Q2 FY27, nearly 30% of the traded gas volumes were from the power sector. For the first half 
of the year, traded gas volume reached around 70 million MMBtu, higher by nearly 71% over 
H1 FY26.  
For Q2 FY27, IGX recorded a profit after tax of INR23.4 crores, which was higher by 144% 
compared with INR9.6 crores in Q2 FY26. PAT in H1 FY27 stood at INR39.7 crores, an increase 
of 67.4% over H1 FY26. 

 
Indian Energy Exchange Limited 
October 30, 2026

As you may be aware, we had filed a DRHP, (Draft Red Herring Prospectus), for an IPO of IGX 
earlier in July this financial year. As per PNGRB regulations, (Petroleum and Natural Gas 
Board), we have to lower our existing holding from 47.3% to 25% by end of December 2026, 
and the IPO process remains on track. 
 
Our other diversification initiatives are also gradually gathering momentum. For Q2 FY27, ICX 
Private Limited issued nearly 52 lakhs I-RECs, a growth of 38.4% Y-o-Y. Issuance in the first 
half of FY27 reached 94 lakhs, a growth of 15% over H1 FY26. Revenue for ICX in Q2 FY27 
stood at INR2.3 crores, higher by 20.8% on a year-on-year basis. I-REC is a globally recognized 
digital certificate that serves as a transferable proof of generation of 1 megawatt hour of energy 
from renewable sources. 
 
With regards our initiative to build a coal exchange in India, IEX has incorporated Indian Coal 
Exchange Limited as a wholly owned subsidiary for this purpose. Recently in September, Indian 
Coal Exchange Limited applied for a license with Coal Controller Organisation, CCO, the 
regulatory body for coal exchanges. 
 
Indian Coal Exchange aims to be a physical delivery-based coal trading exchange, providing an 
organized, transparent and technology-enabled marketplace for coal trading in accordance with 
the Coal Exchange Rules, 2026. The exchange will facilitate trades at designated delivery points, 
enabling efficient price discovery and wider market access. 
 
Further in line with the Government’s vision of bringing transparency in trades of all 
commodities, Ministry of Mines has also notified final regulations for a mineral exchange. This 
development is being explored and should provide us with another diversification opportunity. 
 
With the power consumption forecast to hit nearly 2,700 billion units going forward with peak 
demand of 388 gigawatt by 2032, we believe power demand growth will continue to drive 
exchange volume growth in the coming few years. In response to this expected demand growth, 
the MoP has been regularly monitoring the road map of thermal capacity addition, which has 
now been revised from an earlier 80 gigawatt by 2032 to 115 gigawatt by 2035. 
 
In addition, the Government and regulators continue to take policy measures to ease supply 
liquidity to rationalize power prices on exchange. India’s power sector continues to experience 
fast-paced transition. The government focus on green hydrogen, data centers, AI economy, 
electric vehicles, pump storage, battery energy storage, all this will lead to innovation of new 
products and market segment on the exchanges. 
 
Battery Energy Storage Systems and FDRE round-the-clock tenders are gaining traction. To 
further deepen the green markets, we have continued to advocate market-based options like 
CfDs, virtual PPAs and merchant models for RE capacity addition. 
 
And going forward, with large-scale rooftop solar, we see emergence of local energy markets 
and ecosystem where exchanges will play a central role. These developments are poised to 
become key enablers in expanding and deepening the country's power market to support a 
successful energy transition.

accounting purpose as specified in the said Regulations. Based on legal opinions obtained, the Company continues with the consistently followed practice of recouping from the retained earnings an 
additional charge of depreciation relatable to the increase in value of assets arising from fair valuation, which amounts to Rs. 47 crore, Rs 46 crore, Rs 47 crore, Rs 93 crore, Rs 94 crore and Rs 188 
crore for the respective periods presented.

adjustments of AAD computed in terms of the Tariff regulations, as amended from time to time.

3 In the above standalone financial results of the Company. revenue from operations has been arrived at based on the relevant orders of the West Bengal Electricity Regulatory Commission 
(WBERC), the Regulator and levy of Fuel and Power Purchase Adjustment Surcharge (FPPAS) from June 2024 as per applicable rules. The effect of adjustments relating to cost of fuel, purchase of 
power and those having bearing on revenue account, deferred tax estimate and certain other fixed costs, as appropriate, based on the Company's understanding of the applicable regulatory 
provisions amended till date and available orders of the competent authorities have been included in Regulatory income/ (expense) (net), which may necessitate further adjustments upon receipt of 
subsequent orders/directions in this regard, including finalisation of the underlying issues relating to mining of coal from Sarisatoli coal mine, which commenced operations from April, 2015 and other 
matters pending under appeal for various years. These estimates have been recognised assuming recovery over a period of time, in consonance with the applicable regulations and application of 
prudence. Further, the APR orders for 2019-20 & 2020-21 and MYT order for the period 2023-24 to 2025-26 received during the previous years and APR order for 2021-22 and 2022-23 received 
during the current period has deviated from past practices / extant regulations in certain matters, for which the Company has filed/in process of filing necessary appeals. Based on legal opinion 
obtained, the Company is confident of the matter being adjudicated in its favour. Accordingly, necessary adjustment, if any, will be made on the matter reaching finality.However, as matter of 
prudence, the Company has made provision of Rs 80 crore (net of unwinding of discount impact) in respect of certain old regulatory asset balances in the current period. 
4 In terms of applicable Regulations under the Electricity Act, 2003, depreciation on tangible assets other than freehold land is provided on straight line method on a pro-rata basis at the rates specified 
therein, the basis of which is considered by the West Bengal Electricity Regulatory Commission (WBERC) in determining the Company's tariff for the year, which is also required to be used for 
accounting purpose as specified in the said Regulations. Based on legal opinions obtained, the Company continues with the consistently followed practice of recouping from the retained earnings an 
additional charge of depreciation relatable to the increase in value of assets arising from fair valuation, which amounts to Rs. 47 crore, Rs 46 crore, Rs 47 crore, Rs 93 crore, Rs 94 crore and Rs 188 
crore for the respective periods presented. 
Consequent to change in WBERC regulations relating to Advance Against Depreciation (AAD) with effect from 01 .04.2023, the net depreciation charge has been computed after necessary 
adjustments of AAD computed in terms of the Tariff regulations, as amended from time to time. 
5 (i) Other expenses includes interest on security deposit of Rs. 34 crore, Rs. 34 crore, Rs. 32 crore, Rs. 68 crore, Rs. 65 crore and Rs. 137 crore for the respective periods. 
(ii) EPS without Regulatory income/ (expense) (net) works out to Rs 1.78, Rs 1.56, Rs 1.57, Rs 3.35, Rs 2.68 and Rs 3.59 for the respective periods. 
6 The Company is primarily engaged in generation and distribution of electricity and does not operate in any other reportable segment. 
7 With regard to the Company's power purchase from one of its subsidiaries (provider), West Bengal Electricity Regulatory Commission (WBERC) has issued the tariff order (considering applicable 
Annual Performance Review (APR) orders for Generation and Transmission Project) for the years 2018-19 to 2025-26, wherein certain underlying matters have been dealt with in deviation from past 
practices of tariff determination and kept for disposal through future truing up exercise, impact of which is not ascertained. The said provider not being in agreement with the same, has since filed 
appeal in respect of the above Tariff Order before the Hon'ble Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) on the grounds interalia, that the orders have been passed after substantial period of delay, 
the applicable periods are long over and directions passed are impossible to comply because of significant delay in passing the said orders. However, since the Tariff Order from the financial year 
2022-23 onwards were issued during applicable financial years, the said provider has given effect to the same from 2022-23 onwards with application of principles in terms of applicable Regulations. 
With respect to APR orders of the said provider from WBERC for the years 2014-15 to 2022-23 including refund orders for the aforesaid APR Orders, the said provider not being in agreement with 
the same, has filed/in process of filing necessary appeals in the matter before the Hon'ble APTEL in respect of APR Orders and refund orders. Based on legal opinion obtained, the provider is 
confident of the matter being adjudicated in its favour. Accordingly, necessary adjustment, if any, will be made on the matter reaching finality.

Hexaware Selected as Strategic Technology Partner by 
the European Bank for Reconstruction and 
Development 
Five-year partnership to support the EBRD’s Technology Blueprint Northstar through AI and 
continuous improvement 
November 5, 2026: Hexaware Technologies [NSE: HEXT], a global AI-ﬁrst digital and IT solutions 
company, has been selected as strategic technology partner for the European Bank for 
Reconstruction and Development (EBRD). The ﬁve-year Strategic Partner Framework covers the 
Bank’s Run-Change-Transform technology portfolio. 
The EBRD’s Technology Blueprint focuses on driving efficiency, effectiveness and innovation 
through digitally enabled processes powered by AI, data, and intelligent automation. Hexaware 
will help embed AI into the Bank’s operations and establish a continuous improvement engine to 
identify optimization opportunities, automate processes, and drive increased efficiencies in our 
delivery model. The partnership focuses on measurable outcomes alongside ﬁxed capacity and 
resource augmentation delivery. 
Partnership Highlights 
• 
Technology services: Software engineering and quality assurance; IT operations and 
support; IT security, identity and access management; cloud, data, and analytics; SAP 
application support and modernization; treasury risk operations; and low-code, no-code, 
and AI-powered development 
• 
As part of the framework, Hexaware plan to deploy their AI frameworks: RapidX® for 
agentic software development lifecycle acceleration; Amaze® for AI-powered data 
engineering and modernization; Tensai® Reasoning Ops for intelligent operations and 
AIOps 
• 
Delivery model: Hexaware operating as an integrated part of the EBRD’s technology 
organization, supported by onshore and offshore delivery centers, with enterprise-grade 
AI deployment at scale. 
Simon Reeves, Director of Technology, EBRD, said, “The Strategic Parter Framework is about 
creating deeper partnerships that are aligned to outcomes yet constantly drive continuous 
improvement. We want our strategic partners operating as part of one team, no matter where they 
are based geographically. As an existing Partner, we’re pleased to strengthen and deepen our 
relationship with Hexaware and look forward to their innovation, capability and fresh thinking 
while helping us to deliver the objectives of our Tech Blueprint.”  
Subhash Jose, Managing Director for IT and Chief Information Officer, EBRD, said, “Our Tech 
Blueprint is about building a technology organisation that continuously improves, adapts and 
delivers greater value to the Bank. The Strategic Partner Framework plays an important role in that 

journey, helping us to combine strong engineering foundations with AI, automation and modern 
ways of working to improve how we deliver technology services.” 
Parameshwaran Iyer, EVP & Head, Europe, Hexaware, said, “This partnership is a signiﬁcant 
validation of our AI-native solution delivery model and our commitment to global development 
and stability. We intend to take this approach to other International Financial Institutions and 
Multi-lateral Development Banks to help them foster long-term economic growth across 
European nations” 
Parag Pawar, BFS Portfolio Head, Europe, Hexaware, said, “We’re excited to bring these 
capabilities to the EBRD and are committed to delivering sustained, measurable efficiency gains 
through intelligent automation, continuous improvement, and enterprise-grade, governance-
compliant AI deployment at scale.” 
About Hexaware 
Hexaware is a global technology and business process services company driven by a singular 
purpose: to create smiles through great people and technology. Our Zero Friction Enterprise™ 
approach combines AI innovation with human expertise to remove the technological and 
operational barriers that slow business progress. Globally, we help enterprises reduce 
complexity, accelerate transformation, and create lasting business value. 
Learn more about Hexaware at https://hexaware.com/ 
About the EBRD 
The EBRD is a multilateral bank that promotes the development of the private sector and 
entrepreneurial initiative in 40 economies across three continents. The Bank is owned by 77 
countries as well as the EU and the EIB. EBRD investments are aimed at making the economies 
in its regions competitive, inclusive, well governed, green, resilient and integrated. Follow us 
on the web, Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, X and YouTube. 
For details, please contact: 
Reena Kamble | Aishwarya Pillai 
mediarelations@hexaware.com 
Hexaware Technologies Limited

Simon Reeves, Director of Technology, EBRD, said, “The Strategic Parter Framework is about 
creating deeper partnerships that are aligned to outcomes yet constantly drive continuous 
improvement. We want our strategic partners operating as part of one team, no matter where they 
are based geographically. As an existing Partner, we’re pleased to strengthen and deepen our 
relationship with Hexaware and look forward to their innovation, capability and fresh thinking 
while helping us to deliver the objectives of our Tech Blueprint.”  
Subhash Jose, Managing Director for IT and Chief Information Officer, EBRD, said, “Our Tech 
Blueprint is about building a technology organisation that continuously improves, adapts and 
delivers greater value to the Bank. The Strategic Partner Framework plays an important role in that 

journey, helping us to combine strong engineering foundations with AI, automation and modern 
ways of working to improve how we deliver technology services.” 
Parameshwaran Iyer, EVP & Head, Europe, Hexaware, said, “This partnership is a signiﬁcant 
validation of our AI-native solution delivery model and our commitment to global development 
and stability. We intend to take this approach to other International Financial Institutions and 
Multi-lateral Development Banks to help them foster long-term economic growth across 
European nations” 
Parag Pawar, BFS Portfolio Head, Europe, Hexaware, said, “We’re excited to bring these 
capabilities to the EBRD and are committed to delivering sustained, measurable efficiency gains 
through intelligent automation, continuous improvement, and enterprise-grade, governance-
compliant AI deployment at scale.” 
About Hexaware 
Hexaware is a global technology and business process services company driven by a singular 
purpose: to create smiles through great people and technology. Our Zero Friction Enterprise™ 
approach combines AI innovation with human expertise to remove the technological and 
operational barriers that slow business progress. Globally, we help enterprises reduce 
complexity, accelerate transformation, and create lasting business value. 
Learn more about Hexaware at https://hexaware.com/ 
About the EBRD 
The EBRD is a multilateral bank that promotes the development of the private sector and 
entrepreneurial initiative in 40 economies across three continents. The Bank is owned by 77 
countries as well as the EU and the EIB. EBRD investments are aimed at making the economies 
in its regions competitive, inclusive, well governed, green, resilient and integrated. Follow us 
on the web, Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, X and YouTube. 
For details, please contact:

Emami delivers robust Q2FY27 performance with 36% 
revenue growth; Domestic Business surges 49% 
 
• 
Consolidated revenues grew 36% to ₹1,088 crore; like-to-like growth of 24% 
• 
Domestic Business grew 49% with volume growth of 43%;  
 Like-to-like domestic growth of 32% with volume growth of 26% 
• 
Strategic Investments portfolio grew 73% on a like-to-like basis  
 Contributed ~26% of domestic business in Q2FY27 
• 
EBITDA grew 25% to ₹222 crore and PBT grew 29% to ₹194 crore 
• 
Completed share buyback of ₹281.24 crore 
• 
Board approves first interim dividend of ₹5 per share 
 
Kolkata, 5th November, 2026 :   The Board of Directors of Emami Limited met on Thursday, 
5th November 2026 to consider the unaudited financial results of the Company for the 
second quarter and half year ended 30th September 2026. 
 
Building on the momentum of Q1, the Company delivered another quarter of broad-based 
double-digit growth, driven by the strong performance of both its core brands and 
Strategic Investments. The results reflect the Company's continued progress in building a 
more diversified and future-ready consumer products portfolio. The operating 
environment was not an easy one, marked by renewed geopolitical tensions in West Asia, 
floods in Nepal, persistent inflationary pressure across a range of commodities, and 
deficient rainfall in several parts of the country. Even so, demand conditions remained 
steady, and the Company’s diversified portfolio, sharper execution and the rapid scale-up 
of its new-age growth engines enabled it to deliver a strong set of numbers. 
 
On a consolidated basis, Revenue from Operations grew by 36% to ₹1,088 crore during 
Q2FY27. Domestic Business grew by 49%, driven by volume growth of 43%. On a like-to-
like basis, after considering the previous period’s numbers of Axiom Ayurveda and IncNut 
Digital, consolidated revenues grew by 24% and Domestic Business grew by 32%, with 
volume growth of 26%. 
 
Skin Care grew by 31%, led by the BoroPlus and Talc portfolios. Hair & Scalp Care grew by 
30%, with strong growth in Navratna Cool Oils and 7 Oils in One. Health Care grew by 11%, 
led by the Pain Management range. The Strategic Investments portfolio grew by 73% on 
a like-to-like basis and now contributes 26% of domestic business, reinforcing its role as 
an important growth engine and broadening the Company's presence across emerging 
consumer segments and categories. 
 
 

 
 
 
 
The quarter also witnessed a series of launches aimed at expanding the Company's 
consumer reach and strengthening its relevance across emerging needs and consumption 
occasions. The Company entered the baby care category with the “FromMaa” range under 
the BoroPlus brand, and introduced the Kesh King Scalp First range in modern trade and 
e-commerce. The Strategic Investments portfolio also launched several innovative, new-
age products during the quarter. 
 
The Company’s channel transformation continued at pace, reflecting its increasing 
alignment with evolving shopping behaviours and rapidly expanding digital and organised 
retail ecosystems. Organised channels contributed 37% of domestic business and Quick 
Commerce accounted for ~15% of total digital sales. 
 
Despite significant external disruptions across certain international markets, the 
underlying International Business remained resilient during Q2FY27. While reported 
revenues declined by 2%, the business grew 6% excluding Nepal and Iraq, supported by 
healthy momentum across key markets. The Company has implemented multiple 
mitigation measures across logistics, pricing and cost management to navigate the 
prevailing supply-chain challenges. With secondary sales trends improving and supply 
conditions gradually stabilizing, the Company expects the International Business growth 
trajectory to strengthen progressively in the coming quarters. 
 
On profitability, input costs remained elevated through the quarter; however, EBITDA 
grew by 25% to ₹222 crore and Profit Before Tax grew by 29% to ₹194 crore. Profit After 
Tax stood at ₹144 crore, lower by 3%, largely due to the normalisation of the effective tax 
rate following the phase-out of fiscal benefits. For the first half of FY27, revenues stood at 
₹2,127 crore, up 25%. EBITDA was ₹449 crore, up 14%, and Profit Before Tax was ₹388 
crore, up 15%. 
 
Mr Harsha V Agarwal, Vice Chairman and Managing Director, Emami Limited said: 
 
"We delivered another quarter of strong growth, with revenues increasing 36% and 
Domestic Business growing 49%. The strong performance of our core brands, coupled with 
the rapid scale-up of our Strategic Investments portfolio, which now contributes 
approximately 26% of domestic business, reinforces our strategy of building multiple 
growth engines for the future and expanding our presence across evolving consumer 
segments. As we continue to invest behind innovation, AI-enabled capabilities and new-
age consumer brands, we are creating a more diversified, agile and future-ready business. 
While inflationary and geopolitical headwinds persist, our robust portfolio, execution 
strength and productivity-led approach give us confidence of navigating these challenges 
effectively”.  
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
Mr Mohan Goenka, Vice Chairman and Whole-Time Director, Emami Limited said: 
 
"Despite elevated input costs, we delivered EBITDA growth of 25% to ₹222 crore through 
disciplined execution, calibrated pricing actions and sustained productivity improvements. 
Our continued focus on efficiencies across procurement, manufacturing, supply chain and 
revenue management is helping support healthy margins while enabling investments for 
future growth. Transformation initiatives such as Project SETU and SalesCode.AI are 
enhancing planning, execution and decision-making across the sales ecosystem, 
strengthening our operational agility and scalability. Reflecting our confidence in the 
business and commitment to shareholder value, we successfully completed a share 
buyback of over ₹281 crore and declared an interim dividend of ₹5 per share." 
 
 
 
About Emami Ltd 
Emami Limited (NSE: EMAMILTD, BSE: 531162), founded in 1974, is the flagship company of the Emami Group 
and one of India’s leading FMCG companies in the personal care and healthcare space. With a portfolio of over 
1000 products, Emami’s iconic brands include Navratna, BoroPlus, Zandu, Kesh King, Dermicool, Smart & 
Handsome, Mentho Plus, 7 Oils in One, Creme 21 among others. 
 
The Company has consistently strengthened and diversified its portfolio through strategic acquisitions and 
investments across high-growth consumer segments. In addition to acquisitions such as Zandu, Kesh King, Creme 
21 and Dermicool, Emami has strategically invested in a new generation of consumer brands, including The Man 
Company, Brillare, Alofrut and IncNut, which have since become subsidiaries of the Company. Other strategic 
investments include The Furball Story and TruNative, reflecting Emami’s focus on identifying and nurturing 
emerging consumer businesses. 
 
Emami’s products reach over 5.4 million retail outlets in India through a network of 4000+ distributors, while its 
international presence spans 70+ countries. Known for its strong consumer connect, innovative marketing and 
distinctive brand-building capabilities, Emami continues to leverage its deep consumer insights, brand-building 
expertise and strategic investment approach to create enduring brands and new avenues for growth in India 
and international markets.

Emami delivers robust Q2FY27 performance with 36% 
revenue growth; Domestic Business surges 49% 
 
• 
Consolidated revenues grew 36% to ₹1,088 crore; like-to-like growth of 24% 
• 
Domestic Business grew 49% with volume growth of 43%;  
 Like-to-like domestic growth of 32% with volume growth of 26% 
• 
Strategic Investments portfolio grew 73% on a like-to-like basis  
 Contributed ~26% of domestic business in Q2FY27 
• 
EBITDA grew 25% to ₹222 crore and PBT grew 29% to ₹194 crore 
• 
Completed share buyback of ₹281.24 crore 
• 
Board approves first interim dividend of ₹5 per share 
 
Kolkata, 5th November, 2026 :   The Board of Directors of Emami Limited met on Thursday, 
5th November 2026 to consider the unaudited financial results of the Company for the 
second quarter and half year ended 30th September 2026. 
 
Building on the momentum of Q1, the Company delivered another quarter of broad-based 
double-digit growth, driven by the strong performance of both its core brands and 
Strategic Investments. The results reflect the Company's continued progress in building a 
more diversified and future-ready consumer products portfolio. The operating 
environment was not an easy one, marked by renewed geopolitical tensions in West Asia, 
floods in Nepal, persistent inflationary pressure across a range of commodities, and 
deficient rainfall in several parts of the country. Even so, demand conditions remained 
steady, and the Company’s diversified portfolio, sharper execution and the rapid scale-up 
of its new-age growth engines enabled it to deliver a strong set of numbers. 
 
On a consolidated basis, Revenue from Operations grew by 36% to ₹1,088 crore during 
Q2FY27. Domestic Business grew by 49%, driven by volume growth of 43%. On a like-to-
like basis, after considering the previous period’s numbers of Axiom Ayurveda and IncNut 
Digital, consolidated revenues grew by 24% and Domestic Business grew by 32%, with 
volume growth of 26%. 
 
Skin Care grew by 31%, led by the BoroPlus and Talc portfolios. Hair & Scalp Care grew by 
30%, with strong growth in Navratna Cool Oils and 7 Oils in One. Health Care grew by 11%, 
led by the Pain Management range. The Strategic Investments portfolio grew by 73% on 
a like-to-like basis and now contributes 26% of domestic business, reinforcing its role as 
an important growth engine and broadening the Company's presence across emerging 
consumer segments and categories. 
 
 

 
 
 
 
The quarter also witnessed a series of launches aimed at expanding the Company's 
consumer reach and strengthening its relevance across emerging needs and consumption 
occasions. The Company entered the baby care category with the “FromMaa” range under 
the BoroPlus brand, and introduced the Kesh King Scalp First range in modern trade and 
e-commerce. The Strategic Investments portfolio also launched several innovative, new-
age products during the quarter. 
 
The Company’s channel transformation continued at pace, reflecting its increasing 
alignment with evolving shopping behaviours and rapidly expanding digital and organised 
retail ecosystems. Organised channels contributed 37% of domestic business and Quick 
Commerce accounted for ~15% of total digital sales. 
 
Despite significant external disruptions across certain international markets, the 
underlying International Business remained resilient during Q2FY27. While reported 
revenues declined by 2%, the business grew 6% excluding Nepal and Iraq, supported by 
healthy momentum across key markets. The Company has implemented multiple 
mitigation measures across logistics, pricing and cost management to navigate the 
prevailing supply-chain challenges. With secondary sales trends improving and supply 
conditions gradually stabilizing, the Company expects the International Business growth 
trajectory to strengthen progressively in the coming quarters. 
 
On profitability, input costs remained elevated through the quarter; however, EBITDA 
grew by 25% to ₹222 crore and Profit Before Tax grew by 29% to ₹194 crore. Profit After 
Tax stood at ₹144 crore, lower by 3%, largely due to the normalisation of the effective tax 
rate following the phase-out of fiscal benefits. For the first half of FY27, revenues stood at 
₹2,127 crore, up 25%. EBITDA was ₹449 crore, up 14%, and Profit Before Tax was ₹388 
crore, up 15%. 
 
Mr Harsha V Agarwal, Vice Chairman and Managing Director, Emami Limited said: 
 
"We delivered another quarter of strong growth, with revenues increasing 36% and 
Domestic Business growing 49%. The strong performance of our core brands, coupled with 
the rapid scale-up of our Strategic Investments portfolio, which now contributes 
approximately 26% of domestic business, reinforces our strategy of building multiple 
growth engines for the future and expanding our presence across evolving consumer 
segments. As we continue to invest behind innovation, AI-enabled capabilities and new-
age consumer brands, we are creating a more diversified, agile and future-ready business. 
While inflationary and geopolitical headwinds persist, our robust portfolio, execution 
strength and productivity-led approach give us confidence of navigating these challenges 
effectively”.  
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
Mr Mohan Goenka, Vice Chairman and Whole-Time Director, Emami Limited said: 
 
"Despite elevated input costs, we delivered EBITDA growth of 25% to ₹222 crore through 
disciplined execution, calibrated pricing actions and sustained productivity improvements. 
Our continued focus on efficiencies across procurement, manufacturing, supply chain and 
revenue management is helping support healthy margins while enabling investments for 
future growth. Transformation initiatives such as Project SETU and SalesCode.AI are 
enhancing planning, execution and decision-making across the sales ecosystem, 
strengthening our operational agility and scalability. Reflecting our confidence in the 
business and commitment to shareholder value, we successfully completed a share 
buyback of over ₹281 crore and declared an interim dividend of ₹5 per share." 
 
 
 
About Emami Ltd 
Emami Limited (NSE: EMAMILTD, BSE: 531162), founded in 1974, is the flagship company of the Emami Group 
and one of India’s leading FMCG companies in the personal care and healthcare space. With a portfolio of over 
1000 products, Emami’s iconic brands include Navratna, BoroPlus, Zandu, Kesh King, Dermicool, Smart & 
Handsome, Mentho Plus, 7 Oils in One, Creme 21 among others. 
 
The Company has consistently strengthened and diversified its portfolio through strategic acquisitions and 
investments across high-growth consumer segments. In addition to acquisitions such as Zandu, Kesh King, Creme 
21 and Dermicool, Emami has strategically invested in a new generation of consumer brands, including The Man 
Company, Brillare, Alofrut and IncNut, which have since become subsidiaries of the Company. Other strategic 
investments include The Furball Story and TruNative, reflecting Emami’s focus on identifying and nurturing 
emerging consumer businesses. 
 
Emami’s products reach over 5.4 million retail outlets in India through a network of 4000+ distributors, while its 
international presence spans 70+ countries. Known for its strong consumer connect, innovative marketing and 
distinctive brand-building capabilities, Emami continues to leverage its deep consumer insights, brand-building 
expertise and strategic investment approach to create enduring brands and new avenues for growth in India 
and international markets.

Sub: Outcome of Board Meeting held on 5th November, 2026 
Dear Sir/ Madam, 
In furtherance to our intimation dated 24th October, 2026, and pursuant to Regulation 30 and 
other applicable regulations (if any) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘Listing Regulations’), this is to inform you that the Board of 
Directors of the Company, at its meeting held today, i.e, 5th November, 2026, has inter-alia: 
1. considered and approved the Unaudited Financial Results (Standalone & Consolidated)
for the quarter and half-year ended 30th September, 2026. In this regard, pursuant to
Regulation 33 of the Listing Regulations, we are enclosing herewith the Unaudited
Financial Results (Standalone & Consolidated) of the Company, for the quarter and half-
year ended 30th September, 2026, along with the Limited Review Report, issued by the
Statutory Auditors of the Company – marked as Annexure - A;
The full format of the aforesaid results is annexed herewith for making the same available
on the website of the Stock Exchanges. The results are also available on the Company’s
website at www.emamiltd.in.
2. declared and approved the payment of 1st Interim Dividend of Rs. 5/- per equity share
having face value of Re. 1/- each fully paid up i.e. 500% on 42,92,00,000 equity shares
of the Company for the financial year 2026-27. The interim dividend will be paid on or
before 4th December, 2026.
Record date for ascertaining the name of the members / beneficial owners who will be
entitled to receive the Interim Dividend is Friday, 13th November, 2026.

 
 
 
 
3. considered and approved the appointment of Shri Debendra Banthiya, qualified Company 
Secretary (ICSI Membership No – F7790), as the Company Secretary & Compliance 
Officer of the Company with effect from 5th November, 2026. The details required as per 
Regulation 30 of the Listing Regulations, and SEBI Master Circular No. 
HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFDPOD2/I/3762/2026 dated January 30, 2026, are enclosed and 
marked as Annexure – B; 
 
Further, Shri Debendra Banthiya has also been appointed as the Nodal Officer of the 
Company, in compliance with Rule 7 (2A) of Investor Education and Protection Fund 
Authority (Accounting, Audit, Transfer and Refund) Rules, 2016. 
 
The Board meeting commenced at 12:00 Noon and concluded at 1:35 P.M. 
The aforesaid information will also be available on the Company’s website at www.emamiltd.in.  
This is for your information and record. 
Thanking you, 
Yours faithfully, 
For Emami Limited 
 
 
 
N.H. Bhansali 
CEO- Finance, Strategy & Business Development and CFO

1.
We have reviewed the accompanying Statement of Unaudited Consolidated Financial
Results of Emami Limited (the “Holding Company”) and its subsidiaries (the Holding
Company and its subsidiaries together referred to as “the Group”) and its associates for
the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and year to date from April 01, 2026 to
September 30, 2026 (the “Statement”) attached herewith, being submitted by the Holding
Company pursuant to the requirements of Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended (the “Listing
Regulations”).
2.
The Holding Company’s Management is responsible for the preparation of the Statement
in accordance with the recognition and measurement principles laid down in Indian
Accounting Standard 34, (Ind AS 34) “Interim Financial Reporting” prescribed under
Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 as amended, read with relevant rules issued
thereunder and other accounting principles generally accepted in India and in
compliance with Regulation 33 of the Listing Regulations. The Statement has been
approved by the Holding Company’s Board of Directors. Our responsibility is to express
a conclusion on the Statement based on our review.
3.
We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review
Engagements (SRE) 2410, “Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the
Independent Auditor of the Entity” issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of
India. This standard requires that we plan and perform the review to obtain moderate
assurance as to whether the Statement is free of material misstatement. A review of
interim financial information consists of making inquiries, primarily of persons
responsible for financial and accounting matters, and applying analytical and other
review procedures. A review is substantially less in scope than an audit conducted in
accordance with Standards on Auditing and consequently does not enable us to obtain
assurance that we would become aware of all significant matters that might be identified
in an audit. Accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion.
We also performed procedures in accordance with the Master Circular issued by the Securities 
and Exchange Board of India under Regulation 33(8) of the Listing Regulations, to the extent 
applicable except with respect to one (1) subsidiary (including their two (2) subsidiaries), for 
Annexure - A

Basis for Qualified Conclusion 
 
5. 
As disclosed in the note 3(a) to the Statement, the accompanying Statement of unaudited 
consolidated financial results include unaudited interim financial results and other 
unaudited financial information in respect of Consolidated financial results of One (1) 
subsidiary (including its two (2) subsidiaries), whose interim financial information/ 
financial results reflect total revenues of Rs. 8,357 lacs, total net profit after tax of Rs. 
941 lacs and total comprehensive income of Rs. 946 lacs for the quarter ended 
September 30, 2026, as considered in the Statement, which have not been reviewed by 
any auditor. 
 
These unaudited interim financial results and other unaudited financial information have been 
approved and furnished to us by the management and our conclusion on the Statement, in so 
far as it relates to the affairs of these subsidiaries, is based solely on such unaudited interim 
financial results and other unaudited financial information. Accordingly, we are unable to 
comment on the financial impact, if any, on the Statement, if the same had been reviewed. 
 
Our review report for quarter June 30, 2026, was also qualified in connection with certain 
unreviewed components. 
 
Qualified Conclusion 
 
6. 
Based on our review conducted and procedures performed as stated in paragraph 3 
above and based on the consideration of the review reports of other auditors referred to 
in paragraph 7 below, except for the possible effects of our observations in para 5 above, 
nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe that the accompanying 
Statement, prepared in accordance with recognition and measurement principles laid 
down in the aforesaid Indian Accounting Standards (‘Ind AS’) specified under Section 
133 of the Companies Act, 2013, as amended, read with relevant rules issued thereunder 
and other accounting principles generally accepted in India, has not disclosed the 
information required to be disclosed in terms of the Listing Regulations, including the 
manner in which it is to be disclosed, or that it contains any material misstatement. 
 
7. 
The accompanying Statement includes the unaudited interim financial results and other 
financial information, in respect of: 
 
• 
Three (3) subsidiaries, whose unaudited interim financial results include total 
assets of Rs. 18,580 lacs as at September 30, 2026, total revenues of Rs. 8,414 
lacs and Rs. 14,401 lacs, total net profit/(loss) after tax of Rs. 563 lacs and Rs.

(439 lacs) and total comprehensive income/(loss) of Rs. 448 lacs and Rs. (440 
lacs), for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and the period ended on that date 
respectively and net cash inflows of Rs. 97 lacs for the period from April 01, 2026 
to September 30, 2026, as considered in the Statement which have been reviewed 
by their respective independent auditors. 
 
• 
Consolidated financial results in respect on One (1) subsidiary (including its Six (6) 
subsidiaries), whose unaudited interim financial results include total assets of  
Rs. 25,678 lacs as at September 30, 2026, total revenues of Rs. 11,540 lacs and  
Rs. 19,872 lacs, total net profit after tax of Rs. 1,130 lacs and Rs. 1,622 lacs and 
total comprehensive income of Rs. 909 lacs and Rs. 1,533 lacs, for the quarter 
ended September 30, 2026 and the period ended on that date respectively and net 
cash outflow of Rs. 189 lacs for the period from April 01, 2026 to September 30, 
2026, as considered in the Statement which have been reviewed by their 
independent auditor. 
 
• 
Consolidated financial results of One (1) subsidiary (including its one (1) 
subsidiary), whose interim financial information/ financial results reflect total assets 
of Rs. 9,985 lacs as at September 30, 2026, total revenues of Rs. 6,599 lacs and 
Rs. 8,068 lacs, total net loss after tax of Rs. 360 lacs and Rs. 452 lacs and total 
comprehensive loss of Rs. 399 lacs and Rs. 491 lacs, for the quarter ended 
September 30, 2026 and for the period from June 01, 2026 to September 30, 2026 
respectively and net cash inflow of Rs. 17 lacs for the period from June 01, 2026 
to September 30, 2026, as considered in the Statement, which have been reviewed 
by their independent auditor. 
 
The independent auditor’s reports on interim financial information/ financial results of these 
entities have been furnished to us by the Management and our conclusion on the Statement, 
in so far as it relates to the amounts and disclosures in respect of these subsidiaries is based 
solely on the report of such auditors and procedures performed by us as stated in paragraph 
3 above. 
 
8. 
The accompanying Statement includes unaudited interim financial results and other 
unaudited financial information in respect of two (2) associates, whose interim financial 
information/financial results includes the Group’s share of net loss of Rs. 34 lacs and Rs. 
189 lacs and Group’s share of total comprehensive loss of Rs. 34 lacs and Rs. 189 lacs 
for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and for the period ended on that date 
respectively.  
 

 
 
Chartered Accountants  
The unaudited interim financial information/ financial results and other unaudited 
financial information of the these associates have not been reviewed by any auditors and 
have been approved and furnished to us by the Management and our conclusion on the 
Statement, in so far as it relates to the affairs of these associates, is based solely on 
such unaudited interim financial results and other unaudited financial information. 
According to the information and explanations given to us by the Management, these 
interim financial information/financial results are not material to the Group. 
 
Our conclusion on the Statement in respect of matters stated in para 7 and 8 above is not 
modified with respect to our reliance on the work done and the reports of the other auditors 
and the financial results/financial information certified by the Management.

Sub: Outcome of Board Meeting held on 5th November, 2026 
Dear Sir/ Madam, 
In furtherance to our intimation dated 24th October, 2026, and pursuant to Regulation 30 and 
other applicable regulations (if any) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘Listing Regulations’), this is to inform you that the Board of 
Directors of the Company, at its meeting held today, i.e, 5th November, 2026, has inter-alia: 
1. considered and approved the Unaudited Financial Results (Standalone & Consolidated)
for the quarter and half-year ended 30th September, 2026. In this regard, pursuant to
Regulation 33 of the Listing Regulations, we are enclosing herewith the Unaudited
Financial Results (Standalone & Consolidated) of the Company, for the quarter and half-
year ended 30th September, 2026, along with the Limited Review Report, issued by the
Statutory Auditors of the Company – marked as Annexure - A;
The full format of the aforesaid results is annexed herewith for making the same available
on the website of the Stock Exchanges. The results are also available on the Company’s
website at www.emamiltd.in.
2. declared and approved the payment of 1st Interim Dividend of Rs. 5/- per equity share
having face value of Re. 1/- each fully paid up i.e. 500% on 42,92,00,000 equity shares
of the Company for the financial year 2026-27. The interim dividend will be paid on or
before 4th December, 2026.
Record date for ascertaining the name of the members / beneficial owners who will be
entitled to receive the Interim Dividend is Friday, 13th November, 2026.

 
 
 
 
3. considered and approved the appointment of Shri Debendra Banthiya, qualified Company 
Secretary (ICSI Membership No – F7790), as the Company Secretary & Compliance 
Officer of the Company with effect from 5th November, 2026. The details required as per 
Regulation 30 of the Listing Regulations, and SEBI Master Circular No. 
HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFDPOD2/I/3762/2026 dated January 30, 2026, are enclosed and 
marked as Annexure – B; 
 
Further, Shri Debendra Banthiya has also been appointed as the Nodal Officer of the 
Company, in compliance with Rule 7 (2A) of Investor Education and Protection Fund 
Authority (Accounting, Audit, Transfer and Refund) Rules, 2016. 
 
The Board meeting commenced at 12:00 Noon and concluded at 1:35 P.M. 
The aforesaid information will also be available on the Company’s website at www.emamiltd.in.  
This is for your information and record. 
Thanking you, 
Yours faithfully, 
For Emami Limited
