Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to Sky Gold & Diamonds Limited Q2 and H1 
FY27 Earnings Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only 
mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. 
Should you need assistance during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing 
star, then zero on your touchtone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Ms. Vidhi Vasa from MUFG Intime. Thank you, and over to 
you, ma'am. 
Vidhi Vasa: 
Thank you, Huda. On behalf of MUFG Intime, I welcome you all to Sky Gold & Diamonds 
Limited Q2 and H1 FY27 earnings conference call. On the management side, we have Mr. 
Mangesh Chauhan, Managing Director; Mr. Darshan Chauhan, Whole-Time Director; Mr. 
Mahendra Chauhan, Whole-Time Director; and Mr. Siddharth Sipani, Chief Financial Officer. 
 
I hope everybody had an opportunity to go through our investor deck that we have uploaded on 
exchange and the company's website. I would like to mention a short disclaimer before we begin 
the call. This call may contain some of the forward-looking statements which are completely 
based upon our beliefs, opinion, and expectations as of today. These statements are not a 
guarantee of our future performance and involve unforeseen risks and uncertainties. 
 
With this, now I hand over the call to Mr. Mangesh Chauhan. Over to you, sir. 
Mangesh Chauhan: 
Good morning, everybody. I would like to start this con-call with Darshan Chauhan, Whole-
Time Director of Sky Gold & Diamonds. 
Darshan Chauhan: 
Thank you, Mangesh Bhai. Good morning, everyone. Let me begin by thanking my team. Today, 
I want to go beyond the quarter. I want to tell you how Sky Gold was built, where we started, 
why India's reputed retailers choose to work with us, and how we have used every rupee of 
capital you have trusted us with. I also want to explain why we believe this is one of the most 
capital-efficient businesses in our industry. 
 
One note before I begin: Under SEBI guidelines, we are not supposed to give forward-looking 
guidance. That is one of the reasons you have not seen future guidance in our latest quarter 
presentation. Today, I will speak only about what we have built and what we have delivered. 
 
Sky Gold started with a simple goal, build a solid product portfolio and earn the trust of our 
customers. We saw early that jewelry retail was moving from unorganized to organized, and that 
bet paid off. Today, the same shift is happening in jewelry manufacturing. 
 
Our roots are in South Indian design, where we have built expertise over two decades. When we 
listed in 2018, we were a small company with a design team of 15 to 20 CAD designers. But 
even then, we promoters had one ambition: to become India's number one jewelry manufacturer. 
The ambition has grown since. Our vision is to build a global design-led jewelry manufacturing 
business that is asset-light. 
 
Why do retailers come to Sky Gold? Why do the highly reputed retailers choose us? There are 
four reasons: First, we specialize in lightweight jewelry. As gold prices rise, customers want 

 
 
Sky Gold & Diamonds Limited 
 
 
October 31, 2026 
Page 3 of 3 
 
lighter pieces. We adopted 3D printing with paper casting as early as 2020, and now run 40 such 
machines. Together with direct casting, laser cutting, hollow stamping, this makes our jewelry 
20% to 30% lighter. We have also cut gold loss from 1.5% to 0.5%. 
 
Second, we don't just make jewelry, we co-create it. Our design team of around 180 people 
studies each retailer's portfolio and its competitors. We study what each state and each 
community wants. Our team brings sketches, prototypes, and samples before anything goes into 
production. That approach gives us one of the best selection rates in the industry, and keeps 
unsold inventory low for our customers. It is also why value-added products now make up over 
half our revenue, from insignificant percentage three years ago. 
Third, we execute. In our industry, execution means two things. Timely delivery and sharper 
delivery with strict quality control. We deliver in less than 30 days, significantly faster delivery 
timeline for the complex products that we are selling. When our products arrive on time and sell 
well in the store, the repeat orders come quickly.  
Fourth, we are one-stop shop. A retailer who buys gold jewelry from us can now buy diamond 
jewelry, chains, bangles, diamond-studded jewelry and uncut jewelry from the same partner. 
Behind that sits a large back office team that handles customization, custom orders, and after-
sales service. Our customers can focus on retail, we take care of the rest. We are always one call 
away.  
Over the last eight years, we have invested in three things at once: design, technology and people. 
On design, we grew from 15 to 20 CAD designers to a team of around 180. We hired talent that 
understood the gaps in the market and needs of each region. On technology, we have adopted 
first-hand technology, but a machine is only as good as the person running it. A doctorate in 
material science with over three decades of experience oversees these operations.  
On people, we built a marketing team to take us from South Indian business to pan-India one. 
We hired professionals with 20 years of experience and deep relationships in the trade. In the 
past, we had highlighted about the expansion in management bandwidth after appointing a 
professional CEO, business heads and CFO. Also, the presence of Thiru, who has three decades 
of manufacturing experience.  
In addition, he has spent close to a decade at one of the most reputed jewelry conglomerates. To 
keep this talent, we made ESOPs a part of how we reward performance. We recently honored 
employees who have been with us for more than five years as they were the backbone of our 
growth journey.  
Now let me take you through on how we have used your capital. Our capital raising history tells 
a simple story. Each time we have raised capital, we have deployed it with discipline and 
converted it into a step change in scale. We listed on BSE SME platform in October 2018, raising 
INR25.56 crores at INR180 per share. At the time, we had just crossed INR500 crores in 
turnover.  
The IPO gave us the platform, governance standard and visibility of a listed company, and the 
capital to strengthen working capital. We use that platform to build our design team and a pan-

 
 
Sky Gold & Diamonds Limited 
 
 
October 31, 2026 
Page 4 of 4 
 
India marketing team. Over the following years, we compounded steadily, growing turnover 
from more than threefold to INR1,745 crores by FY24.  
In 2023, we moved to the main board of NSE and BSE. In late 2023, we raised INR128 crores 
through a preferential issue of shares and warrants. Notably, promoters participated through 
warrants alongside notable investors, a clear signal of conviction from within. This capital 
allowed us to bring in senior professionals launch our ESOP program, scale our Diamond 
division and build exports. Its impact was immediate. Revenue doubled in a single year from 
INR1,745 crores in FY24 to INR3,548 crores in FY25.  
In October 2024, we completed a QIP of INR270 crores. When our revenue stood at INR3,548 
crores for FY25. During Q2 FY26, we opened our international office in Dubai. We have also 
added new categories through acquisitions. Today, we are running at an annualized revenue of 
INR9,000 crores plus.  
Put simply, across these two funds raised post our IPO, we have taken in about INR398 crores 
of equity. Over the same period, revenue has grown from INR500 crores to INR9,000 crores 
plus, roughly 18x. For most of our early history, we were a South India business. Our vision to 
be India's number one manufacturer meant we had to serve every region, so we built dedicated 
teams for North, East and West and studied what each market and culture wants to wear.  
We also chose our partners well. Our customers include several of India's large listed and 
unlisted jewelry retailers. Of our customers, Kalyan, Senco, and PN Gadgil listed on stock 
exchanges in recent years and opened showrooms rapidly. Because we were already trusted in 
their existing stores, we grew with them as well. That is the organised retail back paying off. As 
the leading retailers grew, the manufacturer who executes best for them grows with them.  
Now, let me take you through our export story. In FY23, our annual exports were only about 
INR35 crores. In Q2 FY27, we have reached exports of INR435 crores. I repeat it FY23 as a 
whole we did INR35 crores of exports, while in current quarter alone we have achieved INR435 
crores.  
Today, exports are roughly 18% of our business, around INR1,600 crores plus on annualized 
basis. This growth of 45x came in three steps.  
Step number one, our Indian customers took us abroad. After COVID, the same corporates we 
served in India asked us to supply their international stores. Our products had already proven 
themselves in India. So they perform well abroad too.  
Step number two, we went where the Indian diaspora lives. In Singapore and Malaysia have 
large South Indian communities and South Indian design is our core strength. We began 
supplying reputed retailers in Singapore and in Malaysia. Within about a year, we were working 
with majority of reputed corporates across GCC.  
Step number three, we planted a flag in Dubai. In September 2025, we started operations of our 
international office in Dubai, led by Mr. Hiralal, who brings 30 plus years of experience in Dubai 
and GCC. Almost every major retailer we worked with came in the opening of our Dubai office.  

 
 
Sky Gold & Diamonds Limited 
 
 
October 31, 2026 
Page 5 of 5 
 
From Dubai, we now serve wholesalers and corporates across GCC region. Our on-boarding 
into Middle East most respected jewelry retailer shows how we win. We are amongst jewelry 
manufacturers who design for Arab clientele as well. Our merchandising team studied the look 
and feel that market wants, and we co-created a gold line with our customer. It was accepted 
first time right and the orders followed.  
We then did the same with other regional international players as well. Hence, reputed regional 
jewelry chains of UAE, each with 15 to 20 showrooms in Dubai, are now our customers. What 
keep our customers are our services. Our Dubai office acts as a one-stop shop available around 
the clock. Behind it sits a dedicated back office team in India. Supporting each customer from 
design to dispatch, and these relationships are personal. I traveled to Dubai regularly in the early 
days, and I still sit with the owners to understand their customer and their timelines.  
Trade shows have helped widen our reach:  
Dubai held around our office inauguration introduced us to buyers from Bahrain, Sri Lanka, 
Malaysia and Singapore.  
Saudi Arabia, where we built a 21-karat line especially for that market before the show.  
United Kingdom, our first show there gave us a good response. One new client started with an 
initial order of 30 kg.  
Malaysia, where we had the largest booth and were the only exhibitor showing gold, diamond 
and other categories together.  
Singapore, which brought a strong response for our diamond jewelry.  
We have also begun working with the customer in Japan whose distribution reaches Hong Kong 
and the US.  
Now let me get into categories. Every new category we add follows the same logic: sell more to 
customers who already trust us.  
Diamond, we started our diamond business two years ago, small and still learning. We then built 
a platform around experienced merchandisers led by Akash, who has more than 22 years in 
diamond jewelry for India and exports market.  
Our edge in diamond comes from being a gold company first. Gold manufacturers lead on 
technology such as laser cutting, electroforming. We brought that technology into diamond 
jewelry. To make lightweight pieces with right balance of gold and diamond, which matters 
more as gold prices rise.  
We began with lightweight every day wear and then moved into bridal. Because temple jewelry 
is our strength of ours, we now make it in diamond in open, closed and combined settings. Closed 
setting is in high demand in South, yet only limited manufacturers have the skill. We built our 

 
 
Sky Gold & Diamonds Limited 
 
 
October 31, 2026 
Page 6 of 6 
 
capabilities by hiring setting experts from the South. We also use niche materials such as ceramic 
and Italian findings and launch 30 to 40 theme-based diamond collections every quarter.  
Diamond carries a higher margin than the company average, and sequentially we have doubled 
its contribution.  
Mangalsutra and uncut diamond, we have added this through acquisitions, which I will come to 
next. The result is the blend we set out to build: an advanced metal business where ROIC is 
effectively infinite, a diamond business with high margins and a value-added gold business that 
now makes up significant part of our revenues.  
Acquisitions: Our acquisitions follow one rule; we do not buy a company alone. We buy its 
management, its expertise, its designs and its customer relationship. In every case, the founders 
have joined our top management because their long-standing jewelry experience is what we are 
really acquiring. Each acquisition does two jobs. It adds a category we can sell to our existing 
top customers and it gives the acquired business access to our design library, our technology, 
and our customer base.  
Starmangalsutra and Rishabh Gold: Mangalsutra is largely handmade and needs real precision. 
Through Starmangalsutra, we already sold mangalsutra to major corporates. Shri. Rishabh Gold 
bought one of the robust mangalsutra manufacturing teams in the country and jewelry 
conglomerates as their customers.  
The partnership works both ways. As a casting company, our cast elements and design library 
let them diversify their mangalsutra range sharply. Their monthly volumes have grown from 
about 20 kg to 25 kg to 150 kg. One of the trusted conglomerates alone now takes 70 kg to 80 
kg of mangalsutra and the relationships have opened doors for our other jewelry categories as 
well. Together, we are today one of India's most trusted mangalsutra manufacturers.  
Purvi Gems: Uncut diamonds, uncut diamond jewelry is in strong demand and carries high 
margins. There are only few Indian manufacturers have the expertise of this product segment. 
We saw that demand from our customers constantly. Purvi was already supplying to reputed 
retailers and its management has around 20 years of experience in this category.  
With our design strength and wider customer relationship, adding this category was a natural 
step. Every acquisition moves us closer to one goal. We have created a perfect ecosystem to 
make our company as a one-stop shop for all the jewelry requirements. Our design work is now 
recognized beyond our customers. The World Gold Council selected many of our products for 
its campaigns, including last year's major push on 24-karat jewelry.  
Today, when the retailers ask the World Gold Council for certain product lines, Sky Gold is 
often the preferred name it suggests. With De Beers, we have co-created collections and are 
giving dedicated space to showcase our products at their exhibitions.  
Capital efficiency and returns. Everything we have described has been guided by a focus on 
improving capital efficiency and returns on capital employed.  

 
 
Sky Gold & Diamonds Limited 
 
 
October 31, 2026 
Page 7 of 7 
 
Our Advance Gold Model is an important part of this strategy. Under this model, customers 
procure and provide the gold, while our revenue reflects the manufacturing work performed by 
us. This reduces our requirement for capital investment and eliminates the need to hold inventory 
or manage receivables in respect of the gold supplied by customers.  
Exports are another important contributor to capital efficiency given their shorter receivable 
cycles. Our earlier disclosures have noted that export receivable days are much less than 
domestic receivables. In H1 FY27, exports contributed to INR811 crores of our revenues. The 
increasing contribution from Advance Gold and exports is expected to moderate the working 
capital intensity of our business.  
We are also focused on improving manufacturing efficiency through technology and process 
improvements. The adoption of direct casting, 3D printing, laser technology, holo stamping has 
enabled us to improve the finish of our jewelry and reduce its weight by approximately 20% to 
30%.  
In addition, our efforts to improve manufacturing efficiency have reduced gold loss significantly. 
Our co-creation and merchandising capabilities also help improve inventory productivity by 
working closely with retailers to develop designs based on consumer preferences. We have 
helped reduce unsold inventory and improve inventory productivity for our retail partners.  
Going forward, our focus remains on increasing the contribution of Advance Gold exports and 
higher margin value-added products including studded and diamond jewelry. While Advance 
Gold and exports support capital efficiency through lower working capital requirement, value-
added and diamond jewelry provides opportunities to improve margin and returns on capital. 
The proof is in the numbers, roughly INR398 crores of equity raised over eight years now 
supports an annualized revenue base of INR9,000 plus crores.  
In past, we have said that Sky Gold growth would be funded entirely by internal cash generation. 
We welcome the scrutiny of our business face on operating cash flow. We had earlier guided for 
INR18,000 crores revenue by FY2030, INR945 crores of PAT, 20% to 25% of PAT converted 
into operating cash flow, and a net debt-free balance sheet by 2030.  
In Q2 FY27, we exited with an annualized revenue of INR9,000 crores plus, an annualized PAT 
of more than INR500 crores. We converted 33% of TTM PAT into operating cash flow. In fact, 
if we factor in the land sale we guided for earlier, net debt in first half FY27 is down 20% from 
FY26 level. We have a consistent record of setting clear targets and beating them.  
Our original growth roadmap reflected our confidence in business long-term potential. And 
quarter after quarter, we have delivered ahead of plan. Most tellingly, we have raised our long-
term targets several times while continuing to outperform them. That is the result of rigorous 
planning and disciplined execution.  
I know many of you have questions about the fundraise we announced recently. In line with the 
regulatory guidelines, I am not allowed to speak about its specific purpose or the use of proceeds. 
What I can do is share you how we as a management team think about the growth and capital.  

 
 
Sky Gold & Diamonds Limited 
 
 
October 31, 2026 
Page 8 of 8 
 
As a management, we believe we should grow along with our customers and not give up market 
share. Importantly, our customers are working to consolidate their supplier base. They want to 
work with fewer larger, established, well-capitalized, professionally run and compliant jewelry 
manufacturers. It was our customers' requirement that gave us the confidence in 2024 to grow 
organically and expand our capacity.  
In the past, our customers have also played an important role in guiding our inorganic growth. 
Our industry has a number of jewelry manufacturers with strong vintage and strength in certain 
product categories. Many of them are struggling with working capital, the compliance burden 
and succession. Several of our historic acquisitions were guided by customers who believe we 
are the logical and preferred acquirer of these companies.  
We have track record of good acquisitions and we have handled post-merger integration well in 
every acquisition so far. We have a cultural familiarity with the companies we acquire, but we 
succeed largely because we have a close relationship with the end customer the jewellery retailer.  
Let me give you some historic examples of companies we have acquired at attractive valuations 
and how we have grown their revenue and profit after acquisition.  
Shri. Rishabh Gold (Mangalsutra) acquired at less than INR10 crores. Monthly volumes have 
grown from about 20 kg to 25 kg to around 150 kg and revenue from INR49 crores to INR175 
crores, with the profit from INR1.6 crores to INR18.8 crores. We are now one of India's reputed 
mangalsutra manufacturers.  
Purvi Gold (Uncut Diamonds) acquired at INR9 crores versus book value of INR6 crores. We 
can use Sky's design team and wider customer relationship as well.  
Following our customer has never let us down. At home, when Kalyan, Senco and PN Gadgil 
listed and expanded rapidly, we grew with them into every new store. When Shri. Rishabh Gold 
joined us, largest conglomerate, become a major customer, and that relationship is now opening 
doors for our other categories.  
Abroad, the story is the same. Our exports began because Indian large jewelry retailers have 
asked us to supply to their stores overseas. That gave us credibility in Singapore and Malaysia, 
then the confidence to open our Dubai office, and then we added reputed regional players in 
UAE. Exports have grown from about INR35 crores plus a year in FY23 to roughly 18% of our 
business today.  
I repeat, FY23 as a whole we did INR35 crores of export, while in current quarter alone we have 
achieved INR435 crores. This is around INR1,600 crores on annualized basis. In each case, we 
invested ahead of the order because our customer told us where they were going and in each 
case the returns followed. This is a high-return business model, and our quarterly result shows 
it.  
Nearly 16% of our volume comes from advanced metal, which employs no capital of ours. 
Together with exports, which carry short receivable cycles, these segments make up more than 

 
 
Sky Gold & Diamonds Limited 
 
 
October 31, 2026 
Page 9 of 9 
 
35% of our volume. In first half FY27, we delivered an annualized PAT run rate of more than 
INR500 crores and our net debt is also down versus FY26 levels.  
The right test for any growth investment is simple, does each rupee we invest earn more than its 
cost of capital? If it does, investing it creates value. Even if free cash flow is lower in the near-
term, what matters is the spread between ROIC and cost of capital and how long we can sustain 
it.  
Consider Walmart between 1973 and 1986, the years it was building out its store network. It had 
negative free cash flow in every one of those 14 years, yet its ROC averaged 18%, well above 
its cost of capital, and its stock returned 33% a year, about 3x the S&P 500. Walmart was not 
burning cash, it was putting every dollar it could to work at high returns while the opportunity 
was in front of it.  
We see real parallels with Sky Gold. Like Walmart then, we are early in structural shift, in our 
case from unorganized to organized jewelry manufacturing. Like Walmart, our growth follows 
a clear demand signal: our customers are consolidating their suppliers and asking us to grow 
with them. And like Walmart, we earn returns well above our cost of capital, helped by advance 
metal, which needs no capital of ours, and exports, which pay quickly. 
So, the real question is not whether cash flow dips while we invest, it is whether every rupee we 
put to work earn well above its cost of capital and deepens our relationship with customers. Our 
record says it does. From 2018 IPO to the 2024 QIP, each round of capital was followed by a 
step change in scale. A business that can reinvest at these returns should do so, even if it means 
giving up some cash flow today, the benefits play out over the long term. 
Why the cash flow will come? Our fundamentals give us every reason for confidence. Our 
founders are in the mid-40s with decades of building ahead of them. Our market is expanding as 
the manufacturing shifts from unorganized to organized, and our unit economics are extremely 
solid. When growth runs in line with returns on capital, a business like ours will generate strong 
cash flow. We remain focused on one measure above all, earning well above our cost of capital 
on every rupee we invest. 
Let me bring it together, we started as a South Indian gold jewellery manufacturer with a small 
design team and one big ambition. Today, we serve India's reputed retailers in every region, 
supply the Gulf and the Far East from our own Dubai office, and offer gold, diamond, 
mangalsutra, and uncut jewellery, all under one roof. We got here by investing in design, 
technology, and people; by growing with our customers and by putting every rupee of capital to 
work. That discipline is not going to change. 
As I said at the start, in line with the SEBI guidelines, we no longer give forward guidance, and 
you will not find it in our presentation. We would rather let our record speak, we set clear targets, 
we beat them, and we raise them several times over. Thank you. Before we take your questions, 
Mahendra Bhai, the eldest of our brothers, would like to say a few words. Thank you very much.

Hello everyone, this is Mahendra Chauhan. I am the eldest of the brothers. As most of you know, 
I rarely join these calls, but this is an important occasion and I would like to say a few words.

mid-40s with tremendous energy, passion, and a deep personal commitment to the business. For 
us, this is not just a business we have built, it is something we have nurtured with years of hard

As you heard earlier, acquisitions have been an important part of our growth. They have helped

Schneider Electric Infrastructure Ltd (SEIL) is a part of Schneider Electric Group 
 
Gurugram, Haryana – 05th November 2026 – Schneider Electric Infrastructure Limited (SEIL/Company), 
a part of Schneider Electric Group, a global energy technology leader, announced its financial results for the 
second quarter and half year of 2026-27, ended 30th September 2026. 
 
SEIL recorded its highest-ever quarterly order intake of INR 1,265 crores in Q2’FY27, ahead of the previous 
high of INR 915 crores in Q1’FY27. Demand remained strong across the established segments and the 
emerging ones, such as data centres and semiconductors. For H1’FY27, order intake was INR 2,180 crores, 
up 24.7% year-on-year. The order backlog stood at INR 2,701 crores as of 30th September 2026, up 49.6% 
year-on-year, which gives the Company healthy sales visibility. 
 
Sales for Q2’FY27 was INR 779 crores, up 19.8% year-on-year and 19.6% over Q1’FY27. The conversion of 
order wins into sales is progressing well, and project execution has picked up. Sales for H1’FY27 stood at 
INR 1,430 crores, up 12.5% year-on-year. 
 
EBIT for Q2’FY27 was INR 56 crores, compared with INR 72 crores in the corresponding quarter of the 
previous year. EBIT for H1’FY27 was INR 64 crores, compared with INR 130 crores in H1’FY26. Profitability 
remains lower than last year. This is due to commodity price volatility and the lag in passing on higher input 
costs on certain legacy orders. Margins are improving sequentially as the Company executes orders booked 
at current cost levels. 
 
Deepak Sharma, Zone President- Greater India, Schneider Electric, and Board Director, Schneider 
Electric Infrastructure Limited, said, “SEIL has delivered another strong order quarter, and the recovery in 
sales in Q2 shows that our execution is gaining momentum. Demand from data centres, semiconductors 
and grid infrastructure continues to be strong as India advances its electrification and industrial 
modernisation journey. While profitability remains below last year, our priority is to convert the strong order 
book into sales, and to improve project margins, through disciplined execution, cost pass-through and 
portfolio enrichment.” 
 
Udai Singh, MD & CEO, Schneider Electric Infrastructure Limited, said, “Highest-ever orders in Q2, a 
strong sequential recovery in sales and a record order backlog make this a solid half year for SEIL. 
Our focus now is on timely delivery, operational excellence and improving the margin quality of our  
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Press Release 
 
 
 
 
 
order book. We are also investing for the future. The Board has approved a capacity expansion at  
our Kolkata facility, and we have been recognised for our work on sustainability and governance. 
With a healthy pipeline and a strong backlog, we are well positioned to create long-term value for 
our customers and shareholders.” 
 
Beyond the numbers, SEIL continued to invest in building capacity for growth while strengthening its 
sustainability and governance credentials. 
 
To support growing demand, the Board of Directors, at its meeting on 29 October 2026, approved a further 
capacity expansion at the Company's Kolkata Medium Voltage Components (KMVC) facility. The Company 
plans to invest INR 211 crores to increase Vacuum Interrupter capacity from 250,000 to 375,000 units per 
annum and to add Breaker capacity of 18,000 units per annum, by the end of FY 2028-29. The investment 
will be funded through internal accruals and/or external borrowings. It supports the Company's capacity 
augmentation requirements, export growth plans and technology upgradation initiatives. 
 
Growth at SEIL goes hand in hand with responsible business practices. Subsequent to the quarter end, the 
Company was recognised with the Excellence in Sustainability Award in the Manufacturing Corporate 
category at the 4th Annual Sustainability Symposium & Excellence Awards 2026, organised by the Indian 
Chamber of Commerce (ICC), and with the Golden Peacock Award 2026 for Excellence in Corporate 
Governance. The recognitions reflect SEIL's progress on decarbonisation, including 100% renewable 
electricity across its manufacturing sites and an approximately 80% reduction in Scope 1 and Scope 2 
emissions over three years, along with its focus on transparency and accountability.  
 
Together with its capacity investments, these efforts underline SEIL's approach of growing the business 
while creating long-term value for all stakeholders. 
 
Schneider Electric Infrastructure Limited (SEIL) 
Schneider Electric Infrastructure Limited (SEIL) is a leading and fast-growing company incorporated in 2011 
which specializes in manufacturing, designing, constructing, and servicing advanced products and systems for 
electricity networks. SEIL's innovation, rooted in EcoStruxure™, supports customers and partners in achieving 
successful digital transformation in energy management. The company's range of products includes 
transformers, switchgears, ring main units, circuit breakers, relays, services, automation solutions, and smart 
grid software, serving various industries such as power generation, oil & gas, transportation, mining, metal and 
minerals (MMM), emerging sectors like Data center, semiconductors, renewables and other electro-intensive 
segments. (CIN - L31900GJ2011PLC064420) https://infra-in.se.com/ 
 
About Schneider Electric   
  
Schneider Electric is a global energy technology leader, driving efficiency and sustainability by electrifying, 
automating, and digitalizing industries, businesses, and homes. Its technologies enable buildings, data 
centers, factories, infrastructure, and grids to operate as open, interconnected ecosystems, enhancing 
performance, resilience, and sustainability. The portfolio includes intelligent devices, software-defined 
architectures, AI-powered systems, digital services, and expert advisory. With 160,000 employees and 1 
million partners in over 100 countries, Schneider Electric is consistently ranked among the world’s most 
sustainable companies.

Mr. Punit Goenka along with senior management team. We will start with the opening remarks 
from Mr. Goenka, followed by commentary on operating and financial performance by Mr. 
Mukund Galgali, our Deputy CEO and CFO and subsequently, we'll open the floor for question-

season. Diwali is a few days away, but let me take this opportunity to wish each one of you and 
your lovely families in advance a very happy and prosperous Diwali and a great year ahead. 
Thank you for joining me and my team this evening for a conversation on the quarter gone by. 
As always, I will throw some light on the macro level strategic growth points, while the finer 
points pertaining to the financial and operational aspects will be touched upon by the domain 
expert, our CFO, in the room. 
For your company, the second quarter of this financial year was one of growth, strategic future-
centric investments and creative decisions focused towards achieving consumer delight. We 
witnessed a 13% growth in our operating revenues year-on-year. Despite the volatile 
geopolitical environment and macroeconomic headwinds that led to a subdued sentiment, 
your company's entrepreneurial spirit, pioneering vision and prudent approach enabled it to 
stay ahead of the curve.  
The revenue growth largely stems from a business that is a result of the key future-centric 
investment decisions as you all might have guessed our sports business. The steps taken in this 
business have led to strategic gains across the board especially for the digital business.

Q2 Performance Summary
o
39.9% revenue growth YoY, broad based as 
o
Top 5 products – 37% of revenue in Q2 FY27 vs 39%/39%/35%/30% in past 4 sequential quarters
o
Top 10 products – 55% of revenue in Q2 FY27 vs 55%/57%/53%/51% in past 4 sequential quarters
o
Pricing continues to remain stable driven by our focus on specialty / differentiated products
o
In our Q1 FY27 investor update, we had guided that sequential USD revenue growth would resume from 
Q2 FY27. In that regard, we are pleased to report USD revenue of $58 Mn for Q2 FY27 which is up 5%+ 
compared to $55Mn in Q1 FY27 . We continue to see strong revenue visibility in coming quarters
o
Gross Margins were stable sequentially and Operating EBITDA Margin is 25% in Q2 FY27 vs 24.2% in Q1 
FY27. In our Q1 FY27 investor update, we had upped our Operating EBITDA Margin guidance for FY27 to 
23%+ from 22-23%, and we now further up this guidance to 24%+ for FY27.
o
Cash flow from operations for the H1FY27 is INR 989 Mn
o
Received 3 product approvals in Q2 FY27. Commercialisation rate continues to be strong as 84% of 
approved products are commercialised. Some recent approvals will be commercialised in the coming 
quarter
o
Specialty portfolio’s contribution to gross profit for the quarter is 36%. Specialty focus underpinned by a 
robust pipeline.

Aashvi Shah: 
Good evening, everyone. This is Aashvi Shah from Adfactors PR Investor 
Relations. On behalf of TBO Tek Limited, I would like to welcome you all 
to the Earnings Conference Call for Q2 and H1 FY27. 
Today on the call, we have with us from the management, Mr. Ankush 
Nijhawan, Co-Founder and Joint Managing Director, Mr. Gaurav 
Bhatnagar, Co-Founder and Joint Managing Director, Mr. Vikas Jain, Chief 
Financial Officer, Mr. Akshat Verma, Whole-Time Director and Chief 
Technology Officer, Mr. Pramendra Tomar, General Counsel and Mr. 
Shreshth Mahajan, Associate Director- Investor Relations. 
We will begin today's call with opening remarks from the management, 
following which we will open the flow for Q&A. Before we begin, I would 
like to remind everyone that certain statements made during this call may 
be forward-looking in nature. These statements are based on 
management's current expectations and are subject to risks and 
uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from 
those expressed or implied. TBO Tek undertakes no obligation to publicly 
update these or revise any forward-looking statements based on 
subsequent events or developments. 
With that, I would now like to hand over the call to Mr. Gaurav Bhatnagar 
for his opening remarks. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Gaurav Bhatnagar: 
Thank you, Aashvi. Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining our 
Q2 & H1 FY27 Earnings Call. 
We are very happy to report that despite a very difficult geopolitical 
climate, we have been able to deliver strong double-digit growth in the 
core organic business as well. We have shared the numbers, but I do want 
to highlight that the 16% growth in GTV led to a 27% growth in adjusted 
EBITDA. So, we are continuing to demonstrate operating leverage for the 
second consecutive quarter. 
These numbers could be a lot stronger, and I just want to highlight a few 
things to demonstrate that once things start to get better, where 

                                                                                                                        TBO Tek Limited 
November 03, 2026 
 
 
Page 3 of 32 
eventually expect the business to be. Middle East, which has been the most 
impacted market because of the ongoing conflict, also delivered 10% 
growth on constant currency basis. With currency, we are seeing a 20% 
growth, but even on constant currency, Middle East delivered a 10% 
growth, which is quite remarkable given the circumstances that we are 
operating in. The market is obviously well below its baseline from a year 
ago. Our belief is that in a market like Middle East, we are continuing to 
gain share.  
Markets like Europe and APAC have delivered north of 30% growth. 
Europe on a fairly large base, has been becoming our largest source 
market now, which again is generally a consequence of the investment we

Equally encouraging is the quality of growth that we are observing. Across 
brands, we witnessed transaction-led growth and growth in our on premise 
channel sales. Both these trends are very heartening and are key to long-term 
sustainable growth trajectory. 
On a macro basis, India's food services industry remains one of the most 
exciting opportunities globally. Redseer's latest report puts the market at about 
USD 90 billion, growing to USD 150 billion by FY31. Within this, the organized 
players are expected to grow at 17% to 18% per annum, against just 3% to 4% 
for the unorganized market, a good tailwind for a company of our scale. The 
broader economy supports this trajectory. Real GDP grew 7.8% in the first 
quarter of this financial year, and Bain estimates that private consumption 
growth accelerated from 8% over 2022-24 to 10.5% in 2025. Indian consumers 
also remain amongst the most confident in the world with net optimism of 27% 
against a global average of minus 12% in the current scenario. 
More importantly, this growth is broad-based. Tier 2 and smaller cities now 
account for about 65% of India's online shoppers and Gen Z for 40% to 45%, 
a clear sign that aspiration is spreading across and well beyond the metros. 

 
 
Page 3 of 12 
 
The headroom in emerging India is vast. India's 30 largest cities have about 20 
branded QSR outlets per million people, while the national figure is closer to 4. 
The brands that combine trust, value and scale will lead this next phase of 
growth, and we are confident that DIL, post-merger with Sapphire Foods will 
be at its forefront. 
 
While the India opportunity is real, the near-term challenges are also far from 
over. We have seen strong food and fuel inflation and job losses because of 
AI adoption. The household budgets are under pressure. With this, we also 
need to reorient ourselves more in favor of value, given the macroeconomic 
reality in the Country and a strong K-shaped economy that India is turning into. 
 
The regulatory environment also continues to evolve rapidly. A heightened 
inspection drive from the food authorities across the country disrupted store 
operations during the inspections. While we strongly believe that a strong focus 
on hygiene and operational control is needed and will help formalization 
journey for the industry, there needs to be consistent application of the same. 
With food inflation firming and interest rates beginning to rise, we expect 
discretionary spending to stay under pressure as our peers have also already 
indicated. By providing sharper value at entry price points, consistent 
marketing and a concerted effort on bringing guests back into our restaurants, 
we feel we are well positioned to perform in the coming quarters. 
 
Our new management team is settling in, and we are confident that our plans 
with respect to pre-merger preparations are progressing well. We are 
expecting that the merger should get approvals in line with our initial plans. 
You will be pleased to know that we have received CCI approval for the merger 
from the authorities. 
 
With this, I will now go to the detailed business and financial highlights.  
The current macroeconomic environment in India presents a complex, and 
highly polarized economic landscape. Coupled with this, the uncertain 
regulatory environment also poses additional complexity.  
If we analyse the data, we see a stark divergence between current micro 
realities and macro expectations. 
 
Basis the above, we have already started work on some specific initiatives on 
our key brands. At KFC, we have taken concerted steps to up our recruitment 
engine through the INR 99 and INR 149 meal combos. While we continue with 
our abundant value proposition on Wednesdays, the same has been 

 
 
Page 4 of 12 
 
supplemented by targeted BOGO (buy one get one) offer in the relevant 
markets. We have taken similar initiatives on Pizza Hut and we will be rolling 
out the same in the next couple of quarters. At Biryani By Kilo, we are 
experimenting with better value proposition for the brand at our food courts 
through the BBK Express outlets. As the brands go deeper into emerging cities, 
a strong customer recruitment engine is a critical investment for the long-term 
growth of the brand. We need to make sure that we can achieve the above 
with a minimal impact on our margins, and hence, we are approaching it in a 
very calibrated manner.  
We have also seen strong inflation coming in at multiple levels in the business 
over the last couple of quarters. Raw materials like chicken, edible oils, dairy, 
etc., are trending higher year-on-year, although there has been some 
mitigation on account of carryover effect of old inventories. LPG availability has 
normalized, but the prices are nearly double as compared to the previous year. 
Several states have announced steep minimum wage hike, further 
compounding the margin pressure. We have taken a very small and calibrated 
1% to 2% price hike on a YTD basis, and we continue to monitor the movement 
of key raw materials. Our endeavour is to take price hikes on a staggered basis 
to protect the already muted consumer sentiment. We have tried to mitigate 
the impact of the above by way of sharper execution on promotions and 
optimization of deals, coupled with cost-saving measures that have helped us 
to protect our overall margins.  
The consolidated DIL revenue for Q2 grew 10.4% year-on-year to INR 1,519 
crore, and operating EBITDA (pre-Ind AS basis) came in at INR 125 crore with 
a growth of almost 34% year-on-year. The gross margins at 68.5% was an 
improvement of 70 basis points over the previous year, and we saw the 
improvement in both our Indian as well as international business. The 
consolidated brand contribution margin expanded to 13% with a brand 
contribution of INR 198 crore, up 23% year-on-year. Together with effective 
management of G&A costs, this helped us post operating EBITDA margin of 
8.2% versus 6.8% in the previous year. Delivering this performance in a 
seasonally soft quarter and amid strong inflation is a testament to the execution 
skills of the DIL team. 
Moving on to the brands now. At KFC, SSSG came in at 4.4% with on-premise 
saliency of 56%. Revenue grew 12.3% year-on-year to INR 642 crore. Gross 
margin was 68.2%, broadly flat year-on-year, accounting for the high food 
inflation. Brand contribution margin came in at 13.9%, virtually flat versus the 
previous year despite steep minimum wage increases, especially in states like 

 
 
Page 5 of 12 
 
Karnataka, Kerala, Andhra and Telangana and elevated LPG prices. We 
added 50 net new stores, taking the KFC network to 844 stores. Alongside the 
value combos, KFC also hosted the Fried Chicken month in July, with a buy-
one-get-one bucket offer every Friday for dine-in and takeaway. We continue 
to see strong customer response to our offerings and campaigns, 
strengthening our belief that the brand can sustainably deliver mid-single 
SSSG growth in the long term. 
At Pizza Hut, SSSG decline narrowed versus the previous quarter at minus 
1.4%, with ADS at INR 32,000 per store per day. Revenue was INR 184 crore, 
nearly flat year-on-year. Gross margin improved to 76.7% on better targeted 
promotions, but higher LPG and wage costs took brand contribution margin to 
minus 1.8%, a loss of INR 3.3 crore like the previous quarter. We ended the 
quarter with 632 stores, adding 6 net new stores to replace underperforming 
stores that we have closed. We tested a new spicy range of pizzas and sides. 
Customer response to the 3-in-1 range of spicy pizzas has been encouraging. 
We are working on new product ideas and laying the groundwork for the long-
term revival of the brand. 
Our Own Brand portfolio of Vaango and Biryani By Kilo delivered healthy 
performance. BBK continues to show strong traction, with a SSSG of 8.1%, 
while Vaango delivered a SSSG of 6.9% positive. We have seen a strong 
turnaround in BBK and the brand has improved on both topline growth and 
margins. The brand contribution margin is now close to double digits. As a 
result, our Own Brands portfolio posted a revenue of INR 95 crore, nearly 11% 
higher year-on-year. Gross margins improved to 65.4% from 62.6% last year, 
and brand contribution came in at INR 9 crore, a margin of 9.4%. Our Own 
Brands' network reached 225 stores, including 26 BBK Express stores. 
 
For our franchisee brands portfolio, revenue growth remained steady at 7% 
year-on-year. Costa delivered an impressive 9.9% SSSG, maintaining its 
strong growth rate. Gross margin at 74.2% was better than 73.6% last year. 
Brand contribution margin came in at 15.5%. The total store count stood at 202 
stores as of the end of the quarter. 
 
Our international business maintained its impressive run in delivering strong 
and consistent growth and posted INR 509 crore in quarterly revenues. This is 
despite Thailand facing severe flooding in September, which resulted in 
business disruption and overall softer consumer environment due to a higher 
fuel cost. Gross margins were better on a year-on-year basis, but declined 
slightly sequentially. Brand contribution margin was up by 1.2% compared to 
last year at 17.9% and came in at INR 91 crore for the quarter. 

 
 
Page 6 of 12 
 
 
On store expansion, our revamped BD structure is now in place and is 
executing well. Of the 70 net new stores, 68 were added in India, taking us to 
1,923 stores in India and 2,325 globally as of September 30, 2026. Our new 
store openings remain in line with the guidance given earlier. 
 
As regards our proposed merger with Sapphire Foods, we are pleased to 
mention that we have received the CCI approval on the merger last week. We 
are awaiting no objection from SEBI now. Once we have received the SEBI 
no-objection, we can proceed with the NCLT application. In summary, we 
continue to remain optimistic about closing the merger process by the end of 
the current financial year. The Sky Gate merger is also moving as per the plan, 
and we are expecting the merger approval from NCLT very shortly. 
 
Lastly, our results for the quarter demonstrate that we continue to execute 5 
key priorities that we have laid for ourselves. (1) Expand our store footprint; (2) 
Maintain positive SSSG; (3) Improve efficiency and margin structure by way of 
judicious cost controls; (4) Build the next level of team/organization structure 
with right processes; and (5) Readiness for the merged entity.

Q2 & H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call 
November 02, 2026 
 
 
 
Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Devyani International's 
Earnings Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the 
listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after 
the presentation concludes. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Anoop Poojari from CDR India. Thank 
you, and over to you, sir. 
Anoop Poojari: 
Good afternoon everyone, and thank you for joining us on Devyani 
International's Q2 & H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call. The Chairman has 
excused himself from today's call due to personal reasons. We have with us 
Mr. Raj Gandhi, Non-Executive Director; Mr. Manish Dawar, President and 
Group CEO; and Mr. Anupam Kumar, CFO of the Company. 
 
We will initiate the call with opening remarks on behalf of Mr. Ravi Jaipuria. 
Since the Chairman could not join us today, Mr. Manish Dawar will read the 
comments on his behalf. This will be followed by key business and financial 
highlights by him. Thereafter, we will have the forum open for a question-and-
answer session.  
Before we begin, I would like to point out that some statements made in today's 
call may be forward-looking in nature, and a disclaimer to this effect has been 
included in the results presentation shared with you earlier. 
 
I will now request Mr. Manish Dawar to read the Chairman's opening remarks. 
Manish Dawar: 
Thanks, Anoop. Good afternoon everyone. So I am going to read the 
comments on behalf of Mr. Jaipuria, and then I will come to the detailed 
business and financial highlights.  
Good afternoon everyone, and thank you for joining us. It gives me great 
pleasure to welcome you to Devyani International's earnings call for the second 

 
 
Page 2 of 12 
 
quarter of FY26-27. 
 
Our growth momentum carried on firmly into the second quarter. We have had 
a good quarter with positive SSSGs ranging from 4% to 9% across our brand 
portfolio in India, except Pizza Hut, which also saw sequentially better 
numbers. We added 70 net new stores during the quarter. KFC led the store 
additions, with 50 net new units added in India. This takes our store footprint 
to 1,923 stores in India and 2,325 stores globally. We are on track to meet our 
full-year guidance of 200 to 220 net new additions with the same discipline, the 
right locations and a clear line of sight to profitability.  
Consistent performance across brands, quarter-after-quarter tells us that the 
steps we have taken to sharpen our consumer proposition are taking hold. 
 
Building on the positive SSSG performance, we delivered consolidated sales 
of INR 1,519 crore, growing 10.4% year-on-year. Despite steep inflation in raw 
materials and wages, the leverage from higher same-store sales and tight cost 
control helped us lift EBITDA by nearly 18% to INR 229 crore. This is one of 
the best Q2 operating EBITDA numbers that we have seen and the same 
helped us post profit before taxes of INR 5.7 crore for the quarter against a 
loss last year. Your Company delivered a PBT of INR 29 crore in H1 versus a 
loss of INR 24 crore in the previous year. 
 
Equally encouraging is the quality of growth that we are observing. Across 
brands, we witnessed transaction-led growth and growth in our on premise 
channel sales. Both these trends are very heartening and are key to long-term 
sustainable growth trajectory. 
On a macro basis, India's food services industry remains one of the most 
exciting opportunities globally. Redseer's latest report puts the market at about 
USD 90 billion, growing to USD 150 billion by FY31. Within this, the organized 
players are expected to grow at 17% to 18% per annum, against just 3% to 4% 
for the unorganized market, a good tailwind for a company of our scale. The 
broader economy supports this trajectory. Real GDP grew 7.8% in the first 
quarter of this financial year, and Bain estimates that private consumption 
growth accelerated from 8% over 2022-24 to 10.5% in 2025. Indian consumers 
also remain amongst the most confident in the world with net optimism of 27% 
against a global average of minus 12% in the current scenario. 
More importantly, this growth is broad-based. Tier 2 and smaller cities now 
account for about 65% of India's online shoppers and Gen Z for 40% to 45%, 
a clear sign that aspiration is spreading across and well beyond the metros. 

 
 
Page 3 of 12 
 
The headroom in emerging India is vast. India's 30 largest cities have about 20 
branded QSR outlets per million people, while the national figure is closer to 4. 
The brands that combine trust, value and scale will lead this next phase of 
growth, and we are confident that DIL, post-merger with Sapphire Foods will 
be at its forefront. 
 
While the India opportunity is real, the near-term challenges are also far from 
over. We have seen strong food and fuel inflation and job losses because of 
AI adoption. The household budgets are under pressure. With this, we also 
need to reorient ourselves more in favor of value, given the macroeconomic 
reality in the Country and a strong K-shaped economy that India is turning into. 
 
The regulatory environment also continues to evolve rapidly. A heightened 
inspection drive from the food authorities across the country disrupted store 
operations during the inspections. While we strongly believe that a strong focus 
on hygiene and operational control is needed and will help formalization 
journey for the industry, there needs to be consistent application of the same. 
With food inflation firming and interest rates beginning to rise, we expect 
discretionary spending to stay under pressure as our peers have also already 
indicated. By providing sharper value at entry price points, consistent 
marketing and a concerted effort on bringing guests back into our restaurants, 
we feel we are well positioned to perform in the coming quarters. 
 
Our new management team is settling in, and we are confident that our plans 
with respect to pre-merger preparations are progressing well. We are 
expecting that the merger should get approvals in line with our initial plans. 
You will be pleased to know that we have received CCI approval for the merger 
from the authorities. 
 
With this, I will now go to the detailed business and financial highlights.  
The current macroeconomic environment in India presents a complex, and 
highly polarized economic landscape. Coupled with this, the uncertain 
regulatory environment also poses additional complexity.  
If we analyse the data, we see a stark divergence between current micro 
realities and macro expectations. 
 
Basis the above, we have already started work on some specific initiatives on 
our key brands. At KFC, we have taken concerted steps to up our recruitment 
engine through the INR 99 and INR 149 meal combos. While we continue with 
our abundant value proposition on Wednesdays, the same has been 

 
 
Page 4 of 12 
 
supplemented by targeted BOGO (buy one get one) offer in the relevant 
markets. We have taken similar initiatives on Pizza Hut and we will be rolling 
out the same in the next couple of quarters. At Biryani By Kilo, we are 
experimenting with better value proposition for the brand at our food courts 
through the BBK Express outlets. As the brands go deeper into emerging cities, 
a strong customer recruitment engine is a critical investment for the long-term 
growth of the brand. We need to make sure that we can achieve the above 
with a minimal impact on our margins, and hence, we are approaching it in a 
very calibrated manner.  
We have also seen strong inflation coming in at multiple levels in the business 
over the last couple of quarters. Raw materials like chicken, edible oils, dairy, 
etc., are trending higher year-on-year, although there has been some 
mitigation on account of carryover effect of old inventories. LPG availability has 
normalized, but the prices are nearly double as compared to the previous year. 
Several states have announced steep minimum wage hike, further 
compounding the margin pressure. We have taken a very small and calibrated 
1% to 2% price hike on a YTD basis, and we continue to monitor the movement 
of key raw materials. Our endeavour is to take price hikes on a staggered basis 
to protect the already muted consumer sentiment. We have tried to mitigate 
the impact of the above by way of sharper execution on promotions and 
optimization of deals, coupled with cost-saving measures that have helped us 
to protect our overall margins.  
The consolidated DIL revenue for Q2 grew 10.4% year-on-year to INR 1,519 
crore, and operating EBITDA (pre-Ind AS basis) came in at INR 125 crore with 
a growth of almost 34% year-on-year. The gross margins at 68.5% was an 
improvement of 70 basis points over the previous year, and we saw the 
improvement in both our Indian as well as international business. The 
consolidated brand contribution margin expanded to 13% with a brand 
contribution of INR 198 crore, up 23% year-on-year. Together with effective 
management of G&A costs, this helped us post operating EBITDA margin of 
8.2% versus 6.8% in the previous year. Delivering this performance in a 
seasonally soft quarter and amid strong inflation is a testament to the execution 
skills of the DIL team. 
Moving on to the brands now. At KFC, SSSG came in at 4.4% with on-premise 
saliency of 56%. Revenue grew 12.3% year-on-year to INR 642 crore. Gross 
margin was 68.2%, broadly flat year-on-year, accounting for the high food 
inflation. Brand contribution margin came in at 13.9%, virtually flat versus the 
previous year despite steep minimum wage increases, especially in states like 

 
 
Page 5 of 12 
 
Karnataka, Kerala, Andhra and Telangana and elevated LPG prices. We 
added 50 net new stores, taking the KFC network to 844 stores. Alongside the 
value combos, KFC also hosted the Fried Chicken month in July, with a buy-
one-get-one bucket offer every Friday for dine-in and takeaway. We continue 
to see strong customer response to our offerings and campaigns, 
strengthening our belief that the brand can sustainably deliver mid-single 
SSSG growth in the long term. 
At Pizza Hut, SSSG decline narrowed versus the previous quarter at minus 
1.4%, with ADS at INR 32,000 per store per day. Revenue was INR 184 crore, 
nearly flat year-on-year. Gross margin improved to 76.7% on better targeted 
promotions, but higher LPG and wage costs took brand contribution margin to 
minus 1.8%, a loss of INR 3.3 crore like the previous quarter. We ended the 
quarter with 632 stores, adding 6 net new stores to replace underperforming 
stores that we have closed. We tested a new spicy range of pizzas and sides. 
Customer response to the 3-in-1 range of spicy pizzas has been encouraging. 
We are working on new product ideas and laying the groundwork for the long-
term revival of the brand. 
Our Own Brand portfolio of Vaango and Biryani By Kilo delivered healthy 
performance. BBK continues to show strong traction, with a SSSG of 8.1%, 
while Vaango delivered a SSSG of 6.9% positive. We have seen a strong 
turnaround in BBK and the brand has improved on both topline growth and 
margins. The brand contribution margin is now close to double digits. As a 
result, our Own Brands portfolio posted a revenue of INR 95 crore, nearly 11% 
higher year-on-year. Gross margins improved to 65.4% from 62.6% last year, 
and brand contribution came in at INR 9 crore, a margin of 9.4%. Our Own 
Brands' network reached 225 stores, including 26 BBK Express stores. 
 
For our franchisee brands portfolio, revenue growth remained steady at 7% 
year-on-year. Costa delivered an impressive 9.9% SSSG, maintaining its 
strong growth rate. Gross margin at 74.2% was better than 73.6% last year. 
Brand contribution margin came in at 15.5%. The total store count stood at 202 
stores as of the end of the quarter. 
 
Our international business maintained its impressive run in delivering strong 
and consistent growth and posted INR 509 crore in quarterly revenues. This is 
despite Thailand facing severe flooding in September, which resulted in 
business disruption and overall softer consumer environment due to a higher 
fuel cost. Gross margins were better on a year-on-year basis, but declined 
slightly sequentially. Brand contribution margin was up by 1.2% compared to 
last year at 17.9% and came in at INR 91 crore for the quarter. 

 
 
Page 6 of 12 
 
 
On store expansion, our revamped BD structure is now in place and is 
executing well. Of the 70 net new stores, 68 were added in India, taking us to 
1,923 stores in India and 2,325 globally as of September 30, 2026. Our new 
store openings remain in line with the guidance given earlier. 
 
As regards our proposed merger with Sapphire Foods, we are pleased to 
mention that we have received the CCI approval on the merger last week. We 
are awaiting no objection from SEBI now. Once we have received the SEBI 
no-objection, we can proceed with the NCLT application. In summary, we 
continue to remain optimistic about closing the merger process by the end of 
the current financial year. The Sky Gate merger is also moving as per the plan, 
and we are expecting the merger approval from NCLT very shortly. 
 
Lastly, our results for the quarter demonstrate that we continue to execute 5 
key priorities that we have laid for ourselves. (1) Expand our store footprint; (2) 
Maintain positive SSSG; (3) Improve efficiency and margin structure by way of 
judicious cost controls; (4) Build the next level of team/organization structure 
with right processes; and (5) Readiness for the merged entity. 
 
With this, I would request the moderator to open the forum for any questions 
or suggestions that you may have. Thank you very much.

prep_items.text:
November 05, 2026 
 
To, 
National Stock Exchange of India Limited 
(NSE: RATEGAIN) 
 
BSE Limited 
(BSE: 543417) 
 
Sub: 
Disclosure under Regulation 30 read with Schedule III of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 
Ref:  
Intimation regarding prepayment of loan 
 
Dear Sir / Ma’am, 
 
This is with reference to the disclosure filed by the Company on October 29, 2025, pursuant to Regulation 30 read with 
Schedule III of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“LODR Regulation”), that 
RateGain Travel Technologies Limited, (hereinafter referred to as the “Company”) had signed a Facility Agreement on 
October 29, 2025 (“Facility Agreement”), and issued corporate guarantee (“Guarantee”) in favor of  The Hongkong 
and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (“HSBC”) and CitiGroup Global Markets Asia Limited (“Citibank”) in 
respect of loan facilities being availed by RateGain Technologies Limited, UK (“RateGain UK”), a wholly owned 
subsidiary of the Company. 
 
Further, the Company had intimated the Stock Exchanges on February 05, 2026 and August 05, 2026, regarding the 
prepayment of USD 19,000,000 (USD 19 Million) and USD 9,750,000 (USD 9.75 Million), respectively, along with the 
applicable loan instalments of USD 6,250,000 (USD 6.25 Million) by RateGain UK to lenders out of the total credit 
facilities of USD 125,000,000 (USD 125 Million). 
In continuation of the aforesaid disclosures, we wish to inform you that RateGain UK has further prepaid an amount of 
USD 46,250,000 (USD 46.25 Million) to its bankers, out of the total credit facilities of USD 125,000,000 (USD 125 
Million). 
Consequent to the aforesaid prepayment, the outstanding loan/debt stands reduced to USD 31,250,000 (USD 31.25 
Million), and a drawn credit facility of an aggregate maximum amount of up to USD 40 Million, as intimated to the Stock 
Exchanges on August 20, 2026. 
You are further informed that the guarantee provided by the Company shall also stand reduced to the aforesaid extent, in 
accordance with the terms of the Facility Agreement. 
 
This is for your information and records. 
 
Yours faithfully, 
For RateGain Travel Technologies Limited 
 
 
 
Mukesh Kumar 
General Counsel, 
Company Secretary & Compliance Officer 
Membership No.: A17925 
 
 
Mukesh 
Kumar
Digitally signed by 
Mukesh Kumar

“Our strong momentum continued through Q2 and H1 FY’27, driven by overall market growth, market share gains and disciplined 
execution across the business. Value-Added Revenue grew 32.2% in Q2 and 25.3% in H1, Volumes grew 25.4% in Q2 and 20.7% in H1

Vehicle Suspension Systems.
During the period, we continued to deepen customer relationships and expand our technology footprint. In ART, we secured multiple 
platform wins across domestic and international OEMs, entered a new passenger vehicle whitespace, expanded engagement with 
leading Japanese and Vietnamese OEMs, and advanced our portfolio through successful commercialization and localization initiatives. 
In CA and PT, we strengthened our order pipeline through key wins across commercial vehicle, CNG, and spark plug applications.

Future Leadership Award from National CSR Leadership Congress, reflecting our unwavering commitment to operational excellence 
and sustainability.

investments, we remain well positioned to sustain above-market growth and drive superior shareholder returns over the long term.”

Operational

“We delivered a strong performance in Q2 FY’27, building on the momentum from the start of the year. Revenue from operations 
increased 34.2% YoY to INR 17.2 billion, while Value Added Revenue1 grew 32.2% to INR 15.2 billion, driven by higher volumes and 
the continued ramp-up of new program launches. For H1 FY’27, revenue from operations stood at INR 32.6 billion (+27.2% YoY) 
and Value Added Revenue reached INR 29.0 billion (+25.3% YoY), reflecting sustained demand across our portfolio.
EBITDA for the quarter grew 20.7% YoY to INR 2,616 million, taking H1 EBITDA to INR 5,085 million, up 14.1% year-on-year. 
Inflationary pressures linked to geopolitical developments remained elevated during the period; however, their impact was 
substantially offset through commercial recovery actions, productivity improvements, and disciplined cost control. PAT for Q2 
FY2027 increased to INR 1,734 million (+15.0% YoY), while H1 PAT stood at INR 3,386 million (+6.2% YoY). Q2 / H1 FY’26 includes 
one-time interest income related to Motocare entity sale amounting to INR 67 Mn (Net of tax) and INR 254 Mn (Net of Tax) 
respectively.  PAT Growth for Q2 / H1 FY’27 excluding this one-off interest income is 20.4% / 15.4% respectively.
Our operating performance continues to benefit from the maturity of the P3 (People, Performance, Pride) framework, which has 
strengthened execution, enhanced accountability, and reinforced a culture of continuous improvement across the organization. This 
focus on operational excellence has enabled us to respond effectively to external challenges while maintaining strong delivery, 
quality, and cost performance.
Supported by healthy cash generation and prudent capital allocation, our financial position remains robust, and we continue to 
operate with a net debt free balance sheet. While the external environment remains uncertain, we are confident in the resilience of 
our business and remain focused on disciplined execution, commercial rigor, and proactive risk management to deliver sustainable 
profitable growth and long-term value creation.”

Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
In furtherance to our Board Meeting intimation dated Monday, 02nd November, 2026, and pursuant to

Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”), the Board of Directors (“the Board”) of

September, 2026, along with Limited Review Reports thereon:

Year ended 30th September, 2026 of the financial year 2026-27 along with the Limited Review Reports 
issued by the Statutory Auditors, which is enclosed herewith pursuant to Regulation 33(3) of the SEBI 
Listing Regulations.

approved by the Board of Directors of the Company at their meeting held today i.e. Thursday, 05th 
November, 2026.

uploaded on the website of Stock Exchanges at www.nseindia.com and www.bseindia.com as well as on 
the website of the Company at www.lloydsenterprises.in 
 
2. The forfeiture of partly paid-up equity shares of the Company in respect of which the call money 
remains unpaid by the concerned shareholders within the prescribed period, in accordance with the 
terms of issue, the Articles of Association of the Company and applicable provisions of law:

pursuant to the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, the Articles of Association of the Company, and

paid-up equity shares on which the holders thereof failed to pay the outstanding First and Final Call

Company. Consequently, the said 3,35,552 partly paid-up equity shares stand forfeited and all amounts

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call of 
Clean Science and Technology Limited. We have with us on the call Mr. Siddharth Sikchi, 
Managing Director and Promoter; Mr. Sanjay Parnerkar, CFO; and Mr. Pratik Bora, President, 
Commercial. 
 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance 
during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touch-
tone phone. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Siddharth Sikchi for opening remarks. Thank you, and 
over to you, sir. 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
Thank you so much. Good afternoon, all of you, for taking time out to listen to our earnings call 
on Saturday. So let me present to you the Q2 FY27 earnings. 
 
So let me first speak about the basic -- the business performance. The quarter marked yet another 
consequent quarter of being the highest ever revenue in the history of the company, highlighting 
our continued effort to translate from investment phase to asset monetization phase in the new 
HALS segment, wherein base business, we continue to increase our volumes in our flagship 
products, dictating a robust cost competitiveness. 
 
On the base business of Clean Science, the base business saw a resilient volume-led growth 
across Performance and Pharma segment. Export sales increased to 73% of the stand-alone 
business against 64% during the previous quarter. Otherwise, this base business showed a steady 
performance.  
On the HALS segment, on Y-o-Y basis, the HALS segment grew 2x in revenue during the 
quarter. 
 
It was achieved on back of robust HALS volume growth. To give a little perspective, in H1 
FY27, we achieved aggregated volumes of 67% of the total volumes achieved during entire 
previous financial ye ar. This growth means more to us than just numbers show. It reflects a 
fundamental shift in how our customers see us. 
 
We started as a new entrant providing our quality. And today, we are one of the trusted strategic 
partner with the customers. This trust is very difficult to win, and we are very proud to have 
earned this. Further, as we speak, we continue to add new customers and increase the wallet 
share from existing customers every quarter. 
 
On cost improvement fronts, during the quarter and also in the subsequent quarters, we will be 
starting some of the key starting materials for some of these HALS products, which eventually 
will result in improvement in our gross margin. Put all together, healthy volumes, continuous 
process improvement and benefits of operational leverage have resulted in EBITDA margin of 
12% in the first half of FY27. And during this quarter, we reached a PAT positive. 

 
Clean Science and Technology Limited 
 
October 31, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 9 
 
 
CFCL has conducted and completed trials for the advanced grade of HALS product. This marks 
a significant milestone towards the commercial launch of the new product expected to 
commence in H2 of FY27. A little on the input costs. Input costs have remained high during the 
quarter as the Middle East crisis conflict kept the crude-linked feedstock prices high. Key raw 
materials such as phenol, acetone and methanol were 50% to 100% higher year-on-year 
alongside an increase in coal and freight costs. 
 
With Chinese prices yet to move up, the pass-through to the customers was difficult. 
Consequently, the raw material cost rose to 43.3% versus 39.7% on a consolidated basis. 
However, the customer demand remained resilient. 
 
Now let me touch upon the financial performance for the period 30th September '26, stand-alone, 
starting with Q-on-Q comparison. On a sequential basis, revenues improved by 11% to INR226 
crores, largely due to higher volume across Performance, Pharma and FMCG. EBITDA and 
PAT margins are at 36% and 24%, translating into EBITDA of INR82 crores and PAT of INR55 
crores. Margin moderation was primarily due to high raw material costs, which rose to 41% from 
35% in Q1 FY27. 
 
On Y-o-Y comparison, sales grew by 10% during the quarter. The revenue growth was primarily 
led by improved realization, while volumes were broadly stable. The demand environment 
continues to be steady. On a consol basis, company delivered a healthy volume-led growth of 
12%, resulting in revenues of INR295 crores on a consolidated basis with EBITDA and PAT 
margins of INR92 crores and INR56 crores, respectively. 
 
On Y-o-Y comparison, the sales grew 23% during the quarter. The revenue growth was primarily 
led by improved volume growth approximately 10% and realization by 13%. The increase in 
revenue is primarily led by consistent sale of HALS business and consolidated EBITDA grew 
by 6%, supported by turnaround in CFCL. 
 
On a year-to-date basis, consolidated sales grew by 17% to INR559 crores with EBITDA of 
INR188 crores and PAT of INR129 crores. The split was 77% Performance, 14% Pharma 
Intermediates and FMCG was 7%. 
 
A review on the capex. Performance Chemical 2 will get commercialized by quarter 3 to quarter 
4 FY27. During the quarter, capital infusion in subsidiary was approximately INR50 crores and 
INR150 crores in H1 FY27. With this, the total investment in subsidiary company stands at 
INR900 crores. 
 
With this, I conclude my opening remarks and take this opportunity to also wish you all a very 
Happy Diwali and looking forward to the Q&A session. Thank you.

session. The first question is from the line of Sanjesh Jain from ICICI Securities.

margin in this quarter doesn't make sense, right? There is a very sharp inflation in the raw

material, which mathematically compresses the margin. We are holding on to the existing run

inflation. Will that be a fair statement to make?

So but, Sanjesh, I think -- see, we were not able to pass through the price increase to the 
customer. So of course, the percentage-wise came down, but on absolute because of the volume 
growth, we were still able to maintain the absolute number.

So what was the volume growth for this quarter? 
Pratik Bora: 
Sequentially, the entire growth was volume-led. And annually, the growth largely is realization-
led. So what Siddharth is also trying to arrive this at is that during this quarter, the entire raw 
material cost increase on account of the inflationary pressure was not translated to the sales 
growth. Sequentially, the sales growth is largely volume-led. And hence, the margins have taken 
that impact. 
Sanjesh Jain: 
So we are -- this is purely on the stand-alone basis we are discussing, right? 
Pratik Bora:

Sanjesh Jain:

commodity prices which we see in China are far lower than the prices which we are buying in

big enough delta that they are not increasing the prices. They are holding on to all the prices, be 
it hydroquinone, be it MEHQ. And hence, we have to also maintain the prices and absorb all

of performance product one?

Okay. Okay. We haven't proceeded. We didn't make any changes in that plant we were planning

Arun Prasath:

“Clean Science and Technology Limited 
Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call” 
October 31, 2026 
  
 
 
 
 
 
MANAGEMENT: MR. SIDDHARTH SIKCHI –MANAGING DIRECTOR 
AND PROMOTER
