Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call of 
Clean Science and Technology Limited. We have with us on the call Mr. Siddharth Sikchi, 
Managing Director and Promoter; Mr. Sanjay Parnerkar, CFO; and Mr. Pratik Bora, President, 
Commercial. 
 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance 
during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touch-
tone phone. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Siddharth Sikchi for opening remarks. Thank you, and 
over to you, sir. 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
Thank you so much. Good afternoon, all of you, for taking time out to listen to our earnings call 
on Saturday. So let me present to you the Q2 FY27 earnings. 
 
So let me first speak about the basic -- the business performance. The quarter marked yet another 
consequent quarter of being the highest ever revenue in the history of the company, highlighting 
our continued effort to translate from investment phase to asset monetization phase in the new 
HALS segment, wherein base business, we continue to increase our volumes in our flagship 
products, dictating a robust cost competitiveness. 
 
On the base business of Clean Science, the base business saw a resilient volume-led growth 
across Performance and Pharma segment. Export sales increased to 73% of the stand-alone 
business against 64% during the previous quarter. Otherwise, this base business showed a steady 
performance.  
On the HALS segment, on Y-o-Y basis, the HALS segment grew 2x in revenue during the 
quarter. 
 
It was achieved on back of robust HALS volume growth. To give a little perspective, in H1 
FY27, we achieved aggregated volumes of 67% of the total volumes achieved during entire 
previous financial ye ar. This growth means more to us than just numbers show. It reflects a 
fundamental shift in how our customers see us. 
 
We started as a new entrant providing our quality. And today, we are one of the trusted strategic 
partner with the customers. This trust is very difficult to win, and we are very proud to have 
earned this. Further, as we speak, we continue to add new customers and increase the wallet 
share from existing customers every quarter. 
 
On cost improvement fronts, during the quarter and also in the subsequent quarters, we will be 
starting some of the key starting materials for some of these HALS products, which eventually 
will result in improvement in our gross margin. Put all together, healthy volumes, continuous 
process improvement and benefits of operational leverage have resulted in EBITDA margin of 
12% in the first half of FY27. And during this quarter, we reached a PAT positive. 

 
Clean Science and Technology Limited 
 
October 31, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 9 
 
 
CFCL has conducted and completed trials for the advanced grade of HALS product. This marks 
a significant milestone towards the commercial launch of the new product expected to 
commence in H2 of FY27. A little on the input costs. Input costs have remained high during the 
quarter as the Middle East crisis conflict kept the crude-linked feedstock prices high. Key raw 
materials such as phenol, acetone and methanol were 50% to 100% higher year-on-year 
alongside an increase in coal and freight costs. 
 
With Chinese prices yet to move up, the pass-through to the customers was difficult. 
Consequently, the raw material cost rose to 43.3% versus 39.7% on a consolidated basis. 
However, the customer demand remained resilient. 
 
Now let me touch upon the financial performance for the period 30th September '26, stand-alone, 
starting with Q-on-Q comparison. On a sequential basis, revenues improved by 11% to INR226 
crores, largely due to higher volume across Performance, Pharma and FMCG. EBITDA and 
PAT margins are at 36% and 24%, translating into EBITDA of INR82 crores and PAT of INR55 
crores. Margin moderation was primarily due to high raw material costs, which rose to 41% from 
35% in Q1 FY27. 
 
On Y-o-Y comparison, sales grew by 10% during the quarter. The revenue growth was primarily 
led by improved realization, while volumes were broadly stable. The demand environment 
continues to be steady. On a consol basis, company delivered a healthy volume-led growth of 
12%, resulting in revenues of INR295 crores on a consolidated basis with EBITDA and PAT 
margins of INR92 crores and INR56 crores, respectively. 
 
On Y-o-Y comparison, the sales grew 23% during the quarter. The revenue growth was primarily 
led by improved volume growth approximately 10% and realization by 13%. The increase in 
revenue is primarily led by consistent sale of HALS business and consolidated EBITDA grew 
by 6%, supported by turnaround in CFCL. 
 
On a year-to-date basis, consolidated sales grew by 17% to INR559 crores with EBITDA of 
INR188 crores and PAT of INR129 crores. The split was 77% Performance, 14% Pharma 
Intermediates and FMCG was 7%. 
 
A review on the capex. Performance Chemical 2 will get commercialized by quarter 3 to quarter 
4 FY27. During the quarter, capital infusion in subsidiary was approximately INR50 crores and 
INR150 crores in H1 FY27. With this, the total investment in subsidiary company stands at 
INR900 crores. 
 
With this, I conclude my opening remarks and take this opportunity to also wish you all a very 
Happy Diwali and looking forward to the Q&A session. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you very much. Sir, ladies and gentlemen. We will now begin the question-and-answer 
session. The first question is from the line of Sanjesh Jain from ICICI Securities. 
Sanjesh Jain: 
A couple of questions from my side. First, purely on the margin, just to clarify, the percentage 
margin in this quarter doesn't make sense, right? There is a very sharp inflation in the raw 

 
Clean Science and Technology Limited 
 
October 31, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 9 
 
material, which mathematically compresses the margin. We are holding on to the existing run 
rate of 92%. That means we have retained EBITDA per kg despite all the headwinds and 
inflation. Will that be a fair statement to make? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
So but, Sanjesh, I think -- see, we were not able to pass through the price increase to the 
customer. So of course, the percentage-wise came down, but on absolute because of the volume 
growth, we were still able to maintain the absolute number. 
Sanjesh Jain: 
So what was the volume growth for this quarter? 
Pratik Bora: 
Sequentially, the entire growth was volume-led. And annually, the growth largely is realization-
led. So what Siddharth is also trying to arrive this at is that during this quarter, the entire raw 
material cost increase on account of the inflationary pressure was not translated to the sales 
growth. Sequentially, the sales growth is largely volume-led. And hence, the margins have taken 
that impact. 
Sanjesh Jain: 
So we are -- this is purely on the stand-alone basis we are discussing, right? 
Pratik Bora: 
Yes, yes, stand-alone basis. 
Sanjesh Jain: 
So you're telling that this 12.5% growth is entirely the volume-led in the stand-alone business. 
And what is the anticipated price hike required for us to retain that EBITDA per kg kind of a run 
rate? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
So we'll have to really calculate because. 
Pratik Bora 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
Yes. Actually, see, the point is it's market-driven and the prices in China have not risen to the 
point that we can pass any benefit or any cost increase to the customer. Apparently, the 
commodity prices which we see in China are far lower than the prices which we are buying in 
India. 
Sanjesh Jain: 
You mean phenol, acetone prices? The differential are... 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
Yes, at least 10%, 15%, the prices are lower in China. 
Sanjesh Jain: 
Okay. No, no, I got the point. I got it. But how is the economics between HQ route and the 
Anisole route because we thought Chinese are largely on an HQ route, which they were 
disadvantaged at some point of time. This phenol, acetone difference is making all that -- we are 
now competitively at a stage that Chinese are holding up on the price increase for us? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
So basically, the reason is, I think -- see, the crude oil prices -- I mean, the phenol spread if China 
price of phenol is about 1,300, whereas India prices of phenol is over INR1,550. So that delta is 
big enough delta that they are not increasing the prices. They are holding on to all the prices, be 
it hydroquinone, be it MEHQ. And hence, we have to also maintain the prices and absorb all 

 
Clean Science and Technology Limited 
 
October 31, 2026 
 
Page 5 of 9 
 
these raw material prices ourselves to keep the market share in China or in other parts of the 
world. 
Sanjesh Jain: 
Now I'm very clear. Super clear, Siddharth. Second, on the new product, HQ, which we started 
now a quarter back, we said this quarter, we will do commercial. Where are we there, in terms 
of performance product one? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
So in hydroquinone, catechol -- Sanjesh, see, right now, we are at about 30%, 35% capacity 
utilization. And fortunately, all these capacities are currently used for our own captive 
consumption. And small sales have picked up in Europe and I think some -- and also something 
in India. 
Sanjesh Jain: 
Got it. My next question on the HALS, Siddharth. Good to see volume picking up very sharply 
for us. You also mentioned in your opening remarks that we are looking at more backward 
integrating or some of our backward integration projects are in the process of getting 
commissioned. What are these products? And is this for the contract we have done with the 
Geneus or this is a different we are talking about? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
No. See, these -- some base products which we manufacture to make it more cost effective, we 
have identified some of the intermediates. If we are able to make it in-house, it further improves 
our cost competitiveness in these products. So we have already started one product where we 
have put an ethoxylation facility. So that product has started, which is a precursor for one of the 
HALS. 
 
And in the next quarter, we will be starting another intermediate, which we were currently 
buying from China, which we will be making in-house to make these HALS more cost effective. 
Sanjesh Jain: 
Okay. These are solvents or the building blocks we are talking about? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
No, no. These are building blocks. These are raw materials. These are not solvents. 
Sanjesh Jain: 
Got it. Got it. And you mentioned that we have successfully tested the products for the contract. 
When should we start seeing them flowing into revenue? Will it be more like FY28 or something 
next -- this quarter, running quarter? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
Yes, yes. November or December, we'll start shipping this material to Europe. 
Sanjesh Jain: 
Got it. Got it. One last from my side, Siddharth, before I get back into the queue. We were 
expecting to produce barbituric acid. I haven't heard about that for a while now. Any update you 
want to share there? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
See, basically, we realized that currently, the prices which Chinese are offering, we are not able 
to offer those prices. So we have kept this product on hold for the moment. 
Sanjesh Jain: 
Okay. Okay. We haven't proceeded. We didn't make any changes in that plant we were planning 
to, right? 

 
Clean Science and Technology Limited 
 
October 31, 2026 
 
Page 6 of 9 
 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
No, we did that. But we want -- because the major raw material is imported from China, but the 
Chinese producers are not able to -- are not increasing the prices, but the other raw materials 
which you are buying from India have become almost 3x. So it is not making any sense for us 
to produce at the moment. 
Sanjesh Jain: 
Got it. Got it. And then post this performance, to which we are very close to commissioning, 
what is the product pipeline looks like for FY28 and '29? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
So I think we are very bullish on this whole light stabilizer segment. So we are going to de-
bottleneck and we are going to add increased capacities in some of these products and also trying 
to get in allied or adjacencies, which will be catering to the same customers. So you will see all 
these products coming up in the next few quarters. 
Sanjesh Jain: 
No, I missed which product -- life -- sorry, sorry, I missed the product. 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
Light stabilizers adjacencies. HALS adjacencies. It's something which we will start producing 
in the next few quarters. 
Sanjesh Jain: 
Okay. Okay. Nothing in the performance segment apart from the HALS adjacency right now we 
are looking at, right? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
Right now, no, not at the moment. 
Moderator: 
The next question is from the line of Arun Prasath from Avendus Spark. 
Arun Prasath: 
Siddharth, I understood why we have not able to take the price hike. But my question is, what 
will push us and which will eventually make us take the price hike? What is the breaking point? 
What should we monitor from our side, which will indicate that we'll be taking the price hike? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
See, we are continuously trying to increase the prices. When we get a severe pushback, we know 
the prices are where they are currently. And our point is very simple. We don't want to lose our 
market share because gaining these market share again becomes a big problem. So by retaining 
the market share, if we are able to increase the price, we are more than happy to do so. 
Arun Prasath: 
Right. But for that, the demand of the core products should be higher than the discretionary 
capacity at the Chinese. Do you see that gap narrowing down at any point of time? Because 
given the current phenol, acetone trends, it doesn't look like the prices is going to correct unless 
crude takes a major hit. 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
No. But I think, see, eventually, even the Chinese or even the competition has to raise price at 
some point in time. I mean -- but it depends on when are they raising because I don't want to be 
the first one to raise and lose market share. 
Arun Prasath: 
Got it. Understood. And second, on HALS, you said that eventually we'll be allocating more of 
our capital into these. So in terms of product portfolio, anything else we are missing before we're 
getting into the venture into the same de-bottlenecking of the existing products? 

 
Clean Science and Technology Limited 
 
October 31, 2026 
 
Page 7 of 9 
 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
Sorry, I didn't get your question. So the incremental investment is not too heavy because, see, 
ultimately, it earlier was a greenfield project. Now it is more of adding lines -- so now the capex’s 
are not very heavy. 
 
So -- and these are particular products which we believe now we are ready to start offering to 
the market. Say, for instance, a product like 2020. We did a lot of trials. We did some commercial 
trials on plant. And now we believe we have to put up a 1,000 ton line, and we will do so and 
the plant should start by April or May. So these are all advanced version of HALS. 
Arun Prasath: 
Understood. Any indication what is our percentage of advanced, excluding 701 and 770, what 
percentage of the portfolio is from the other HALS currently? Earlier, it used to be 70%, 80%. 
If you can indicate where we are at this point? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
60% is still 770 and 40% is now the advanced HALS. And I think this ratio will keep changing 
as we move quarter-on-quarter basis. 
Arun Prasath: 
Understood. And any idea when we will be able to achieve the -- at what realization level we 
should be targeting higher margins for the HALS portfolio from the current levels? I'm sure this 
is not our steady-state margins. 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
So basically, again, like I think every quarter-on-quarter, we should see improvement because 
the higher grade of HALS will start seeing picking up. So as this movement will start happening 
quarter-on-quarter basis, but the margins will also keep improving quarter-on-quarter. 
 
Number two, as we are getting into the backward integration of making the key precursors, also 
that will help in improving our margins in those particular products of HALS. 
Arun Prasath: 
Understood. Got it. Finally, one question on capex. What will be our full year capex this year 
and probably for FY28, how much we intend to spend? 
Pratik Bora: 
Arun, not much capex now because Performance Chemicals is largely funded. For the 
adjacencies of the pipelines, which Siddharth just alluded to, once we have the investment case 
approved by the Board, we will arrive at the capex number. 
Moderator: 
The next question is from the line of Abhijit Akella from KIE. 
Abhijit Akella: 
First on the phenol price difference between India and China, would you expect that the 
upcoming commissioning of Haldia Petrochemicals could possibly help to narrow the gap and 
bring phenol prices down in India? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
That is always the hope, but you don't know how that is going to pan out, right? 
Abhijit Akella: 
Okay. All right. Then on the HALS portfolio, is it correct that we have generated about 22% of 
this quarter's sales from HALS, so that would work out to about INR66 crores or so, just to 
confirm that number. And the volume number? 

 
Clean Science and Technology Limited 
 
October 31, 2026 
 
Page 8 of 9 
 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
More or less yes. 
Abhijit Akella: 
Yes, the volumes and how do you see the total volumes or utilization going this year and next 
year now? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
So currently, I think we are at about 30%, 35% capacity utilization - 40%. And I think going 
forward, we expect that the coming few quarters, we should touch between 55% to 60% capacity 
utilization. So almost 50% increase. 
Abhijit Akella: 
Okay. Great. And this increase will largely come from the higher-end grades, is it? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
Yes. Absolutely. 
Abhijit Akella: 
Okay. Great. And just from an EBITDA margin trajectory perspective, any outlook you'd like 
to share there? I mean, where do you see it going once you're at 60%? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
Currently, with this whole macroeconomics and with these crude oil prices, I think it is very 
difficult to determine anything. 
Abhijit Akella: 
Yes. 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
So I would like to pass that. 
Abhijit Akella: 
Okay. And yes, sorry. The other one was yes, just on Performance Chemical 2, we are 
mentioning 3Q, we are commissioning the project. So any revenue trajectory you would like to 
sort of share this year, next year? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
So the Performance Chemical 2, the deadline, I mean we are hoping really to start the 
commercial production in Q4, so probably in the month of Jan, Feb. 
Abhijit Akella: 
Yes. In the first calendar year, is it possible to touch, say, 30%, 40% utilization, you would 
think? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
See, it is very difficult to say because this is a tricky product. It has to stabilize samples, 
customers, validation. So it's too preliminary to gauge at what extent we will reach that capacity 
utilization. But of course, the target is to touch 20%, 25% capacity utilization in the first year. 
Abhijit Akella: 
Okay. Understood. And just one last thing from me. The KSMs that you mentioned for HALS, 
how much of sort of increase in margins or backward integration will that lead to? Is it a very 
significant benefit from a margin perspective? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
It will not be very significant, but it will be very important for us because then it makes us -- I 
mean, import-free. I mean, we can then manufacture it and use it for ourselves. So there could 
be between 5%, 7% improvement in margins for those particular segment of HALS. 
Moderator: 
The next question is from the line of Sahil Bhavan from SD Investments. 

 
Clean Science and Technology Limited 
 
October 31, 2026 
 
Page 9 of 9 
 
Sahil Bhavan: 
Am I audible, sir? 
Moderator: 
Yes. 
Sahil Bhavan: 
Sir, I have one question about HALS capacity in total. Sir, so initially, we had a HALS capacity 
of 10,500 metric tons. Now we have HALS in advanced NOR HALS as well. And now we are 
talking about de-bottlenecking into further capacity. So in total, sir, where do you see us ending 
up in terms of the total HALS capacity, sir? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
Yes. HALS capacity as of now is close to 11,500 tons. With this NOR Collaboration Association, 
we would like to add incremental capacity only in the advanced grade of HALS. So that will 
take out our overall capacity to close to 12,500 tons. 
Sahil Bhavan: 
12,500 tons. And sir, I went through our annual report as well, and we are talking about the new 
antioxidant that we have commercialized Clean Antioxidant 962. So sir, can you throw some 
light on that? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
Yes, it's a new grade of antioxidant. Of course, we have started supplying some small quantities, 
but let it pick it up and then I think we will have more picture on it. Currently, I think we are 
making just about 500-odd tons, but it's still not as big as we wanted. So let it come up a little 
bit, then we will be able to get more information. 
Sahil Bhavan: 
Sir, can you throw some light on the capacity that we have put up on this in antioxidant? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
So, basically it is currently -- we have not put any capex for that. It is being manufactured within 
our current assets. 
Sahil Bhavan: 
Okay. And this is, sir, in our parent company, right? 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
Right. 
Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, we'll take that as the last question for today. I now hand the conference 
back to Mr. Siddharth Sikchi for closing comments. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Siddharth Sikchi: 
Thank you so much all for attending this conference. Wishing you all a Happy Diwali in advance 
and looking forward to connecting with you for the next quarterly reviews. Thank you so much. 
Moderator: 
Thank you, members of the management. Ladies and gentlemen, on behalf of Clean Science and 
Technology Limited, that concludes this conference. We thank you for joining us, and you may 
now disconnect your lines. Thank you.

KMEW completes acquisition of TSHD River Pearl 48 to support 
Large-Scale Maintenance Dredging Projects 
 
Mumbai, India, November 05, 2026: Knowledge Marine & Engineering Works Limited 
(KMEW) has completed the acquisition of River Pearl 48, a Trailing Suction Hopper Dredger 
(TSHD), at a capital cost of approximately ₹250 crore. The acquisition strengthens 
KMEW’s fleet and execution capacity for large-scale maintenance dredging projects. 
A River Pearl 48 is a self-propelled vessel that dredges while moving slowly over the 
seabed. 
1. Suction: Trailing pipes with dragheads are lowered to the seabed. Powerful pumps 
draw up a mixture of water and sediment. 
2. Hopper loading: The sediment settles in the vessel’s hopper while excess water flows 
out through overflow systems. 
3. Transport: Once loaded, the vessel sails to a designated disposal or reclamation area. 
4. Discharge: The dredged material is released through bottom doors, pumped ashore, 
or discharged by another method, depending on the project. 
The vessel then returns to the dredging area and repeats the cycle. 
With a maximum dredging depth of 36 m, River Pearl 48 has the potential to dredge 
approximately 8–10 million cubic metres per annum, subject to project conditions and 
deployment. The vessel is expected to support KMEW’s recently awarded three-year 
maintenance dredging contract at New Mangalore Port Authority (NMPA), involving 
principal post-monsoon dredging of 15.9 million cubic metres over three years. 
River Pearl 48 is scheduled for immediate deployment at New Mangalore Port, in time to 
support commencement of the maintenance dredging contract on 15 November 2026. 
The vessel’s Indian ownership, flag, classification and crew align with the Government of 
India’s objective of promoting Indian-owned and Indian-flagged vessels. The vessel falls 
within the ambit of the Right of First Refusal (RoFR) framework, supporting the 
preference for Indian vessels in eligible procurement processes.

Commenting on Successful acquisition of Trailing Suction Hopper Dredger River 
Pearl 48, Mr. Sujay Kewalramani, CEO of Knowledge Marine & Engineering Works 
Ltd said that,  
Completing the acquisition of River Pearl 48 is a major milestone in KMEW’s growth 
journey. With a capital investment of approximately ₹250 crore and the potential to 
dredge 8–10 million cubic metres annually, the vessel strengthens our capacity to 
execute large-scale maintenance dredging assignments. Its immediate deployment 
at New Mangalore Port will support our delivery commitments, while its capabilities 
create a platform for KMEW to explore opportunities in the defence dredging market. 
The vessel’s Indian flag, classification with the Indian Register of Shipping and 100% 
Indian crew reflect our commitment to strengthening India’s maritime capabilities. 
As KMEW grows, we will continue to train and employ Indian nationals, supporting 
the development of skilled talent in the maritime sector.” 
The acquisition reinforces KMEW’s focus on strengthening its marine asset base, 
developing Indian maritime talent and building the capabilities required to 
undertake larger and more technically demanding dredging projects.

KMEW completes acquisition of TSHD River Pearl 48 to support 
Large-Scale Maintenance Dredging Projects 
 
Mumbai, India, November 05, 2026: Knowledge Marine & Engineering Works Limited 
(KMEW) has completed the acquisition of River Pearl 48, a Trailing Suction Hopper Dredger 
(TSHD), at a capital cost of approximately ₹250 crore. The acquisition strengthens 
KMEW’s fleet and execution capacity for large-scale maintenance dredging projects. 
A River Pearl 48 is a self-propelled vessel that dredges while moving slowly over the 
seabed. 
1. Suction: Trailing pipes with dragheads are lowered to the seabed. Powerful pumps 
draw up a mixture of water and sediment. 
2. Hopper loading: The sediment settles in the vessel’s hopper while excess water flows 
out through overflow systems. 
3. Transport: Once loaded, the vessel sails to a designated disposal or reclamation area. 
4. Discharge: The dredged material is released through bottom doors, pumped ashore, 
or discharged by another method, depending on the project. 
The vessel then returns to the dredging area and repeats the cycle. 
With a maximum dredging depth of 36 m, River Pearl 48 has the potential to dredge 
approximately 8–10 million cubic metres per annum, subject to project conditions and 
deployment. The vessel is expected to support KMEW’s recently awarded three-year 
maintenance dredging contract at New Mangalore Port Authority (NMPA), involving 
principal post-monsoon dredging of 15.9 million cubic metres over three years. 
River Pearl 48 is scheduled for immediate deployment at New Mangalore Port, in time to 
support commencement of the maintenance dredging contract on 15 November 2026. 
The vessel’s Indian ownership, flag, classification and crew align with the Government of 
India’s objective of promoting Indian-owned and Indian-flagged vessels. The vessel falls 
within the ambit of the Right of First Refusal (RoFR) framework, supporting the 
preference for Indian vessels in eligible procurement processes.

Completing the acquisition of River Pearl 48 is a major milestone in KMEW’s growth

As KMEW grows, we will continue to train and employ Indian nationals, supporting

The acquisition reinforces KMEW’s focus on strengthening its marine asset base,

Q2/H1-FY27 Operational Highlights
Treatment Solutions:
▪
Change in the estimated cost to complete a few legacy projects in the Treatment Solutions segment has significantly impacted the Company financials for
this quarter.
▪
Turnover for Treatment solutions was impacted by the execution of certain high-value contracts being scheduled for H2. Dispatches to GCC markets were
delayed due to the ongoing Middle East crisis.
Industrial Products:
▪
Industrial Products delivered strong growth during the quarter, recording an increase of approximately 35% YoY.
Lifecycle Services:
▪
Lifecycle services recorded sequential growth during the quarter, while maintaining stable margins.
Specialty Chemicals:
▪
Specialty Chemicals recorded sequential and YoY improvement in turnover during the quarter.
▪
Margins remained under pressure due to input cost inflation arising from the West Asia crisis and costs associated with the Roha facility.
▪
Improved cost pass-through to customers is expected to support margin recovery in the coming months.
Consumer Products:
▪
Consumer Products segment continued to deliver strong volume growth during the quarter.
Other Updates:
▪
Our Advanced Digital solutions offerings is seeing encouraging response, and this segment will positively impact our financial profile in the future.
▪
The Company has significantly invested in strengthening the organisation structure in the overseas geographies. This has improved our market reach, and 
we expect the benefits to accrue in the coming months.

Treatment Solutions:
▪
In Treatment solutions segment, a strong order backlog and planned execution schedules are expected to drive an
improvement in H2 turnover, accompanied by a better margin profile.
Industrial Products:
▪
Healthy order inflows are expected to sustain the Industrial Products segment's growth momentum in the coming
quarters.
Specialty Chemicals:
▪
Offtake from the new resin manufacturing facility at Roha is gradually improving and is expected to contribute
increasingly to segment growth.
Consumer Products:
▪
Continued investments in the consumer products segment are aimed at significantly scaling up the business and
expanding its revenue base.

Q2/H1-FY27 Operational Highlights
Treatment Solutions:
▪
Change in the estimated cost to complete a few legacy projects in the Treatment Solutions segment has significantly impacted the Company financials for
this quarter.
▪
Turnover for Treatment solutions was impacted by the execution of certain high-value contracts being scheduled for H2. Dispatches to GCC markets were
delayed due to the ongoing Middle East crisis.
Industrial Products:
▪
Industrial Products delivered strong growth during the quarter, recording an increase of approximately 35% YoY.
Lifecycle Services:
▪
Lifecycle services recorded sequential growth during the quarter, while maintaining stable margins.
Specialty Chemicals:
▪
Specialty Chemicals recorded sequential and YoY improvement in turnover during the quarter.
▪
Margins remained under pressure due to input cost inflation arising from the West Asia crisis and costs associated with the Roha facility.
▪
Improved cost pass-through to customers is expected to support margin recovery in the coming months.
Consumer Products:
▪
Consumer Products segment continued to deliver strong volume growth during the quarter.
Other Updates:
▪
Our Advanced Digital solutions offerings is seeing encouraging response, and this segment will positively impact our financial profile in the future.
▪
The Company has significantly invested in strengthening the organisation structure in the overseas geographies. This has improved our market reach, and 
we expect the benefits to accrue in the coming months.

19
Future Growth Drivers
Treatment Solutions:
▪
In Treatment solutions segment, a strong order backlog and planned execution schedules are expected to drive an
improvement in H2 turnover, accompanied by a better margin profile.
Industrial Products:
▪
Healthy order inflows are expected to sustain the Industrial Products segment's growth momentum in the coming
quarters.
Specialty Chemicals:
▪
Offtake from the new resin manufacturing facility at Roha is gradually improving and is expected to contribute
increasingly to segment growth.
Consumer Products:
▪
Continued investments in the consumer products segment are aimed at significantly scaling up the business and
expanding its revenue base.

into definitive agreements to acquire Molycop Group (comprising direct and indirect subsidiaries of AIP MC Holdings LLC, including joint ventures) 
through a series of steps. 
The transaction was subjected to customary conditions precedent and approvals from regulatory authorities in various jurisdictions. Upon 
satisfaction of all such conditions and receipt of the requisite approvals, the transaction was completed on 1 June 2026 ("acquisition date"), where 
the Group has acquired controlling stake in Molycop Group. 
In connection with the acquisition of the Molycop Group, comprising the direct and indirect subsidiaries of AIP MC Holdings LLC, including its joint 
ventures, the Company engaged various consultants and legal advisors for commercial and legal due diligence and for preparing and negotiating 
transaction-related documentation.

Dear Sir/ Madam,  
 
Pursuant to the Regulation 8(2) of the of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 
(“PIT Regulations”), this is to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company at its Meeting 
held today i.e. on Thursday, 5th November 2026, inter alia, have considered and approved revision of 
the Code of Practices and Procedures for Fair Disclosure of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information 
(“Code’’). 
 
In compliance with the PIT Regulations, the revised Code is enclosed herewith and the same is being 
uploaded on the Company’s website at www.safaribags.com.  
 
For Safari Industries (India) Limited 
 
 
 
 
Abhijaat Sinha

SAFARI INDUSTRIES (INDIA) LIMITED 
 
 
 
CODE OF PRACTICES AND PROCEDURES 
FOR FAIR DISCLOSURE OF UNPUBLISHED PRICE SENSITIVE INFORMATION 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
CODE OF PRACTICES AND PROCEDURES FOR FAIR DISCLOSURE OF 
UNPUBLISHED PRICE SENSITIVE INFORMATION 
 
1. 
Preamble 
 
Safari Industries (India) Limited (the “Company”) endeavours to preserve the 
confidentiality of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information and is committed to 
transparency, fairness in dealing with all stakeholders and in ensuring adherence to all law 
and regulations in force. 
 
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 
2015, as may be amended from time to time (the “PIT Regulations”) require the Board of 
Directors of every listed company to formulate a code of practices and procedures for fair 
disclosure of unpublished price sensitive information in accordance with the principles 
set out in Schedule A to the PIT Regulations. 
 
This Code is framed pursuant to Regulation 8 read with Schedule A to the PIT 
Regulations and incorporates the policy for determination of legitimate purposes 
required under Regulation 3(2A) of the PIT Regulations. 
 
2. 
Definitions: 
 
For purposes of this Code,  
 
“Company” means Safari Industries (India) Limited  
 
“Board” means its Board of Directors.  
 
References to “UPSI” mean unpublished price sensitive information as defined under the 
PIT Regulations.  
 
Words and expressions used but not defined in this Code shall have the meanings 
respectively assigned to them under the PIT Regulations and the Company’s Internal Code 
of Conduct for Prevention of Insider Trading (“Insider Trading Code”), as amended from 
time to time. In the event of any inconsistency, the PIT Regulations shall prevail. 
 
3. 
Principles of fair disclosure for purposes of Code of Practices and Procedures for Fair 
Disclosure of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information: 
 
The Company is committed to fair and non-discriminatory disclosure of all Unpublished 
Price Sensitive Information and upholds the principles of information fairness, uniformity, 
and confidentiality for UPSI. 
 

The Company will adhere to the following principles to ensure fair disclosure of events 
and occurrence that could impact price of its Securities in the market: 
 
a) Prompt Disclosure: The Company will promptly disclose any UPSI that may impact 
price discovery as soon as credible and substantial information is available, making it 
‘generally available’ to the public on a non-discriminatory basis. 
 
b) Uniform Dissemination: The Company will strive to ensure uniform and universal 
dissemination of UPSI to prevent selective disclosures. 
 
c) The Company Secretary, serving as the Compliance Officer, is responsible for 
administering this code and should be contacted with any questions or concerns related 
to UPSI or the obligations herein. The Company Secretary shall act as chief investor 
relations officer to deal with dissemination of information and disclosure of UPSI. 
 
In the absence or unavailability of the Company Secretary, the Managing Director or 
the Chief Financial Officer or such other senior officer authorised by the Managing 
Director shall discharge the functions of the CIRO. 
 
d) Selective Disclosure: If any UPSI is disclosed selectively, inadvertently, or otherwise, 
the concerned employee must promptly inform the Compliance Officer of the incident. 
 
e) Fair Responses: The Company will provide accurate and fair responses to regulatory 
inquiries about news reports and market rumours. 
 
f) Analyst and Investor Engagements: The Company will ensure that information 
shared with analysts and research personnel does not contain UPSI. Authorized 
representatives will attend meetings with analysts, media, and institutional investors. 
Unanticipated questions may be deferred for later response, with a public 
announcement preceding any answer involving UPSI.  
 
g) Documentation and Access: Best practices will be implemented to post transcripts 
or records of meetings with analysts and investor conferences on the Company’s 
website, providing official confirmation and documentation of disclosures. 
 
h) Third-Party Disclosures: UPSI shared with third parties, such as lenders, customers, 
suppliers, merchant bankers, legal advisors, and auditors, will be done only for 
Legitimate Purposes as necessary to fulfill their duties and responsibilities to the 
Company. 
 
i) Need-to-Know Principle: The Company will engage with third parties for Legitimate 
Purposes, ensuring adherence to the ‘need-to-know’ principle. Recipients of UPSI will 
be required to sign Non-Disclosure Agreements / confidentiality agreements in 
accordance with current policy. 

 
j) Digital Record: The Company will maintain a digital database recording the details 
of individuals or entities who have shared the UPSI as well as with whom UPSI is 
shared. Any Designated Person who is sharing any UPSI for Legitimate Purpose or in 
the ordinary course of business with other employees, collaborators, lenders, 
customers, suppliers, merchant bankers, legal advisors, auditors, insolvency 
professions or other advisors or consultants shall make an entry in the Structured 
Digital Database platform used by the Company. 
 
4. Policy for determination of “Legitimate Purposes”: 
 
4.1. General rule. This policy is framed pursuant to Regulations 3(2A) and 3(2B) of the 
PIT Regulations and forms part of this Code. UPSI may be shared only in furtherance of a 
Legitimate Purpose, performance of duties or discharge of legal obligations and only where 
such sharing is not intended to evade or circumvent the prohibitions of the PIT Regulations. 
 
4.2. Case-by-case assessment. Whether a proposed sharing of UPSI is for a Legitimate 
Purpose shall be determined on a case-by-case basis, having regard to the facts and 
circumstances, including whether: (a) the proposed sharing is in furtherance of a genuine 
corporate, business or statutory purpose; (b) sharing the UPSI is necessary to achieve that 
purpose; (c) the nature and extent of UPSI proposed to be shared is proportionate to and 
commensurate with that purpose; and (d) the proposed recipient has a genuine need to 
access the information and appropriate safeguards can be implemented to maintain 
confidentiality and prevent misuse.  
 
The fact that a purpose falls within an illustrative category below shall not, by itself, make 
the sharing a legitimate purpose. 
 
(a) To comply with applicable laws, regulations, regulatory directions or requirements, or 
pursuant to any investigation, inquiry, legal proceedings or order of a court, tribunal 
or governmental or statutory authority; 
(b) To obtain or provide professional, audit, legal, financial, merchant banking, valuation, 
consulting or other expert services or for performance of statutory or fiduciary duties; 
(c) To pursue or perform specific business or contractual arrangements, including sharing 
with lenders, customers, suppliers, collaborators, business partners or other 
counterparties where UPSI is reasonably necessary for the relevant transaction or 
activity; 
(d) To evaluate, negotiate or implement strategic or corporate transactions, including 
acquisitions, mergers, amalgamations, restructuring or other business opportunities. 
 
Any person in receipt of UPSI pursuant to a Legitimate Purposes shall be considered as an 
“Insider” for the purpose of the Regulations. The person sharing the UPSI shall give the 
recipient due notice, in writing, that the information constitutes UPSI and that the recipient 

is required to maintain its confidentiality and comply with the PIT Regulations, including 
the restriction on trading in the Company’s securities while in possession of UPSI. 
 
The recipient shall use UPSI only for the approved purpose and shall not further disclose 
it except as permitted by the PIT Regulations. Where Regulation 3(4) applies, the parties 
shall execute the prescribed confidentiality and non-disclosure agreements. 
 
Any communication, provision of or access to UPSI, or procurement of UPSI, in 
connection with a transaction covered by Regulation 3(3) shall be undertaken only in 
accordance with that Regulation. 
 
5. Review, amendment and publication: 
 
The Board may review and amend this Code from time to time. If any amendment, 
clarification or other regulatory requirement is inconsistent with this Code, the applicable 
law shall prevail and this Code shall be updated accordingly. This Code and every 
amendment thereto shall be published on the Company’s official website and promptly 
intimated to the stock exchanges in accordance with Regulation 8(2) of the PIT 
Regulations.

(“PIT Regulations”), this is to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company at its Meeting

CODE OF PRACTICES AND PROCEDURES FOR FAIR DISCLOSURE OF 
UNPUBLISHED PRICE SENSITIVE INFORMATION 
 
1. 
Preamble 
 
Safari Industries (India) Limited (the “Company”) endeavours to preserve the 
confidentiality of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information and is committed to 
transparency, fairness in dealing with all stakeholders and in ensuring adherence to all law 
and regulations in force. 
 
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 
2015, as may be amended from time to time (the “PIT Regulations”) require the Board of 
Directors of every listed company to formulate a code of practices and procedures for fair 
disclosure of unpublished price sensitive information in accordance with the principles 
set out in Schedule A to the PIT Regulations. 
 
This Code is framed pursuant to Regulation 8 read with Schedule A to the PIT 
Regulations and incorporates the policy for determination of legitimate purposes 
required under Regulation 3(2A) of the PIT Regulations. 
 
2. 
Definitions: 
 
For purposes of this Code,  
 
“Company” means Safari Industries (India) Limited  
 
“Board” means its Board of Directors.  
 
References to “UPSI” mean unpublished price sensitive information as defined under the 
PIT Regulations.  
 
Words and expressions used but not defined in this Code shall have the meanings 
respectively assigned to them under the PIT Regulations and the Company’s Internal Code 
of Conduct for Prevention of Insider Trading (“Insider Trading Code”), as amended from 
time to time. In the event of any inconsistency, the PIT Regulations shall prevail. 
 
3. 
Principles of fair disclosure for purposes of Code of Practices and Procedures for Fair 
Disclosure of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information: 
 
The Company is committed to fair and non-discriminatory disclosure of all Unpublished 
Price Sensitive Information and upholds the principles of information fairness, uniformity, 
and confidentiality for UPSI. 
 

The Company will adhere to the following principles to ensure fair disclosure of events 
and occurrence that could impact price of its Securities in the market: 
 
a) Prompt Disclosure: The Company will promptly disclose any UPSI that may impact 
price discovery as soon as credible and substantial information is available, making it 
‘generally available’ to the public on a non-discriminatory basis. 
 
b) Uniform Dissemination: The Company will strive to ensure uniform and universal 
dissemination of UPSI to prevent selective disclosures. 
 
c) The Company Secretary, serving as the Compliance Officer, is responsible for 
administering this code and should be contacted with any questions or concerns related 
to UPSI or the obligations herein. The Company Secretary shall act as chief investor 
relations officer to deal with dissemination of information and disclosure of UPSI. 
 
In the absence or unavailability of the Company Secretary, the Managing Director or 
the Chief Financial Officer or such other senior officer authorised by the Managing 
Director shall discharge the functions of the CIRO. 
 
d) Selective Disclosure: If any UPSI is disclosed selectively, inadvertently, or otherwise, 
the concerned employee must promptly inform the Compliance Officer of the incident. 
 
e) Fair Responses: The Company will provide accurate and fair responses to regulatory 
inquiries about news reports and market rumours. 
 
f) Analyst and Investor Engagements: The Company will ensure that information 
shared with analysts and research personnel does not contain UPSI. Authorized 
representatives will attend meetings with analysts, media, and institutional investors. 
Unanticipated questions may be deferred for later response, with a public 
announcement preceding any answer involving UPSI.  
 
g) Documentation and Access: Best practices will be implemented to post transcripts 
or records of meetings with analysts and investor conferences on the Company’s 
website, providing official confirmation and documentation of disclosures. 
 
h) Third-Party Disclosures: UPSI shared with third parties, such as lenders, customers, 
suppliers, merchant bankers, legal advisors, and auditors, will be done only for 
Legitimate Purposes as necessary to fulfill their duties and responsibilities to the 
Company. 
 
i) Need-to-Know Principle: The Company will engage with third parties for Legitimate 
Purposes, ensuring adherence to the ‘need-to-know’ principle. Recipients of UPSI will 
be required to sign Non-Disclosure Agreements / confidentiality agreements in 
accordance with current policy. 

 
j) Digital Record: The Company will maintain a digital database recording the details 
of individuals or entities who have shared the UPSI as well as with whom UPSI is 
shared. Any Designated Person who is sharing any UPSI for Legitimate Purpose or in 
the ordinary course of business with other employees, collaborators, lenders, 
customers, suppliers, merchant bankers, legal advisors, auditors, insolvency 
professions or other advisors or consultants shall make an entry in the Structured 
Digital Database platform used by the Company. 
 
4. Policy for determination of “Legitimate Purposes”: 
 
4.1. General rule. This policy is framed pursuant to Regulations 3(2A) and 3(2B) of the 
PIT Regulations and forms part of this Code. UPSI may be shared only in furtherance of a 
Legitimate Purpose, performance of duties or discharge of legal obligations and only where 
such sharing is not intended to evade or circumvent the prohibitions of the PIT Regulations. 
 
4.2. Case-by-case assessment. Whether a proposed sharing of UPSI is for a Legitimate 
Purpose shall be determined on a case-by-case basis, having regard to the facts and 
circumstances, including whether: (a) the proposed sharing is in furtherance of a genuine 
corporate, business or statutory purpose; (b) sharing the UPSI is necessary to achieve that 
purpose; (c) the nature and extent of UPSI proposed to be shared is proportionate to and 
commensurate with that purpose; and (d) the proposed recipient has a genuine need to 
access the information and appropriate safeguards can be implemented to maintain 
confidentiality and prevent misuse.  
 
The fact that a purpose falls within an illustrative category below shall not, by itself, make 
the sharing a legitimate purpose. 
 
(a) To comply with applicable laws, regulations, regulatory directions or requirements, or 
pursuant to any investigation, inquiry, legal proceedings or order of a court, tribunal 
or governmental or statutory authority; 
(b) To obtain or provide professional, audit, legal, financial, merchant banking, valuation, 
consulting or other expert services or for performance of statutory or fiduciary duties; 
(c) To pursue or perform specific business or contractual arrangements, including sharing 
with lenders, customers, suppliers, collaborators, business partners or other 
counterparties where UPSI is reasonably necessary for the relevant transaction or 
activity; 
(d) To evaluate, negotiate or implement strategic or corporate transactions, including 
acquisitions, mergers, amalgamations, restructuring or other business opportunities. 
 
Any person in receipt of UPSI pursuant to a Legitimate Purposes shall be considered as an 
“Insider” for the purpose of the Regulations. The person sharing the UPSI shall give the 
recipient due notice, in writing, that the information constitutes UPSI and that the recipient 

is required to maintain its confidentiality and comply with the PIT Regulations, including 
the restriction on trading in the Company’s securities while in possession of UPSI. 
 
The recipient shall use UPSI only for the approved purpose and shall not further disclose 
it except as permitted by the PIT Regulations. Where Regulation 3(4) applies, the parties 
shall execute the prescribed confidentiality and non-disclosure agreements. 
 
Any communication, provision of or access to UPSI, or procurement of UPSI, in 
connection with a transaction covered by Regulation 3(3) shall be undertaken only in 
accordance with that Regulation. 
 
5. Review, amendment and publication: 
 
The Board may review and amend this Code from time to time. If any amendment, 
clarification or other regulatory requirement is inconsistent with this Code, the applicable 
law shall prevail and this Code shall be updated accordingly. This Code and every 
amendment thereto shall be published on the Company’s official website and promptly 
intimated to the stock exchanges in accordance with Regulation 8(2) of the PIT 
Regulations.

APPENDIX

Revenue from Operations
Revenue recognised from the sale of products and services in accordance 
with Ind AS 115.
PAT / PAT Margin (%)
PAT refers to profit/loss for the relevant year after tax. PAT Margin (%) is 
calculated as profit/loss for the relevant year divided by Total income for the 
relevant year, expressed as a percentage.
Gross Profit / Gross Margin (%)
Gross Profit is Revenue from operations minus direct costs, which includes cloud 
infrastructure expenses, purchase of traded goods, and employee benefit 
expenses attributable to Support and Managed Services. Gross Margin (%) is 
Gross Profit divided by Revenue from operations, expressed as a percentage.
Adjusted Operating Cash Flow
Operating cash flow as reported under Ind AS 7, excluding the cash impact of 
non-recurring items including the pre-IPO ESOP and SAR buyback settlement 
and IPO-related transaction costs.
Adjusted EBITDA
Adjusted EBITDA is Revenue from Operations minus Direct Costs and Indirect 
costs. Indirect costs include expenses relating to Sales & Marketing, Research 
and Development, Customer Success and General and Administrative 
Expenses. Adjusted EBITDA does not include ESOP costs, Interest Income, Taxes, 
Depreciation and/or Amortization related charges.
Free Cash Flow / Adjusted Free Cash Flow
Free Cash Flow is Operating Cash Flow less capital expenditure. Adjusted Free 
Cash Flow is Adjusted Operating Cash Flow less capital expenditure for the 
reporting period.
Adjusted EBITDA Margin (%)
Adjusted EBITDA for the relevant year divided by Revenue from operations for 
the relevant year, expressed as a percentage.
Constant Currency Growth
Underlying growth excluding the effect of foreign currency rate fluctuations. 
Current-period revenue from contracts denominated in currencies other than 
INR is translated using the average exchange rates of the comparative period.
Annexure A: Definitions of Key Terms (Financial)
amagi 20
APPENDIX

Net Revenue Retention (NRR) Rate
NRR Rate (%) is computed as Revenue from operations for the current Fiscal 
from all customers existing at the end of the previous Fiscal, divided by 
Revenue from operations generated from the same customers in the previous

PAT / PAT Margin (%)
PAT refers to profit/loss for the relevant year after tax. PAT Margin (%) is

Gross Profit / Gross Margin (%)
Gross Profit is Revenue from operations minus direct costs, which includes cloud 
infrastructure expenses, purchase of traded goods, and employee benefit 
expenses attributable to Support and Managed Services. Gross Margin (%) is 
Gross Profit divided by Revenue from operations, expressed as a percentage.
Adjusted Operating Cash Flow
Operating cash flow as reported under Ind AS 7, excluding the cash impact of 
non-recurring items including the pre-IPO ESOP and SAR buyback settlement 
and IPO-related transaction costs.
Adjusted EBITDA
Adjusted EBITDA is Revenue from Operations minus Direct Costs and Indirect 
costs. Indirect costs include expenses relating to Sales & Marketing, Research 
and Development, Customer Success and General and Administrative 
Expenses. Adjusted EBITDA does not include ESOP costs, Interest Income, Taxes, 
Depreciation and/or Amortization related charges.
Free Cash Flow / Adjusted Free Cash Flow
Free Cash Flow is Operating Cash Flow less capital expenditure. Adjusted Free 
Cash Flow is Adjusted Operating Cash Flow less capital expenditure for the 
reporting period.
Adjusted EBITDA Margin (%)
Adjusted EBITDA for the relevant year divided by Revenue from operations for 
the relevant year, expressed as a percentage.
Constant Currency Growth
Underlying growth excluding the effect of foreign currency rate fluctuations. 
Current-period revenue from contracts denominated in currencies other than 
INR is translated using the average exchange rates of the comparative period.

2. CEO’s Address 
Dear Shareholders, 
Two years ago, in this same quarter, Amagi nearly broke even at the Adjusted EBITDA level. Revenue 
this quarter was ₹476 Cr against ₹278 Cr then, 1.7 times in two years. Adjusted EBITDA margin moved 
from just below zero to 18.7%. We turned operating cash flow from an outflow into a meaningful inflow 
(₹134 Cr this quarter), and closed with ₹1,774 Cr of cash and no debt. Growth, profitability and cash 
have moved together. This is a deliberate choice, and one we intend to maintain. 
Streaming is now half of US television viewing. Viewers moved first. Advertising followed. Operations, 
where our solutions deliver, are moving now. The theme is unification. Customers who ran broadcast, 
FAST and VOD separately now want creation, distribution and monetization on one platform. We 
heard this at LA PLAY, our own conference in Los Angeles, previously LA FAST, from the 700-plus 
customers and partners who joined us. The platform they want to consolidate onto is what we 
announced at LA PLAY as the Amagi Media Industry Cloud. 
We are making three bets. 
a.​ Cost efficiencies: our customers spend more on people than on technology to keep channels 
on air. We launched agentic network operations. Agents run the workflow, people take the 
decisions. 
b.​ Audience expansion: our customers want to extend into social platforms. Mobile-first, vertical 
solutions matter. A leading US broadcast group went live with Amagi NEWSPULSE to 
summarize news for its national newsroom. Alongside NEWSPULSE, we introduced FANPULSE 
for live sport on social networks, STUDIO for live production, and integrated localization for 
local access and language. 
c.​ Revenue maximization: content owners, distributors and advertisers need to find each other 
and transact. Our ads and content marketplace connects them.  
We launched four products this quarter, across IBC in Amsterdam and LA PLAY, one under cost 
efficiencies and three under audience expansion. NEWSPULSE was recognized twice at IBC. IDC 
named us a Leader in its MarketScape for the AI-driven business cycle in media. These are early. We 
shall scale them, and show you where each one stands every quarter. 
Our north star does not change. Amagi is built to be an enduring engine of innovation for the media 
industry, bringing our customers technology that maximizes their revenues and improves their cost 
efficiency. The three bets above are this quarter’s expression of it. The opportunity ahead is larger 
than what we have taken so far. Executing through it in a disciplined way is where I spend most of my 
time, and the only thing I am paranoid of. 
Thank you, as always, for your trust and partnership. 
Baskar Subramanian​
Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer

4. FAQs  
In this section, we address key questions about our Q2/H1 FY27 performance and business outlook, 
shaped by our assessment of what matters most this quarter and by the valuable feedback we 
continue to receive through ongoing investor and analyst dialogue. 
Quarter Overview 
Q1: How would you summarise this quarter's performance? 
Q2 FY27 was a strong quarter, with revenue reaching a record ₹475.8 Cr, up 27% Y/Y (15% CC growth). 
Growth was led by Streaming Unification (+35% Y/Y) and Monetization & Marketplace (+28% Y/Y). 
Cloud Modernization grew 9% Y/Y against a prior-year base that included revenue recognition from a large 
broadcaster migration, as disclosed in our previous earnings calls. Excluding this base effect, Cloud 
Modernization growth would have been 36% Y/Y, while overall revenue growth would have been 33% 
Y/Y (21% CC growth). For H1 FY27, revenue grew 30% Y/Y to ₹912.7 Cr (18% CC growth), supported by 
customers launching additional channels, expanding distribution across platforms, and deepening 
their engagement with Amagi. 
Adjusted EBITDA grew 114% Y/Y to ₹89.1 Cr, with margin expanding 7.6 ppts Y/Y to 18.7%, driven by 
continued operating leverage in R&D, S&M & CS, and G&A. Gross margin improved 0.8 ppts 
sequentially to 68.1%, while declining 1.6 ppts Y/Y on a reported basis. Excluding the previously 
discussed revenue-recognition effect from the large broadcaster migration, gross margin would 
have been broadly flat Y/Y. For H1 FY27, Adjusted EBITDA grew 139% Y/Y to ₹139.2 Cr, with margin 
expanding 7.0 ppts Y/Y to 15.3%. 
PAT reached ₹74.8 Cr, with margin expanding 14.3 ppts Y/Y to 14.9%, supported by higher Adjusted 
EBITDA, lower ESOP-related expenses, and a lower effective tax rate. 
Cash conversion improved, with H1 FY27 Adjusted OCF reaching ₹94 Cr, representing 67% of Adjusted 
EBITDA.

Q2 marked an important milestone in our AI journey. At IBC 2026, we unveiled four new AI products: 
Amagi STUDIO, FANPULSE, Integrated Localization, and Agentic Network Operations. Together with

engagement, and network operations. These capabilities build on our integrated platform, helping 
media companies simplify operations, reach more audiences, and generate greater value from their 
content. 
Our broader approach to AI also received important industry recognition, with IDC naming Amagi a 
Leader in its 2026 MarketScape assessment of the AI-driven business cycle in the media industry. 
The recognition is particularly relevant as media companies increasingly look to integrate AI across 
their operations, rather than adopt standalone tools. NEWSPULSE also received two industry awards: 
TVTech Best of Show at IBC 2026 and Best Use of Agentic AI in Media at the CSI Awards 2026. 
We also hosted our flagship customer event in Los Angeles, strategically rebranded this year as LA

with senior leaders accounting for 41% of participants. The event underscored a broader industry 
shift: traditional television, FAST, and VOD are increasingly converging, with content owners focused 
on reaching audiences across formats and capturing a greater share of viewing time.  
Customer activity remained strong across our core businesses. Broadcasters and streaming 
platforms across the US, Middle East, and APAC adopted and expanded their use of Amagi to launch 
additional channels and extend distribution, expand monetization capabilities, and modernize 
broadcast operations.

Market & Customers 
Q3: What industry trends are shaping the growth opportunity across our business? 
As previously established, our TAM of approximately $17 Bn across our three core segments provides 
a massive runway, which AI has the potential to nearly double over time by automating manual 
media workflows. ​
Four key industry tailwinds underpin this opportunity: the shift in viewing to streaming, advertising 
spend following streaming audiences, increasing cloud adoption for broadcast operations, and the 
integration of AI across media workflows. These trends continue to shape customer needs and 
create opportunities across our platform. 
Streaming Viewership Growth: Streaming viewership share reached a record 49.6% of US TV viewing 
in August 2026, up 3.2 ppts Y/Y again exceeding the combined share of broadcast and cable. Live 
sports continued to anchor the shift to streaming this quarter, driven by major events, from the FIFA 
World Cup to the new football season in the US. Within streaming, FAST continues to play an 
established role, accounting for ~10% of total streaming time. As content owners distribute 
programming across traditional TV, FAST, and streaming platforms, managing separate workflows 
becomes increasingly complex. Amagi's end-to-end platform simplifies these operations, allowing 
customers to centrally prepare and manage content while distributing it across multiple platforms. 
CTV Ad Spend Growth: Advertising budgets continue to follow viewers onto streaming. US CTV ad 
spend is projected to reach roughly $37.5 billion in 2026, up about 19% Y/Y. Yet streaming accounts 
for about 49% of US TV viewing, compared with roughly 42% of TV ad spend, leaving further room for 
growth. With ad-supported tiers expanding and programmatic buying accounting for nearly 90% of 
CTV ad spending, content owners increasingly need to match ad inventory with advertiser demand 
and maximize revenue from every impression across platforms. This creates a strong tailwind for 
Amagi's Monetization & Marketplace business. 
Broadcast operations shifting to Cloud: Broadcast and cable (collectively referred to as linear TV) 
still account for a meaningful share of US TV viewing, at 36.4% in August 2026, down 5.2 ppts Y/Y. 
Despite the decline in viewership, linear TV remains a significant profit pool, and broadcasters are 
focused on operating it at lower cost by moving their playout infrastructure from on-premises 
hardware to the cloud. Cloud playout now accounts for 10.2% of linear channels worldwide, up 4.5

AI permeating Media Workflows: AI is moving from pilots into production across specific media

Q4: Around 90% of broadcast media operations still run on on-premise infrastructure. What could 
accelerate the migration to the cloud? 
The opportunity remains compelling, with a long runway, but cloud migration is not simply a 
technology-replacement decision. Broadcasters depend on these systems to keep channels running 
continuously, and existing infrastructure typically operates on long replacement cycles. We see three 
factors that could accelerate adoption:  
●​
Hardware Renewals & Consolidation: Migrations rarely happen mid-cycle. Broadcasters 
aggressively evaluate cloud alternatives when existing physical hardware reaches 
end-of-life, or when station groups consolidate and need to quickly centralise master control. 
●​
Compelling Economics & Agility: Cloud playout materially lowers five-year total cost of 
ownership. It also gives broadcasters the agility to spin up FAST channels, test new formats, 
or enter new markets without massive upfront capital expenditure. 
●​
Proven Reliability: Because broadcast operations have zero margin for error, customers 
usually build confidence through phased deployments, starting with disaster recovery or a 
few select markets before migrating their core operations. 
Because these enterprise-grade transformations involve lengthy decision cycles, phased rollouts, 
and milestone-based revenue recognition, we continue to view Cloud Modernization as a multi-year 
growth engine rather than a linear quarterly metric. Full-year performance will remain the most 
accurate measure of our progress 
Q5: How did market trends translate into customer activity for us in Q2 FY27? 
One of the most consistent themes in our customer conversations is the growing unification of 
broadcast and streaming workflows. As broadcasters move their existing channel operations to the 
cloud, they gain the flexibility to launch FAST channels and reach additional streaming platforms 
without building separate playout workflows for each destination. Q2 provided further evidence of 
this shift, from large broadcast migrations to new ways of reaching audiences. 
The broadcast migrations are an important starting point. The local news network of a major US 
cable operator moved live newsroom playout in two markets to Amagi CLOUDPORT and is now 
9 

 
scaling to 60 regional feeds across more than 30 markets. A leading Middle East entertainment 
network chose CLOUDPORT to replace its on-premise playout across 15 channels, bringing 
scheduling, graphics, and automation onto the cloud. Both deployments illustrate how broadcasters 
are moving core channel operations onto cloud infrastructure, creating the foundation for broader 
distribution opportunities over time. 
At the streaming unification end, we are also seeing new viewership formats and destinations 
emerge. KT Studio Genie, part of South Korea's KT Group, migrated 16 FAST channels to Amagi without 
downtime and launched Genie Shorts, bringing mobile-first vertical-video content onto connected 
TVs through FAST. Its unified playout setup enables it to reach additional platforms without separate 
playout workflows. 
In Monetization & Marketplace, customers are looking to generate more revenue from existing 
content and advertising inventory. Scripps, a major US broadcaster with more than 60 local stations, 
expanded its use of THUNDERSTORM and ADS PLUS to introduce in-content advertising within its Tablo 
streaming app. NDTV, one of India's leading news broadcasters, adopted Amagi AdFlow Orchestrator 
to convert long linear ad breaks into shorter, platform-specific formats for FAST and CTV, creating 
more monetization opportunities without changing its feeds. 
Existing customer relationships are also extending into AI. A leading US broadcast group is using 
Amagi NEWSPULSE’s AI summarization capabilities to create programming for distribution on its 
national news channels. 
Product Strategy & Outlook 
Q6: Beyond our three segments, where are we investing for the next phase of growth?  
We see a significant opportunity to improve the economics of media operations and generate more 
value from the content our customers already produce. Our position across the glass-to-glass value 
chain provides a foundation to pursue three major growth opportunities: cost efficiencies, audience 
expansion, and revenue maximization: 
●​
Cost Efficiencies: As discussed in our Q1 FY27 call, media companies typically spend $2 to $4 
on people for every $1 spent on technology, primarily on routine operations. We are 
aggressively addressing this imbalance. Through AI Smart Scheduler, Agentic Network 
Operations, and our broader shift toward agent-led media ops, AI now handles routine 
execution while humans retain strategic control. This lets us manage more channels and 
capture in-house workflows, expanding our reach beyond traditional outsourcing.​
 
●​
Audience Expansion: With social media now capturing 54% of US video ad spending, content 
owners must look beyond traditional TV. Historically, adapting a single live broadcast into 
multi-format social content required significant editorial effort. Products like NEWSPULSE (for 
news), FANPULSE (for sports), and Amagi STUDIO demonstrate how AI can instantly transform 
live feeds into short-form, vertical stories. This allows our customers to reach entirely new 
audiences without a proportional increase in production costs. ​

What connects these opportunities is the content, customer relationships, and distribution network

Q7: How are AI agents transforming managed services?   
In managed services, channel operations are largely end-to-end and manual, from preparing 
content, building schedules, and running live events to monitoring feeds and resolving faults as they 
occur. In the current model, adding channels means adding people. 
Amagi Intella takes an AI-first approach to managed services, combining AI agents with human 
operators. The agents handle specific, repetitive work, such as monitoring channels, diagnosing 
faults, building schedules, inserting ad breaks, and increasingly resolving issues within defined 
parameters on their own. Anything outside those parameters is escalated to the human operators. 
This frees people from routine execution, allowing them to focus on judgement and 
decision-making.

from diagnosing faults to resolving known ones, we expect operators to manage more channels

Four key industry tailwinds underpin this opportunity: the shift in viewing to streaming, advertising

integration of AI across media workflows. These trends continue to shape customer needs and 
create opportunities across our platform. 
Streaming Viewership Growth: Streaming viewership share reached a record 49.6% of US TV viewing

World Cup to the new football season in the US. Within streaming, FAST continues to play an 
established role, accounting for ~10% of total streaming time. As content owners distribute 
programming across traditional TV, FAST, and streaming platforms, managing separate workflows 
becomes increasingly complex. Amagi's end-to-end platform simplifies these operations, allowing 
customers to centrally prepare and manage content while distributing it across multiple platforms.

spend is projected to reach roughly $37.5 billion in 2026, up about 19% Y/Y. Yet streaming accounts

Q4: Around 90% of broadcast media operations still run on on-premise infrastructure. What could 
accelerate the migration to the cloud? 
The opportunity remains compelling, with a long runway, but cloud migration is not simply a 
technology-replacement decision. Broadcasters depend on these systems to keep channels running 
continuously, and existing infrastructure typically operates on long replacement cycles. We see three 
factors that could accelerate adoption:  
●​
Hardware Renewals & Consolidation: Migrations rarely happen mid-cycle. Broadcasters 
aggressively evaluate cloud alternatives when existing physical hardware reaches 
end-of-life, or when station groups consolidate and need to quickly centralise master control. 
●​
Compelling Economics & Agility: Cloud playout materially lowers five-year total cost of 
ownership. It also gives broadcasters the agility to spin up FAST channels, test new formats, 
or enter new markets without massive upfront capital expenditure. 
●​
Proven Reliability: Because broadcast operations have zero margin for error, customers 
usually build confidence through phased deployments, starting with disaster recovery or a 
few select markets before migrating their core operations. 
Because these enterprise-grade transformations involve lengthy decision cycles, phased rollouts, 
and milestone-based revenue recognition, we continue to view Cloud Modernization as a multi-year 
growth engine rather than a linear quarterly metric. Full-year performance will remain the most 
accurate measure of our progress

scheduling, graphics, and automation onto the cloud. Both deployments illustrate how broadcasters 
are moving core channel operations onto cloud infrastructure, creating the foundation for broader 
distribution opportunities over time. 
At the streaming unification end, we are also seeing new viewership formats and destinations 
emerge. KT Studio Genie, part of South Korea's KT Group, migrated 16 FAST channels to Amagi without 
downtime and launched Genie Shorts, bringing mobile-first vertical-video content onto connected 
TVs through FAST. Its unified playout setup enables it to reach additional platforms without separate 
playout workflows. 
In Monetization & Marketplace, customers are looking to generate more revenue from existing 
content and advertising inventory. Scripps, a major US broadcaster with more than 60 local stations, 
expanded its use of THUNDERSTORM and ADS PLUS to introduce in-content advertising within its Tablo 
streaming app. NDTV, one of India's leading news broadcasters, adopted Amagi AdFlow Orchestrator 
to convert long linear ad breaks into shorter, platform-specific formats for FAST and CTV, creating 
more monetization opportunities without changing its feeds. 
Existing customer relationships are also extending into AI. A leading US broadcast group is using 
Amagi NEWSPULSE’s AI summarization capabilities to create programming for distribution on its 
national news channels. 
Product Strategy & Outlook 
Q6: Beyond our three segments, where are we investing for the next phase of growth?  
We see a significant opportunity to improve the economics of media operations and generate more 
value from the content our customers already produce. Our position across the glass-to-glass value 
chain provides a foundation to pursue three major growth opportunities: cost efficiencies, audience 
expansion, and revenue maximization: 
●​
Cost Efficiencies: As discussed in our Q1 FY27 call, media companies typically spend $2 to $4 
on people for every $1 spent on technology, primarily on routine operations. We are 
aggressively addressing this imbalance. Through AI Smart Scheduler, Agentic Network 
Operations, and our broader shift toward agent-led media ops, AI now handles routine 
execution while humans retain strategic control. This lets us manage more channels and 
capture in-house workflows, expanding our reach beyond traditional outsourcing.​
 
●​
Audience Expansion: With social media now capturing 54% of US video ad spending, content 
owners must look beyond traditional TV. Historically, adapting a single live broadcast into 
multi-format social content required significant editorial effort. Products like NEWSPULSE (for 
news), FANPULSE (for sports), and Amagi STUDIO demonstrate how AI can instantly transform 
live feeds into short-form, vertical stories. This allows our customers to reach entirely new 
audiences without a proportional increase in production costs. ​

Amagi delivers record quarterly revenue of ₹476 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 27%; Adjusted 
EBITDA more than doubles to ₹89 Cr and PAT rises nearly 30-fold to ₹75 Cr 
 
Bengaluru, November 5, 2026: Amagi Media Labs Limited (NSE: AMAGI, BSE: 544679), a cloud-native SaaS platform 
providing AI-enabled solutions to global media and entertainment companies, today announced its financial results 
for Q2 FY27 and the half-year ended September 30, 2026. 
The Company delivered its highest-ever quarterly revenue, Adjusted EBITDA and Profit After Tax. Revenue grew 27% 
year-over-year to ₹476 Cr. Adjusted EBITDA increased 114% to ₹89 Cr, with margin expanding 7.6 percentage points to 
18.7%, reflecting continued operating leverage. 
Key highlights 
• Q2 FY27 performance 
✓ Revenue increased 27% Y/Y to ₹476 Cr. 
✓ Adjusted EBITDA grew 114% Y/Y to ₹89 Cr; margin expanded 7.6 percentage points to 18.7%. 
✓ PAT rose nearly 30-fold Y/Y to ₹75 Cr; margin improved 14.3 percentage points to 14.9%. 
• H1 FY27 performance 
✓ Revenue grew 29.5% Y/Y to ₹913 Cr. 
✓ Adjusted EBITDA increased 139% Y/Y to ₹139 Cr; margin expanded 7.0 percentage points to 15.3%. 
✓ PAT increased nearly 17-fold Y/Y to ₹109 Cr, with margin expanding 10.5 percentage points to 11.4%. 
✓ Adjusted OCF reached ₹94 Cr, versus an outflow of ₹98 Cr in H1 FY26; cash and treasury at ₹1,774 Cr, no debt. 
• Platform and Business Momentum 
✓ Industry Recognition: Named a Leader in IDC MarketScape 2026 for the AI-driven business cycle in media. 
✓ NEWSPULSE Milestones: Won TVTech’s Best of Show at IBC 2026 and Best Use of Agentic AI in Media at CSI 
Awards 2026; live at local stations of a major US broadcast group. 
✓ AI Innovation: Launched four AI products: Amagi STUDIO, FANPULSE, Integrated Localization and Agentic NOC. 
✓ Customer Momentum: Expanded engagements with media networks across the US, Middle East and APAC. 
As Amagi accelerates its AI-led transformation, the Company is broad-basing its Board by appointing Dr. Bhaskar 
Ghosh, former Chief Strategy & Innovation Officer at Accenture, and Srividhya Srinivasan, Co-founder and Chief 
Technology Officer of Amagi. Their extensive experience in AI, technology and enterprise transformation will bring 
valuable expertise to the Board and support Amagi's next phase of growth. 
Commenting on Q2 FY27 results, Baskar Subramanian, Managing Director & CEO, said: “Q2 marked new highs for 
revenue, Adjusted EBITDA and PAT. Alongside stronger cash generation in the first half, this reflects the progress we 
have made in scaling the business with greater operating discipline. 
We see three major opportunities ahead: helping customers operate more efficiently, reach new audiences and 
maximize revenues from their content. We expect AI to play an important role across all three. With NEWSPULSE 
moving into customer operations and four new AI products launched this quarter, we are building on our Media 
Industry Cloud. 
Our ambition remains to build an enduring engine of innovation for the media industry. We remain focused on turning 
innovation into customer adoption while sustaining growth, profitability and cash generation.” 
 
About Amagi Media Labs Limited: 
Founded in 2008, Amagi Media Labs Limited is a cloud-native SaaS platform serving the global media and entertainment industry. The Company 
enables media companies to launch, manage, distribute, and monetize live, linear, and on-demand content across cable, OTT, and FAST platforms 
without investing in traditional broadcast infrastructure. Its diversified platform, which includes Streaming Unification, Monetization & Marketplace, and 
Cloud Modernization, allows media companies to run end-to-end content operations, get comprehensive distribution reach, and offer monetization 
capabilities across streaming-led environments. The Company is one of the few players in the media technology space that offers end-to-end, AI-
enabled solutions across the video value chain. For more information, please visit https://www.amagi.com/
