✓ Revenue grew 29.5% Y/Y to ₹913 Cr. 
✓ Adjusted EBITDA increased 139% Y/Y to ₹139 Cr; margin expanded 7.0 percentage points to 15.3%. 
✓ PAT increased nearly 17-fold Y/Y to ₹109 Cr, with margin expanding 10.5 percentage points to 11.4%. 
✓ Adjusted OCF reached ₹94 Cr, versus an outflow of ₹98 Cr in H1 FY26; cash and treasury at ₹1,774 Cr, no debt. 
• Platform and Business Momentum 
✓ Industry Recognition: Named a Leader in IDC MarketScape 2026 for the AI-driven business cycle in media. 
✓ NEWSPULSE Milestones: Won TVTech’s Best of Show at IBC 2026 and Best Use of Agentic AI in Media at CSI 
Awards 2026; live at local stations of a major US broadcast group. 
✓ AI Innovation: Launched four AI products: Amagi STUDIO, FANPULSE, Integrated Localization and Agentic NOC. 
✓ Customer Momentum: Expanded engagements with media networks across the US, Middle East and APAC. 
As Amagi accelerates its AI-led transformation, the Company is broad-basing its Board by appointing Dr. Bhaskar 
Ghosh, former Chief Strategy & Innovation Officer at Accenture, and Srividhya Srinivasan, Co-founder and Chief 
Technology Officer of Amagi. Their extensive experience in AI, technology and enterprise transformation will bring 
valuable expertise to the Board and support Amagi's next phase of growth. 
Commenting on Q2 FY27 results, Baskar Subramanian, Managing Director & CEO, said: “Q2 marked new highs for 
revenue, Adjusted EBITDA and PAT. Alongside stronger cash generation in the first half, this reflects the progress we 
have made in scaling the business with greater operating discipline. 
We see three major opportunities ahead: helping customers operate more efficiently, reach new audiences and 
maximize revenues from their content. We expect AI to play an important role across all three. With NEWSPULSE 
moving into customer operations and four new AI products launched this quarter, we are building on our Media 
Industry Cloud. 
Our ambition remains to build an enduring engine of innovation for the media industry. We remain focused on turning 
innovation into customer adoption while sustaining growth, profitability and cash generation.” 
 
About Amagi Media Labs Limited: 
Founded in 2008, Amagi Media Labs Limited is a cloud-native SaaS platform serving the global media and entertainment industry. The Company 
enables media companies to launch, manage, distribute, and monetize live, linear, and on-demand content across cable, OTT, and FAST platforms 
without investing in traditional broadcast infrastructure. Its diversified platform, which includes Streaming Unification, Monetization & Marketplace, and 
Cloud Modernization, allows media companies to run end-to-end content operations, get comprehensive distribution reach, and offer monetization 
capabilities across streaming-led environments. The Company is one of the few players in the media technology space that offers end-to-end, AI-
enabled solutions across the video value chain. For more information, please visit https://www.amagi.com/

Board of Directors. Our responsibility is to express a conclusion on the Statement based on our review.

2410, ''Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the Entity" issued 
by the Institute of Chartered Accountants oflndia. This standard requires that we plan and perform the review

financial information consists of making inquiries, primarily of persons responsible for financial and 
accounting matters, and applying analytical and other review procedures. A review is substantially less in 
scope than an audit conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing and consequently does not enable 
us to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant matters that might be identified in an

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the Akums Drugs and Pharmaceuticals Limited 
Q2 FY27 Earning Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only 
mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. 
Should you need assistance during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing 
star then zero on your touch-tone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Ankit Jain from Akums. Thank you and over to you, sir. 
Ankit Jain: 
Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you, Swapnali, for introducing me. Welcome, everyone, to 
Akums Q2 FY27 Earnings Call. I am Ankit Jain and I Head Investor Relations at Akums Drugs 
and Pharmaceuticals Limited. On today's call, we are joined by Mr. Sanjeev Jain, Managing 
Director; Mr. Sandeep Jain, Managing Director; Mr. Sumeet Sood, CFO; Mr. Davinder Dogra, 
Deputy CFO; and Mr. Sahil Maheshwari, Head, Strategy. 
 
I will commence with our standard disclaimer that any discussion on today's call might include 
certain forward-looking statements, which are predictions or projections of future events. Our 
businesses face several risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ 
materially from what is expressed or implied in such statements. 
 
At Akums, we do not undertake any obligation to publicly update any forward-looking 
statements whether as a result of any new information, future events or otherwise. I hope you've 
had the opportunity to go through our financial results and review our investor presentation that 
were shared yesterday. 
 
I would now like to hand over the call to our Managing Director, Mr. Sandeep Jain, to discuss 
our performance. Thank you. 
Sandeep Jain: 
Thank you, Ankit. Namaste, everyone, and thank you for joining us today for our Q2 FY27 and 
H1 FY27 earnings call. I am pleased to announce another quarter of strong performance by 
Akums, one of the world's leading pharmaceutical CDMO. The performance was driven by 
double-digit volume growth during the quarter. The revenue grew by more than 30% on year-
on-year basis and EBITDA more than doubled during the corresponding period. 
 
Even sequentially, the quarter-on-quarter revenue growth stood at an impressive 15% and 
EBITDA increased by 11.5%. Led by strong order book and improved utilization of newer 
facilities, the CDMO business achieved a volume growth of more than 20% on September net 
MAT basis showcasing increasing penetration of our offering within the India pharma market. 
 
The improved performance is also an indicator of our resilience during times of global 
headwinds and geopolitical uncertainties. While the availability and the prices of input materials 
remain volatile, the demand outlook for CDMO remains strong. We today operate at healthy 
utilization levels of above 50%. 
 
During the quarter, we successfully integrated the 2 manufacturing plants acquired from 
Oriflame. With this, we have strengthened our beauty and personal care play as a fast-growing 
category in India. To cater to growing demand, we will operationalize a new facility at Baddi. 

 
 
Akums Drugs & Pharmaceuticals Limited 
 
 
November 03, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 14 
 
The plant will have oral solids in Phase 1 with an annual capacity of over 6 billion units, which 
will fully operationalize by Q1 FY28. 
 
With this plant, we will have 2 plants in Baddi in line with our stated objectives of geographical 
diversification. We remain steadfast on expanding as well as deepening our global footprints 
with special emphasis on regulated market. 
 
We have 2 products approved in Europe, 8 filed and over 30 in R&D, which we expect to 
commercialize over next 3-4 years. Our 2 facilities are EU-GMP certified and few more are in 
the pipeline. Our European CDMO project is progressing as per our stated plans with supplies 
commencing in FY28. 
 
Our JV with the Zambia government is also progressing smoothly with commercial supplies 
from the Indian plant scheduled during Q4 FY27 and considering the prolonged shipping time 
to Zambia, we expect to book revenues during Q1 FY28. 
 
The process for setting up the plant in the Zambia is well underway with technical discussions 
already complete. The plant is expected to become operational in 2029, expanding our 
manufacturing presence outside India. 
 
Our domestic branded formulations segment had a steady quarter with 8% year-on-year growth 
in revenue and improvement in profitability on a sequential basis. We expect the segment to 
deliver growth on par with IPM by FY28 as the current initiatives start bearing fruits. 
 
Our international branded formulations business saw growth accelerating both on year-on-year 
and quarter-on-quarter basis. It is expected to maintain this momentum going forward in the year 
and will be key engine to drive Akums' growth. 
 
API segment continued on its journey towards becoming EBITDA breakeven as our endeavor 
continued. The trade generics segment remained EBITDA positive during the quarter with the 
third straight quarter of achieving profitability.  
Sustainability is core to Akums in whatever we do. We are proud to announce that our company 
has an EcoVadis Bronze medal. We are on our journey to be amongst the top global companies 
focused on environment, labor rights, ethics and sustainability. We also won the Water 
Management Champion Award by CII for green practices.  
We also successfully transitioned to S/4HANA this quarter. This will provide real-time analytics 
across key business performances indicators.  
With number of initiatives underway, we remain confident in our ability to create long-term 
shareholder value and delivering positive results. 
 
I shall now request our CFO, Mr. Sumeet Sood, to take you through the detailed financials for 
the quarter. Over to you, Mr. Sumeet. 
Sumeet Sood: 
Thank you, sir. Thank you very much. Good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to present the 
financial highlights for the quarter 30th September 2026.  

 
 
Akums Drugs & Pharmaceuticals Limited 
 
 
November 03, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 14 
 
Revenue on a consolidated basis stood at INR1,342 crores; an increase of 31.9% year-on-year, 
Q 2 FY26 it was INR 1,018 crores and an increase of 15.1% quarter-on-quarter, Q1 FY27 it was 
INR 1,167 crores. 
 
EBITDA for the quarter stood at a healthy INR195 crores; a multi fold increase of 106% year-
on-year, Q2 FY26 was INR94 crores and an increase of 11.5% quarter-on-quarter, Q1 FY27 was 
INR175 crores. 
 
Margins were healthy at 14.5% as against 9.3% in Q2 FY26 and 15% in Q1 FY27. EBITDA 
with other income stood at INR224 crores, an increase of 76.3% year-on-year and an increase 
of 9.1% quarter-on-quarter. 
 
Profit after tax stood at INR115 crores; an increase of 168.3% year-on-year, Q2 FY26, it was 
INR43 crores and an increase of 13.5% quarter-on-quarter, Q1 FY27 it stood at INR101 crores. 
If we come to the segment-wise performance if we look at the CDMO revenue, it stood at 
INR1,115 crores, an increase of 38.6% year-on-year and an increase of 15.6% quarter-on-
quarter. 
 
The revenue growth, as explained by Sandeep ji, was largely driven by a healthy increase in 
volumes. EBITDA for the quarter for this business stood at INR168 crores; an increase of 99.6% 
year-on-year, for the Q2 FY26 it was at INR84 crores and an increase of 2.9% quarter-on-
quarter, Q1 FY27 it stood at INR163 crores. 
 
Domestic branded formulations revenue stood at INR132 crores, an increase of 8.2% year-on-
year and an increase of 14.4% quarter-on-quarter. EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR24 
crores; a decline of 8.9% year-on-year, Q2 FY26 it was INR26 crores and an increase of 103% 
quarter-on-quarter, Q1 FY27 it was INR12 crores. 
 
For the international branded formulation, revenue stood at INR44 crores; an increase of 95.2% 
year-on-year, quarter 2 FY26 it stood at INR22 crores and an increase of 26.7% quarter-on-
quarter, Q1 FY27 it was INR35 crores. EBITDA for the quarter was at INR9.9 crores, an 
increase of 80.5% year-on-year and an increase of 43.8% quarter-on-quarter. 
 
If we look at the API, the revenue stood at INR29 crores; a decrease of 35.3% year-on-year, Q2 
FY26 it was INR44 crores and a decline of 9.1% quarter-on-quarter, Q1 FY27 it stood at INR32 
crores. EBITDA loss was slightly higher on this quarter, which is INR 5.7 crores while 
significantly lower than Q2 FY26 INR14 crores, however, higher than Q1 FY27 at INR3.9 
crores. 
 
We continue to focus on higher gross margin products and expect the full year losses to be lower 
than last year. If we come to the trade generic business, the revenue stood at INR23 crores, a 
decrease of 5.4% year-on-year and an increase of 10.1% quarter-on-quarter. EBITDA for the 
quarter stood at INR1.2 crores. 
 
Our balance sheet continues to remain healthy and cash and cash equivalent as has been 
constantly increasing stands at INR1,680 crores. The company had a free cash flow for H1 of 
INR45.5 crores after account for business acquisition driven by healthy operating cash flow to

EBITDA at a ratio of 69.2%. Based on the above, we conclude the financial highlights for the 
quarter.

Thank you, sir. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. We have the first question 
from the line of Saksham Tyagi from Desvelado Advisory. 
Saksham Tyagi: 
So, my first question was that I just wanted an update on the Europe and Zambia business like 
how is it going and where do we stand currently? In the previous con call, you mentioned that 
you expect the Zambia business to deliver a revenue of $25 million. So, I just wanted to know 
what's the progress so far on that? 
Sahil Maheshwari: 
Sure. So, this is Sahil, Saksham. So both the businesses, as we have been telling, both are 
businesses which are well with us. These are confirmed businesses. I'll first take Zambia because 
that is closer to delivery. 
 
So, post the midyear elections for the President where the current regime was re-elected. Soon 
after it, we went into discussing the purchase order and we have now received the purchase 
orders. We are in process of now supplying the purchase orders, which we think post the 
manufacturing lead time, we should be able to supply them in Q4. 
 
Since this like most of our CDMO is ex works. So in our factory once it leaves our warehouse, 
we book the revenue ex works. Here we have to deliver at Lusaka warehouse of the Zambian 
government. So that shipping time lines from Haridwar from where we'll mostly manufacture to 
Lusaka in Zambia is roughly 100 and 120 days. 
 
So while we will dispatch the goods in Q4, which will be as a goods in transit in our financial 
accounts, we'll be able to book the revenue once we have a delivery, which will be in Q1. So, 
the business is, as you rightly said, $25 million fully intact with a margin profile which are 
slightly better than our CDMO margins. 
 
So that all remains consistent. And subsequently when we deliver this, we will again have a 
discussion on another $25 million round of supplies committed by the Government of Zambia. 
So that's on the Zambia business. On the European business, as we said, we have compiled the 
dossier. 
 
The dossier has been filed. While it is up to the regulator, we believe that it could take 1 or 2

ABOUT ELECTRONICSMART INDIA LIMITED
Electronics Mart India Limited (EMIL),is one of India's largest consumer durables and electronics retailers, with a legacy spanning over four decades .
Founded in 1980 by Mr. Pavan Kumar Bajaj in Hyderabad, the company has grown from a single store to a formidable multi - state retail network,
firmly establishing itself as the largest electronics retailer in South India.
EMIL operates an extensive network of 229 stores across more than 100+ cities in Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and the National Capital Region,
offering consumers a curated selection of over 8,000 + SKUsacross 100+ leading domestic and international brands. Its product portfolio spans
large appliances, including air conditioners, televisions, washing machines, and refrigerators, mobile phones, small appliances, IT products, and a
growing range of smart home and lifestyle solutions .
The company is committed
to delivering a premium and differentiated
retail experience, underpinned
by strong brand partnerships, a deep
understanding of regional consumer preferences, and a proven ability to scale responsibly . EMIL's retail footprint
spans both multi - brand outlets
and exclusive brand outlets, catering to a diverse and aspirational consumer base across urban and semi- urban markets .
Listed on the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) & Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), EMIL continues to expand its reach, deepen its brand
partnerships, and invest in long- term capabilities — positioning itself as a trusted destination for the evolving Indian consumer at every stage of
their electronics and home lifestyle journey .
Commenting on the Company's Performance, Mr. Karan Bajaj, CEO of EMIL, said, 
"Ht F'r27 has been a robust half for EMIL, with every key metric moving in the right direction . Revenue grew 30 % to Rs. 
4,319crores, gross profit rose 49% with margins expanding 210bps to 164%, EBITDAnearly doubled to Rs. 369 crores 
at an 8.6 % margin, and PAT rose over 4x to Rs. 161crores. 
02 is seasonally a softer quarter for consumer durables . Despite this, we delivered 19'/4 revenue growth, SSSG of 
165% and a 180 bps expansion in EBITDAmargin to 6.9%, with growth broad-based across categories . Mobiles grew 
31%, driven by new smartphone launches and continued traction in existing models, while air conditioners grew 53% 
even in the off-season. Premium and emerging categories such as built-in appliances, dishwashers, tablets and 
wearables also delivered strong double - digit growth, and our average ticket size rose 191/4, reflecting our strength in 
premium categories . 
The South market remains a scaled, profitable engine for us, with revenue up 28% in Ht and EBITDAmargin up 320 
bps to 9.3 %. The North cluster is on a similar path: revenue grew 36 % in Ht and EBITDAmargin rose to 3.4 % from 10 % 
as our stores mature and scale. More than half of our network is under four years old, so we expect margins to keep 
improving as a better product mix and operating leverage take effect .. 
We are on track to enter West Bengal, our next growth cluster, and we are confident it will add to our growth . 
Our focus on working capital continues to pay off, with pre IND- AS operating cash flow growing to Rs. 304 crores 
With festive demand off to a strong start and a solid first half behind us, we remain firmly on track to deliver growth , 
while continuing to invest in the customer experience that has underpinned EMIL 'sgrowth for over four decades ."

Robust H1 FY27: EBITDA nearly doubles; PAT grows over 4x
H1 FY27: Revenue growth of 30%; EBITDA growth of 93%; PAT growth of 326%
Q2 FY27: Revenue growth of 19%; EBITDA growth of 61%; PAT growth of 149%
EBITDA Margin expansion of 180 bps in Q2 FY27 and 280 bps in H1 FY27
North Cluster revenue up 45% in Q2 FY27, with margins steadily improving
Hyderabad, 05 th November 2026
Electronics
Mart India Limited , one of the largest electronics retailers in India, has announced
its unaudited financial results for the quarter and half year ended 30 th September 2026
Key Highlights for Q2 FY27
• Revenue from Operations of Rs. 1,900 crores, up 19% Y- o- Y
• Gross Profit of Rs. 293 crores, up 31%Y- o- Y; GP Margin up 130 bps to 15.4%
• EBITDAof Rs. 131crores, up 61%Y- o- Y; EBITDAMargin up 180 bps to 6.9%
• PATof Rs. 40 crores, up 149%Y- o- Y; PATMargin up 110bps to 2.1%
• South Cluster revenue up 16%Y- o- Y; EBITDAMargin up 220 bps to 7.4%
• North Cluster revenue up 45%Y- o- Y; EBITDAMargin up 430 bps Y- o- Y to 1.6%
• Same Store Sales Growth (SSSG)of 16.5%
• Product Mix: Mobiles 53%; Large Appliances 33%; Small Appliances, IT& Others 14%
Key Highlights for H1FY27
• Revenue from Operations of Rs. 4,319crores, up 30 %Y- o- Y
• Gross Profit of Rs. 710crores, up 49%Y- o- Y; GP Margin up 210 bps to 16.4%
• EBITDAof Rs. 369 crores, up 93%Y- o- Y; EBITDAMargin up 280 bps to 8.6%
• PATof Rs. 161crores, up 326%Y- o- Y; PATMargin up 260 bps to 3.7%
• South Cluster revenue up 28%Y- o- Y; EBITDAMargin up 320 bps to 9.3%
• North Cluster revenue up 36%Y- o- Y; EBITDAMargin up 240 bps to 3.4%
• Same Store Sales Growth (SSSG)of 27.5%
• Product Mix: Mobiles 45%; Large Appliances 41%; Others 14%
• Pre IND- AS Operating Cash Flow of Rs. 304 crores ; Working Capital at 61days vs 77 days
• 229 stores across 100+ cities, with 6 net store additions during the first half

ABOUT ELECTRONICSMART INDIA LIMITED
Electronics Mart India Limited (EMIL),is one of India's largest consumer durables and electronics retailers, with a legacy spanning over four decades .
Founded in 1980 by Mr. Pavan Kumar Bajaj in Hyderabad, the company has grown from a single store to a formidable multi - state retail network,
firmly establishing itself as the largest electronics retailer in South India.
EMIL operates an extensive network of 229 stores across more than 100+ cities in Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and the National Capital Region,
offering consumers a curated selection of over 8,000 + SKUsacross 100+ leading domestic and international brands. Its product portfolio spans
large appliances, including air conditioners, televisions, washing machines, and refrigerators, mobile phones, small appliances, IT products, and a
growing range of smart home and lifestyle solutions .
The company is committed
to delivering a premium and differentiated
retail experience, underpinned
by strong brand partnerships, a deep
understanding of regional consumer preferences, and a proven ability to scale responsibly . EMIL's retail footprint
spans both multi - brand outlets
and exclusive brand outlets, catering to a diverse and aspirational consumer base across urban and semi- urban markets .
Listed on the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) & Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), EMIL continues to expand its reach, deepen its brand
partnerships, and invest in long- term capabilities — positioning itself as a trusted destination for the evolving Indian consumer at every stage of
their electronics and home lifestyle journey .
Commenting on the Company's Performance, Mr. Karan Bajaj, CEO of EMIL, said, 
"Ht F'r27 has been a robust half for EMIL, with every key metric moving in the right direction . Revenue grew 30 % to Rs. 
4,319crores, gross profit rose 49% with margins expanding 210bps to 164%, EBITDAnearly doubled to Rs. 369 crores 
at an 8.6 % margin, and PAT rose over 4x to Rs. 161crores. 
02 is seasonally a softer quarter for consumer durables . Despite this, we delivered 19'/4 revenue growth, SSSG of 
165% and a 180 bps expansion in EBITDAmargin to 6.9%, with growth broad-based across categories . Mobiles grew 
31%, driven by new smartphone launches and continued traction in existing models, while air conditioners grew 53% 
even in the off-season. Premium and emerging categories such as built-in appliances, dishwashers, tablets and 
wearables also delivered strong double - digit growth, and our average ticket size rose 191/4, reflecting our strength in 
premium categories . 
The South market remains a scaled, profitable engine for us, with revenue up 28% in Ht and EBITDAmargin up 320 
bps to 9.3 %. The North cluster is on a similar path: revenue grew 36 % in Ht and EBITDAmargin rose to 3.4 % from 10 % 
as our stores mature and scale. More than half of our network is under four years old, so we expect margins to keep 
improving as a better product mix and operating leverage take effect .. 
We are on track to enter West Bengal, our next growth cluster, and we are confident it will add to our growth . 
Our focus on working capital continues to pay off, with pre IND- AS operating cash flow growing to Rs. 304 crores 
With festive demand off to a strong start and a solid first half behind us, we remain firmly on track to deliver growth , 
while continuing to invest in the customer experience that has underpinned EMIL 'sgrowth for over four decades ."

Sub: Outcome of the Board Meeting held on 5th November, 2026 
Dear Sirs, 
We write to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company at its Meeting held today 
has inter-alia, approved the following:  
 
1. the Unaudited Standalone & Consolidated Financial Results of the Company for the 
quarter and half-year ended 30th September, 2026, which are enclosed along with the 
Limited Review Report thereon issued by the Statutory Auditors of the Company 
(submitted with unmodified opinion) - marked as Annexure A. 
 
2. re-appointment of Mr. Udyavar Vittal Kamath (DIN: 00648897) as an Executive 
Director of the Company for a period of 1 (one) year w.e.f. 1st February, 2027, as per 
the terms & conditions as recommended by the Nomination and Remuneration 
Committee and in accordance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, the 
Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘Listing Regulations’) & subject to the approval of 
the shareholders.  
 
The details as required under the Listing Regulations read with SEBI Master Circular 
No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated 30th January, 2026, are 
enclosed herewith – marked as Annexure B. 
 
The meeting commenced at 11:45 a.m. and concluded at 2:40 p.m.  
 
This is for your information and record. 
 
Thanking you, 
 
Yours faithfully, 
For Texmaco Rail & Engineering Limited 
 
 
Sandeep Kumar Sultania

During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Nomination and Remuneration Committee of the Board approved the grant of 10,32, 780 options to eligible employees of the Company under Texmaco Rail Long Term Incentive Plan 2026. The 
grant of options is subject to the terms and conditions of the Texmaco Rail LTIP 2026, including the applicable vesting conditions. In accordance with Ind AS 102 - Share-based Payment, the Company has recognized a share-based payment expense

Group has recognised a gain on deemed disposal of its interest in the JV amounting to '1'7,601.26 lakhs, in accordance with the requirements of Ind AS 28, Investments in Associates and Joint Ventures. The gain has been presented as an exceptional 
item in the Statement of Profit and Loss for the quarter ended 30 September 2026. 
5. As on 30th September, 2026, the Company has 7 (Seven) Subsidiaries, 2 (two) Joint Ventures & 1 (one) Associate.

Sub: Outcome of the Board Meeting held on 5th November, 2026 
Dear Sirs, 
We write to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company at its Meeting held today 
has inter-alia, approved the following:  
 
1. the Unaudited Standalone & Consolidated Financial Results of the Company for the 
quarter and half-year ended 30th September, 2026, which are enclosed along with the 
Limited Review Report thereon issued by the Statutory Auditors of the Company 
(submitted with unmodified opinion) - marked as Annexure A. 
 
2. re-appointment of Mr. Udyavar Vittal Kamath (DIN: 00648897) as an Executive 
Director of the Company for a period of 1 (one) year w.e.f. 1st February, 2027, as per 
the terms & conditions as recommended by the Nomination and Remuneration 
Committee and in accordance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, the 
Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘Listing Regulations’) & subject to the approval of 
the shareholders.  
 
The details as required under the Listing Regulations read with SEBI Master Circular 
No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated 30th January, 2026, are 
enclosed herewith – marked as Annexure B. 
 
The meeting commenced at 11:45 a.m. and concluded at 2:40 p.m.  
 
This is for your information and record. 
 
Thanking you, 
 
Yours faithfully, 
For Texmaco Rail & Engineering Limited

Sub: Outcome of the Board Meeting held on 5th November, 2026 
Dear Sirs, 
We write to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company at its Meeting held today 
has inter-alia, approved the following:  
 
1. the Unaudited Standalone & Consolidated Financial Results of the Company for the 
quarter and half-year ended 30th September, 2026, which are enclosed along with the 
Limited Review Report thereon issued by the Statutory Auditors of the Company 
(submitted with unmodified opinion) - marked as Annexure A. 
 
2. re-appointment of Mr. Udyavar Vittal Kamath (DIN: 00648897) as an Executive 
Director of the Company for a period of 1 (one) year w.e.f. 1st February, 2027, as per 
the terms & conditions as recommended by the Nomination and Remuneration 
Committee and in accordance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, the 
Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘Listing Regulations’) & subject to the approval of 
the shareholders.  
 
The details as required under the Listing Regulations read with SEBI Master Circular 
No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated 30th January, 2026, are 
enclosed herewith – marked as Annexure B. 
 
The meeting commenced at 11:45 a.m. and concluded at 2:40 p.m.  
 
This is for your information and record. 
 
Thanking you, 
 
Yours faithfully, 
For Texmaco Rail & Engineering Limited

1. The above results have been reviewed by Audit Committee and approved by the Board of Directors at their respective meetings held on 5th November, 2026. These results have also been reviewed by the Statutory Auditors, as required under the 
SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, who have issued their report thereon with an unmodified opinion. 
2. The above Financial Results have been prepared in accordance with IND-AS as precsribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with Companies (Indian Accounts) Rules, 2015 as amended from time to time. 
3. 
During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Nomination and Remuneration Committee of the Board approved the grant of 10,32, 780 options to eligible employees of the Company under Texmaco Rail Long Term Incentive Plan 2026. The 
grant of options is subject to the terms and conditions of the Texmaco Rail LTIP 2026, including the applicable vesting conditions. In accordance with Ind AS 102 - Share-based Payment, the Company has recognized a share-based payment expense 
of '1'64.32 lakh during the quarter, with a corresponding credit to Share-based Payment Reserve under Other Equity. 
4. During the quarter, Texmaco Touax Railcar Leasing Private Limited (the "Joint Venture") issued equity shares to a new investor, resulting in a dilution of the Group's shareholding in the JV from 50% to 34% on a fully diluted basis. Consequently, the 
Group has recognised a gain on deemed disposal of its interest in the JV amounting to '1'7,601.26 lakhs, in accordance with the requirements of Ind AS 28, Investments in Associates and Joint Ventures. The gain has been presented as an exceptional 
item in the Statement of Profit and Loss for the quarter ended 30 September 2026. 
5. As on 30th September, 2026, the Company has 7 (Seven) Subsidiaries, 2 (two) Joint Ventures & 1 (one) Associate. 
6. The figures for the corresponding previous periods have been regrouped/ reclassified wherever necessary, to make them comparable. 
7. The above results are also available on the Company's website www.texmaco.in and on the stock exchange websites (www.bseindia.com and www.nseindia.com).

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to P N Gadgil Jewellers Limited Q2 FY27 
Earnings Conference Call hosted by Nuvama Institutional Equities. As a reminder, all 
participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask 
questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference 
call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touchtone phone. Please note 
that this conference is being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Aayush Adukia from Nuvama Institutional Equities. 
Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Aayush Adukia: 
Thank you, Yusuf. Good afternoon, everyone. On behalf of Nuvama, it is a pleasure to welcome 
you to P N Gadgil Jewellers Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call. From the management today, 
we have Dr. Saurabh Gadgil, Chairman and MD and Mr. Deepak Vijay, CFO. I would like to 
hand over the call to the management for their opening remarks. Over to you, Saurabh. 
Saurabh Gadgil: 
Thank you, Aayush. Good evening, everyone, and a very warm welcome to the Q2 FY27 
Earnings Conference Call of P N Gadgil Jewellers Limited. I hope you had an opportunity to 
review our financial results, our investor presentations and press release, which is uploaded on 
the exchanges and on the company's website. 
 
To begin with, I would like to express my sincere gratitude to our customers, employees, 
franchisee partners, vendor partners and shareholders for their continued trust and support. Their 
confidence in PNG Jewellers continues to inspire us as we build on legacy and deliver a strong 
performance in the second quarter and the first half of FY27.  
This July to September quarter is traditionally a relatively subdued period for the jewellery 
industry, largely coinciding with Chaturmas when wedding-related demand tends to be lower. 
Despite this seasonal moderation, consumer demand remained healthy. With gold prices 
continuing to remain elevated, customers increasingly graduated towards lightweight designs, 
studded jewellery and old gold exchange.  
These evolving preferences continue to create opportunities for trusted organized retailers with 
established brands and a strong focus on transparency and customer confidence. PNG Jewellers 
has delivered a revenue of INR2,666 crores, up 22% Y-o-Y. And EBITDA grew 57% Y-o-Y to 
INR224.6 crores, with EBITDA margin expanding 186 bps to 8.4%, while profit after tax grew 
53% Y-o-Y to INR121 crores with a PAT margin of 4.5%.

News Release 
HYDERABAD, INDIA (5 Nov 2026) -- SUVEN Life Sciences Limited ("Suven") today announced unaudited financial 
results for the quarter and half year ended 30 Sep 2026. The unaudited financial results were reviewed by the 
audit committee and approved by the Board of Directors in their meeting held on 5 Nov 2026 at Hyderabad. 
 
(a) Suven, a Biopharmaceutical company, engaged in Drug Discovery and Development of New Chemical Entities (NCEs) in 
Central Nervous System (CNS) disorders targeting unmet medical needs, globally. 
(b) The statement of operations includes financial of Suven Neurosciences, Inc., a Delaware Company, wholly owned 
subsidiary (WOS) of Suven, involved in clinical development programs of the Company. 
(c) Clinical development pipeline: 
 
SUVN-502 (Masupirdine) – Completed enrollment milestone in Global Phase 3 Trial for Agitation in Alzheimer’s 
Dementia. The last patient last visit will be in quarter 1, 2027 calendar year enabling progression towards database 
lock and reporting of topline data potentially in Q2 - 2027 calendar year. 
 
SUVN-G3031 (Samelisant) – Global Phase-3 clinical study to confirm efficacy and safety of Samelisant in narcolepsy 
is in progress. 
 
SUVN-911 (Ropanicant) – Phase 2B clinical study in USA is completed with successful outcome. Targeting for Global 
Phase -3 program initiation during Q2-2027 calendar year. 
 
SUVN-D4010 (Usmarapride) – Phase-2 Proof of Concept (PoC) Study for Cognitive Dysfunction initiated during 
October 2026. 
 
SUVN-I6107 – Phase 1 study for establishing safety and pharmacokinetics completed and Phase 2 enabling 
toxicological studies are underway. 
For more information on Suven please visit our Web site at http://www.suven.com

HYDERABAD, INDIA (5 Nov 2026) -- SUVEN Life Sciences Limited ("Suven") today announced unaudited financial 
results for the quarter and half year ended 30 Sep 2026. The unaudited financial results were reviewed by the 
audit committee and approved by the Board of Directors in their meeting held on 5 Nov 2026 at Hyderabad. 
 
(a) Suven, a Biopharmaceutical company, engaged in Drug Discovery and Development of New Chemical Entities (NCEs) in 
Central Nervous System (CNS) disorders targeting unmet medical needs, globally. 
(b) The statement of operations includes financial of Suven Neurosciences, Inc., a Delaware Company, wholly owned 
subsidiary (WOS) of Suven, involved in clinical development programs of the Company. 
(c) Clinical development pipeline: 
 
SUVN-502 (Masupirdine) – Completed enrollment milestone in Global Phase 3 Trial for Agitation in Alzheimer’s 
Dementia. The last patient last visit will be in quarter 1, 2027 calendar year enabling progression towards database 
lock and reporting of topline data potentially in Q2 - 2027 calendar year. 
 
SUVN-G3031 (Samelisant) – Global Phase-3 clinical study to confirm efficacy and safety of Samelisant in narcolepsy 
is in progress. 
 
SUVN-911 (Ropanicant) – Phase 2B clinical study in USA is completed with successful outcome. Targeting for Global 
Phase -3 program initiation during Q2-2027 calendar year. 
 
SUVN-D4010 (Usmarapride) – Phase-2 Proof of Concept (PoC) Study for Cognitive Dysfunction initiated during 
October 2026. 
 
SUVN-I6107 – Phase 1 study for establishing safety and pharmacokinetics completed and Phase 2 enabling 
toxicological studies are underway.

Report of the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors of Triveni Power Transmission 
Limited dated November 5, 2026 certifying distribution of proceeds to eligible 
shareholders of fractional shares (Eligible Shareholders) pursuant to the Composite 
Scheme Of Arrangement amongst Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises Limited (“Amalgamating 
Company ”), 
Triveni Engineering & Industries Limited 
(“Amalgamated 
Company”/”Demerged Company”) and Triveni Power Transmission Limited 
(“Resulting Company”) and their respective shareholders and creditors (“The Scheme”) 
Present-Committee Members

Mr Siraj Azmat Chaudhry, Member

Ealiadl

This report of the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors is made in compliance with 
SEBI Master Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/POD-2/P/CIR/2023/93 dated June 20, 2023 
(“SEBI Master Circular”) as amended from time to time. 
I BACKGROUND 
1.1 The Composite Scheme of Arrangement amongst Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises 
Limited (“Amalgamating Company ), Triveni Engineering & Industries Limited 
(“Amalgamated Company”/”Demerged Company”) and Triveni Power 
Transmission Limited (“Resulting Company”/’the Company”) and their 
respective shareholders and creditors (“ The Scheme”) was approved by the 
Hon’ble National Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad Bench (‘NCLT") vide its 
Orders dated May 07, 2026 and May 18, 2026. Accordingly, as on May 19, 2026 
i.e. Effective Date (as defined in the Scheme) the Power Transmission Business 
of the Demerged Company stood transferred to and vested in the Resulting 
Company in accordance with Part IV of the Scheme, without any further act or 
deed. 
1.2 In terms of the provision of the Scheme, the eligible shareholders of Triveni 
Engineering & Industries Limited (Demerged Company), as on the record date 
(ie., July 22, 2026) were issued and allotted the equity shares of Triveni Power 
Transmission Limited (Resulting Company) on July 28, 2026 in the share 
entitlement ratio of 1:3 i.e. 1 (One) fully paid-up Equity Shares of the Resulting 
Company of the face value of INR 2 (Indian Rupees Two) each were issued and 
allotted, at par as fully paid-up to the equity shareholders of the Demerged 
Company for every 3 (Three) Equity Shares of INR 1 (Indian Rupee One) each 
held by the shareholders of the Demerged Company, as on the Record Date. 
1.3 The fully paid-up equity shares allotted to the shareholders of Triveni Engineering 
& Industries Limited (Demerged Company) shall rank pari-passu in all respect 
with the existing fully paid-up equity shares of the Company.

1.4 While determining the allotment pursuant to the Scheme, 73,009 shareholders 
became entitled to fractional entitlements. In accordance with the provision of the 
Scheme, allotment of 35,852 equity shares of INR 2/- each arising out of 
consolidation of fractional entitlements, were directly credited to a separate demat 
account titled “Triveni Power Transmission Limited — Trustee Demat Share 
Escrow Account” (DP ID: IN300118, Client ID: 11850701) opened and 
maintained by Mitcon Credentia Trusteeship Services Limited, who were 
appointed by the Board of Directors of the Company to hold fractional shares in 
trust for the benefit of the shareholders entitled to such fractional entitlements in 
compliance with the Scheme and applicable SEBI circulars. 
1.5 In terms of SEBI Master Circular, a report from the Audit Committee is required 
to certify that the proceeds from the sale of consolidated fractional entitlements 
are given to Eligible Shareholders in proportion to their entitlements. This report 
is made to comply with the requirements of the said Master Circular. 
II TREATMENT OF FRACTIONAL ENTITLEMENTS 
2.1 As per the SEBI Master Circular, the fractional entitlements are required to be sold by 
the Trustee in the open market within 90 days and the net sale proceeds thereof, after 
deductions of the applicable taxes and expenses incurred, to be distributed to the 
respective eligible equity shareholders of the Demerged Company in proportion to 
their respective fractional entitlements. 
2.2 The distribution of sale proceeds (after deduction of the expenses incurred) has been 
completed on 30™ October, 2026 as per following details:

Report of the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors of Triveni Power Transmission 
Limited dated November 5, 2026 certifying distribution of proceeds to eligible 
shareholders of fractional shares (Eligible Shareholders) pursuant to the Composite 
Scheme Of Arrangement amongst Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises Limited (“Amalgamating 
Company ”), 
Triveni Engineering & Industries Limited 
(“Amalgamated

This report of the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors is made in compliance with 
SEBI Master Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/POD-2/P/CIR/2023/93 dated June 20, 2023 
(“SEBI Master Circular”) as amended from time to time. 
I BACKGROUND 
1.1 The Composite Scheme of Arrangement amongst Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises 
Limited (“Amalgamating Company ), Triveni Engineering & Industries Limited 
(“Amalgamated Company”/”Demerged Company”) and Triveni Power 
Transmission Limited (“Resulting Company”/’the Company”) and their 
respective shareholders and creditors (“ The Scheme”) was approved by the 
Hon’ble National Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad Bench (‘NCLT") vide its 
Orders dated May 07, 2026 and May 18, 2026. Accordingly, as on May 19, 2026 
i.e. Effective Date (as defined in the Scheme) the Power Transmission Business 
of the Demerged Company stood transferred to and vested in the Resulting 
Company in accordance with Part IV of the Scheme, without any further act or 
deed. 
1.2 In terms of the provision of the Scheme, the eligible shareholders of Triveni 
Engineering & Industries Limited (Demerged Company), as on the record date 
(ie., July 22, 2026) were issued and allotted the equity shares of Triveni Power 
Transmission Limited (Resulting Company) on July 28, 2026 in the share 
entitlement ratio of 1:3 i.e. 1 (One) fully paid-up Equity Shares of the Resulting 
Company of the face value of INR 2 (Indian Rupees Two) each were issued and 
allotted, at par as fully paid-up to the equity shareholders of the Demerged 
Company for every 3 (Three) Equity Shares of INR 1 (Indian Rupee One) each 
held by the shareholders of the Demerged Company, as on the Record Date. 
1.3 The fully paid-up equity shares allotted to the shareholders of Triveni Engineering 
& Industries Limited (Demerged Company) shall rank pari-passu in all respect 
with the existing fully paid-up equity shares of the Company.

1.4 While determining the allotment pursuant to the Scheme, 73,009 shareholders 
became entitled to fractional entitlements. In accordance with the provision of the 
Scheme, allotment of 35,852 equity shares of INR 2/- each arising out of 
consolidation of fractional entitlements, were directly credited to a separate demat 
account titled “Triveni Power Transmission Limited — Trustee Demat Share 
Escrow Account” (DP ID: IN300118, Client ID: 11850701) opened and 
maintained by Mitcon Credentia Trusteeship Services Limited, who were 
appointed by the Board of Directors of the Company to hold fractional shares in 
trust for the benefit of the shareholders entitled to such fractional entitlements in 
compliance with the Scheme and applicable SEBI circulars. 
1.5 In terms of SEBI Master Circular, a report from the Audit Committee is required 
to certify that the proceeds from the sale of consolidated fractional entitlements 
are given to Eligible Shareholders in proportion to their entitlements. This report 
is made to comply with the requirements of the said Master Circular. 
II TREATMENT OF FRACTIONAL ENTITLEMENTS 
2.1 As per the SEBI Master Circular, the fractional entitlements are required to be sold by 
the Trustee in the open market within 90 days and the net sale proceeds thereof, after 
deductions of the applicable taxes and expenses incurred, to be distributed to the 
respective eligible equity shareholders of the Demerged Company in proportion to 
their respective fractional entitlements. 
2.2 The distribution of sale proceeds (after deduction of the expenses incurred) has been 
completed on 30™ October, 2026 as per following details:

Q2 & H1FY27 Earnings Conference Call” 
November 02, 2026 
 
 
 
 
 
MANAGEMENT: MR. ASHISH RAI – GROUP CEO & VICE CHAIRMAN – 
AURIONPRO SOLUTIONS LIMITED 
MR. VIPUL PARMAR – CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER – 
AURIONPRO SOLUTIONS LIMITED 
MR. NINAD KELKAR – COMPANY SECRETARY – AURIONPRO 
SOLUTIONS LIMITED                    
 

                                              Aurionpro Solutions Limited 
 
 
November 02, 2026 
 
 
Page 2 of 19 
 
Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Aurionpro Solutions Limited's Q2 and H1 FY27 
Results Conference Call. 
Today on this call, we have with us from the Management, Mr. Ashish Rai – Group CEO and Vice-
Chairman, Mr. Vipul Parmar – Chief Financial Officer and Mr. Ninad Kelkar – Company Secretary. 
Let me draw your attention to the fact that today's discussion may include certain forward-looking 
statements, which are predictions, projections, or other estimates about future events. These 
statements reflect management's current expectations about the future performance of the 
company and are subject to various risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ 
materially. 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an opportunity 
for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Ashish Rai – Group CEO and Vice Chairman at Aurionpro 
Solutions Limited. Following his comments, we will open the forum for question-and-answer 
session. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Ashish Rai: 
Thank you, and good morning, everyone, and welcome to our Q2 FY27 Earnings Call. 
This quarter marks an important operational step up for Aurionpro. 
We delivered INR 415 crores in revenue, up 16% both year-on-year as well as quarter-on-quarter 
sequentially. Crossing quarterly revenue threshold for the first time ever establishes a strong 
baseline for the quarters ahead. We achieved this growth while preserving solid profitability, even 
as we absorbed input cost pressures, we absorbed and maintained an aggressive pace of R&D 
investment. 
For the quarter, EBITDA came in at INR 71 crores at a 17.2% margin, and PAT stood at INR 50 crores 
at a 12% margin. 
Following a quiet start to the fiscal year, momentum is visibly building. When an industry undergoes 
a generational technology shift like we are going through, it calls for a disproportionate 
commitment to product innovation. We lean into that investment cycle early, and this quarter, we 
are beginning to see clear market validation of our roadmap. 

                                              Aurionpro Solutions Limited 
 
 
November 02, 2026 
 
 
Page 3 of 19 
Let me walk you through what we are seeing across the two business units, starting with banking 
and fintech. 
Global banking, as we all know, is in the middle of a fundamental transition from legacy process-
driven software towards agentic AI-native systems. Over the recent quarters, the speed of this 
change and regional geopolitical headwinds as well prompted banks to take a longer look at their 
technology roadmaps. While that stretched out some decision timelines and go-lives, the 
underlying shift plays directly to our strengths. Delayed implementations are largely back on 
schedule, and the near-term drag from those headwinds is behind us. 
Because we committed the capital and engineering bandwidth especially to build a genuinely built-
from-scratch AI-native banking stack, we are meeting the market with ready products just as the 
demand is inflecting. Commercial activity has picked up meaningfully, with several large deals in 
advanced stages and multiple proofs of concept running across Asia, across Europe, led by our 
agentic AI workflows and AI-native platforms in transaction banking trade finance. With our 
foundational architecture in place, we will ship brand-new AI-native software every single quarter 
this year, sometimes more than once in a quarter, helping clients turn this technology shift into 
measurable business results. 
Moving to our Technology Innovation Group, our bets in both transit payments as well as data 
centers are paying off, driving record additions to our order book and pipeline, as you would have 
seen. 
In transit, Aurionpro is firmly established as a premier partner powering India's automated fare 
collection ecosystem across flagship metro and mass transit systems. Having proven our full-stack 
execution at scale across domestic markets and selective global markets, we are taking this 
blueprint to international markets to capture the fast-growing global smart mobility opportunity. 
In data centers, rapid AI workload growth is creating extraordinary demand for high-density 
compute, and we are deepening our footprint through new mandates with leading hyperscalers. 
Our ambition on the data center business is clear. We are building the pre-eminent, independent, 
full-stack AI data center partner in the region, helping hyperscalers, helping AI clouds, and banks 
bring mission-critical capacity online faster with greater predictability. 
What ties transit and data centers together is our atoms-to-bits strategy, which we have talked 
about before, the conviction that the next technology infrastructure cycle belongs to firms fusing 
intelligent software with precision hardware. 
Building on our proven transit manufacturing footprint, we are integrating backward to 
manufacture critical components for both next-generation data centers and mass transit networks. 

                                              Aurionpro Solutions Limited 
 
 
November 02, 2026 
 
 
Page 4 of 19 
Controlling the stack end-to-end gives us tighter command over quality, timelines, and unit 
economics, driving structural margin efficiencies at scale as India's high-tech manufacturing 
expands and we become a key player in it. 
Across H1 FY27, our product investments are converting into commercial velocity, as you have seen. 
As global enterprises embark on history's largest technology cycle to re-architect for the age of AI, 
our priority is capturing long-term growth rather than near-term margin maximization through 
disciplined investments across our businesses. 
Our H1 performance reflects this planned R&D front-loading and related development cost 
capitalization to launch platforms like Verdict for onboarding, Infinity OS, Lexsi Labs offerings, etc 
We believe the incremental intensity of this R&D ramp that we went through, it peaked in H1 and 
will moderate going forward. We head into the second half backed by an order book of more than 
INR 2,000 crores, a deep pipeline, and accelerating execution. Our outlook for H2 remains strong, 
and we remain focused on executing towards the “Vision 2030” and compounding long-term 
shareholder value. 
I want to thank Aurionpro teams around the world for their discipline, for customer focus, and hard 
work over the past six months. 
With that, I will hand it back to the moderator, and let's begin the Q&A. 
Moderator: 
Thank you very much, sir. Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin the question-and-answer 
session. Participants who wish to ask questions through audio and video can do so by pressing the 
Raise Hand icon at the bottom of your screen and wait for your turn to speak. When prompted, you 
can accept the prompt on your screen, unmute your audio and video, introduce the firm you 
represent, and ask your questions or give comments. Participants who wish to ask questions via 
chat can click on the Q&A icon at the bottom of your screen and post your questions. Ladies and 
gentlemen, we will wait for a moment while the question queue assembles. The first question from 
the line of Kunal Bajaj. 
Kunal Bajaj: 
Hi. Good morning, and congratulations on the results. I have broadly three questions. Firstly, you

session. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Ashish Rai: 
Thank you, and good morning, everyone, and welcome to our Q2 FY27 Earnings Call. 
This quarter marks an important operational step up for Aurionpro. 
We delivered INR 415 crores in revenue, up 16% both year-on-year as well as quarter-on-quarter 
sequentially. Crossing quarterly revenue threshold for the first time ever establishes a strong 
baseline for the quarters ahead. We achieved this growth while preserving solid profitability, even 
as we absorbed input cost pressures, we absorbed and maintained an aggressive pace of R&D 
investment. 
For the quarter, EBITDA came in at INR 71 crores at a 17.2% margin, and PAT stood at INR 50 crores 
at a 12% margin. 
Following a quiet start to the fiscal year, momentum is visibly building. When an industry undergoes 
a generational technology shift like we are going through, it calls for a disproportionate 
commitment to product innovation. We lean into that investment cycle early, and this quarter, we 
are beginning to see clear market validation of our roadmap. 

                                              Aurionpro Solutions Limited 
 
 
November 02, 2026 
 
 
Page 3 of 19 
Let me walk you through what we are seeing across the two business units, starting with banking 
and fintech. 
Global banking, as we all know, is in the middle of a fundamental transition from legacy process-
driven software towards agentic AI-native systems. Over the recent quarters, the speed of this 
change and regional geopolitical headwinds as well prompted banks to take a longer look at their 
technology roadmaps. While that stretched out some decision timelines and go-lives, the 
underlying shift plays directly to our strengths. Delayed implementations are largely back on 
schedule, and the near-term drag from those headwinds is behind us. 
Because we committed the capital and engineering bandwidth especially to build a genuinely built-
from-scratch AI-native banking stack, we are meeting the market with ready products just as the 
demand is inflecting. Commercial activity has picked up meaningfully, with several large deals in 
advanced stages and multiple proofs of concept running across Asia, across Europe, led by our 
agentic AI workflows and AI-native platforms in transaction banking trade finance. With our 
foundational architecture in place, we will ship brand-new AI-native software every single quarter 
this year, sometimes more than once in a quarter, helping clients turn this technology shift into 
measurable business results. 
Moving to our Technology Innovation Group, our bets in both transit payments as well as data 
centers are paying off, driving record additions to our order book and pipeline, as you would have 
seen. 
In transit, Aurionpro is firmly established as a premier partner powering India's automated fare 
collection ecosystem across flagship metro and mass transit systems. Having proven our full-stack 
execution at scale across domestic markets and selective global markets, we are taking this 
blueprint to international markets to capture the fast-growing global smart mobility opportunity. 
In data centers, rapid AI workload growth is creating extraordinary demand for high-density

Return on Capital Employed is calculated as EBIT divided by Capital employed. Capital employed is calculated as the sum of Total equity (including non-controlling interest), Non-current borrowings and Current 
borrowings while EBIT is calculated as Profit for the year add Finance costs, Total tax expenses; Return on Equity is calculated as Profit for the year (Excluding share of non-controlling interest) divided by Total equity 
(Excluding non-controlling interest); Net Debt to equity (in times) is calculated as the net debt divided by total equity (including non-controlling interest),where net debt represents sum of Non-current borrowings and 
Current borrowings less cash and cash equivalents; Net Working Capital Days is calculated as Net Working Capital divided by Revenue from Operations, multiplied by 365 days (for fiscal years). Net Working Capital is 
computed as Receivables plus Inventory plus Other Financial and current assets (excluding cash and cash equivalents and current investments) minus Payables and Other financial and current liabilities (excluding 
current borrowings).

To the Board of Directors of Campus Activewear Limited 
1. We have reviewed the accompanying Statement of unaudited financial results of Campus Activewear 
Limited (hereinafter referred to as “the Company”) for the quarter ended 30 September 2026 and year 
to date results for the period from 1 April 2026 to 30 September 2026 (‘the Statement”). 
2. 
This Statement, which is the responsibility of the Company's management and approved by its Board 
of Directors, has been prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement principles laid 
down in Indian Accounting Standard 34 “Interim Financial Reporting” (“Ind AS 34”), prescribed under 
Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013, and other accounting principles generally accepted in India 
and in compliance with Regulation 33 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended (“Listing Regulations”). 
Our responsibility is to issue a report on the Statement based on our review. 
3. We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagements 
(SRE) 2410 “Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the 
Entity”, issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. A review of interim financial 
information consists of making inquiries, primarily of persons responsible for financial and accounting 
matters, and applying analytical and other review procedures. A review is substantially less in scope 
than an audit conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing and consequently does not enable 
us to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant matters that might be identified 
in an audit. Accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion. 
4. 
Based on our review conducted as above, nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe 
that the accompanying Statement, prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement 
principles laid down in the aforesaid Indian Accounting Standard and other accounting principles 
generally accepted in India, has not disclosed the information required to be disclosed in terms of 
Regulation 33 of the Listing Regulations, including the manner in which it is to be disclosed, or that it 
contains any material misstatement.

Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations 2015, this is to inform you that the Board of Directors of the company at its meeting 
held on Thursday, 05th November, 2026 commenced at 01:20 p.m. and concluded at 3.00 P.M., 
have inter alia:
a) Considered, approved and taken on record amongst other items of Agenda the Unaudited 
Financial Results of the Company for the second quarter & half year ended 30th September, 
2026, in compliance with Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations 2015. We are enclosing herewith the following:
1. The Un-audited Financial Results for the second quarter & half year ended 30th September, 
2026.
2. The Limited Review Report for the second quarter ended 30th September, 2026, issued by 
M/s. Das & Prasad, Chartered Accountants (Statutory Auditor of the Company).
b) Considered & approved the proposal to explore investment opportunities in the State of West 
Bengal and other regions over the coming years, with a strategic focus on specialised alloy & 
steel for railways, defense & aerospace applications, precision engineering, aluminum & copper 
alloys & its downstream products, conventional & renewal power in view of the upcoming 
industrial policy initiatives by the Government of West Bengal. The proposal also envisages 
exploring opportunities for collaboration and engagement with various State Governments and 
other relevant stakeholders for facilitating potential investments and business development.
This is for your information and record.
Thanking you.
Yours faithfully,
For Jai Balaji Industries Limited

In terms of the requirements of Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, and in continuation to our previous intimation(s) dated 
March 20, 2026 we hereby inform that the Hon’ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench, (“NCLT”) has passed

November 4, 2026 admitting the application with respect to the Composite Scheme of Arrangement amongst Thomas 
Cook (India) Limited (‘Demerged Company’ or ‘Transferee Company’ or ‘TCIL’) and Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited 
(‘Resulting Company’ or ‘SHRL’) and TC Visa Services (India) Limited (‘Transferor Company 1’ or ‘TCVSL’) and Jardin

17. Overview of the Scheme:  
“The Scheme is divided into following parts: 
1. PART I deals with the definitions of capitalized terms used in 
this Scheme, date of taking effect, operative date, sequencing of 
the Scheme, and the share capital of the Parties; 
2. PART II deals with the demerger of the Demerged 
Undertaking of TCIL into SHRL on a going concern basis, 
issuance of the Resulting Company New Shares by SHRL to the 
Eligible Shareholders in consideration thereof and matters 
incidental thereto;

TCIL of face value of INR 1 each into one share of face value 
of INR 4 each and matters incidental thereto; 
4. PART IV deals with the amalgamation of TCVSL, JTSL and 
BTSL with the Transferee Company; the consequent

5. PART V deals with reduction and reorganization of share

6. PART VI deals with the general terms and conditions that

18. The rationale for the scheme is as follows:    
1. TCIL, is a leading travel company in the country and has 
been offering inter alia broad spectrum of travel related 
services to its customers. TCIL owns and/or operates 
multiple resorts across India providing retreats in scenic 
locations amidst natural surroundings. 
2. It also has resorts which offer a host of curated services 
across multiple attractive market segments including: 
i. Adventure Holidays with experiences such as 
trekking, kayaking, rafting & zip lining, 
ii. Educational trips including survival skills, self-
defence, nature-appreciation etc. for resilience/ 
adaptability for students and corporates; 
iii. Corporate Getaways for team building activities, 
wellness & leadership development programs etc. 
3. SHRL, a wholly owned subsidiary of TCIL has a wide range 
of experience of running and operating resort business,

catering to a different demographic and offering more 
unique and curated experiences. 
4. TCIL and SHRL's Management believes that the Resort 
Business of TCIL would reap more benefit from being owned 
and operated by SHRL in light of their vast expertise in the 
hospitality industry. 
5. Further, SHRL's Management is of the view that SHRL has 
matured over the years and is well poised to chart its own 
growth path and operate as a separate listed entity in the 
fast-growing hospitality industry. 
6. Accordingly, the Management of TCIL is of the view that for 
better focus and maximum result, it is better to divest the 
Resort Business into SHRL and subsequently list SHRL. 
7. The main objective of the proposed restructuring, by way of 
a composite scheme, is to re-organize and segregate the 
different business verticals and focus on core businesses, in 
compliance with relevant regulations. In this manner, the 
two listed entities can each pursue growth opportunities that 
are more aligned with their own industry dynamics, leading 
to improved operational efficiencies and profitability. 
8. The Management of TCIL believes that the proposed 
consolidation of the face value of its equity shares will result 
in a significant improvement in certain key financial ratios. 
This enhancement in ratios is expected to better reflect the 
true market value of the TCIL's shares, aligning the share 
price more appropriately with its intrinsic value. 
9. Such consolidation of share capital is also anticipated to 
convey stronger financial stability and valuation metrics, 
thereby presenting a more accurate picture of the 
Company's financial strength and long-term prospects.

responsibility is to express a conclusion on the Statement based on our review. 
 
3. We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagements (SRE) 2410 'Review of Interim 
Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the Entity' issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI). 
This standard requires that we plan and perform the review to obtain moderate assurance as to whether the Statement is free from material 
misstatement. A review of interim financial information consists of making inquiries, primarily of the Company's personnel responsible for

conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing specified under Section 143(10) of the Companies Act, 2013 and consequently does not

not express an audit opinion.

Consolidated) along with the Limited Review Reports issued by M/s. B D Bansal, Chartered Accountants, Statutory

with relevant circulars issued by stock exchanges in this regard, the following disclosures are being made

Review Report 
To the Board of Directors 
Ceigall India Limited 
 
1. We have reviewed the accompanying statement of unaudited standalone financial results of Ceigall India Limited (" the Company") for the 
quarter ended 30 September 2026 and the year to date results from April 1, 2026 to 30 September 2026 (" the Statement"), attached herewith 
including five jointly controlled operations, CIL-Shiva (JV), CIL-IMC(JV), CIL-PEL (JV), CIL-JSSPL(JV) and CIL-SAM(JV) (hereinafter 
collectively referred to as “The Company”) being submitted by the Company pursuant to the requirements of Regulation 33 of the SEBI 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended ("the Listing Regulations"). 
 
2. The Statement, which is the responsibility of the Company's Management and has been approved by the Company's Board of Directors, has 
been prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement principles laid down in the Indian Accounting Standard 34, "Interim 
Financial Reporting" ("Ind AS 34") prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act,2013 as amended, read with relevant rules issued 
thereunder and other accounting principles generally accepted in India and in compliance with Regulation 33 of the Listing Regulations. Our 
responsibility is to express a conclusion on the Statement based on our review. 
 
3. We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagements (SRE) 2410 'Review of Interim 
Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the Entity' issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI). 
This standard requires that we plan and perform the review to obtain moderate assurance as to whether the Statement is free from material 
misstatement. A review of interim financial information consists of making inquiries, primarily of the Company's personnel responsible for 
financial and accounting matters and applying analytical and other review procedures. A review is substantially less in scope than an audit 
conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing specified under Section 143(10) of the Companies Act, 2013 and consequently does not 
enable us to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant matters that might be identified in an audit. Accordingly, we do 
not express an audit opinion. 
 
4. Based on our review conducted as stated above, nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe that the accompanying Statement, 
prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement principles laid down in the aforesaid Indian Accounting Standard ("Ind AS") 
specified under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 as amended, read with relevant rules issued thereunder and other accounting principles 
generally accepted in India, has not disclosed the information required to be disclosed in terms of Regulation 33 of the Listing Regulations, 
including the manner in which it is to be disclosed, or that it contains any material misstatement. 
 
 
5. Emphasis of Matter

(before consolidation adjustments) total assets of Rs. 492.37 million as at 30th September,2026 and total revenues of Rs. 491.25 million and

on the report of the other auditors and the procedures performed by us as stated in paragraph 3 above.  
 
Our conclusion on the statement is not modified in respect of the above matter.

Subject: Outcome of the Board Meeting held today i.e. Thursday, November 05, 2026 
 
Dear Sir/Madam,  
 
In continuation of our letters dated October 27, 2026 and November 02, 2026 and in terms of Regulation 30 of SEBI 
you that the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today i.e., Thursday, November 05, 2026, inter alia, 
considered and approved the following: 
 
1. Pursuant to Regulation 33 of SEBI Listing Regulation, the Unaudited Financial Results (Standalone and 
Consolidated) along with the Limited Review Reports issued by M/s. B D Bansal, Chartered Accountants, Statutory 
Auditors of the Company for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026, which have been duly reviewed 
and recommended by the Audit Committee. 
 
Further, pursuant to SEBI Circular HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated January 30, 2026, read 
with relevant circulars issued by stock exchanges in this regard, the following disclosures are being made 
 
A. Financial Results  are enclosed herewith as Annexure-I. 
B. Statement on deviation or variation for proceeds of public issue, rights issue, preferential issue, qualified 
institutions placement etc.  Not Applicable. 
C. Disclosure of outstanding default on loans and debt securities  Enclosed as Annexure-IA.  
D. Disclosure of related party transactions  will be filed along with XBRL for financial results.  
 
2. Raising funds upto Rs. 1000 Crores by way of issuance of equity shares and/or any other securities, including 
but not limited to securities convertible into Equity Shares (including warrants, or otherwise), fully convertible 
debentures, partly convertible debentures, convertible preference shares, non-convertible debentures with or 
without warrants, global depository receipts, American depository receipts, foreign currency convertible bonds, 
foreign currency exchangeable bonds or any security convertible into Equity Shares, or any combination thereof or 
further public 
offer, preferential issue, rights issue, private placement including a qualified institutions placement, offshore 
offerings or any other method or combination of methods as may be considered appropriate or necessary and as 
permitted under applicable laws, subject to such regulatory / statutory approvals as may be required and subject to 
approval of Shareholders of the Company by way of special resolution through Postal Ballot. Details as required 
under Regulation 30 of SEBI Listing Regulations read with SEBI Master Circular dated January 30, 2026, are given 
in Annexure-II. 
 
the structure and form of the issuance, issue price, timing, terms and conditions thereof, and all other matters 
connected with or incidental to the proposed fund raising, in accordance with applicable laws. 

 
 
 
3. Increase in Authorized Share Capital of the Company from the existing Authorised Share Capital of Rs. 
110,00,00,000/- (Rupees One Hundred Ten Crore) to Rs. 120,00,00,000/- (Rupees One Hundred and Twenty

Committee, subject to approval of Shareholders of the Company. It is hereby affirmed that Mr. Chandan Singh is

The Details as required under Regulation 30 of SEBI Listing Regulations read with SEBI Master Circular dated 
January 30, 2026, are given in Annexure-III.

Independent Auditor's Review Report on the unaudited Quarterly and Year to date Standalone Financial Results of Ceigall India 
Limited ("the Company") pursuant to the Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulation 
2015, as amended 
 
Review Report 
To the Board of Directors 
Ceigall India Limited 
 
1. We have reviewed the accompanying statement of unaudited standalone financial results of Ceigall India Limited (" the Company") for the 
quarter ended 30 September 2026 and the year to date results from April 1, 2026 to 30 September 2026 (" the Statement"), attached herewith 
including five jointly controlled operations, CIL-Shiva (JV), CIL-IMC(JV), CIL-PEL (JV), CIL-JSSPL(JV) and CIL-SAM(JV) (hereinafter 
collectively referred to as “The Company”) being submitted by the Company pursuant to the requirements of Regulation 33 of the SEBI 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended ("the Listing Regulations"). 
 
2. The Statement, which is the responsibility of the Company's Management and has been approved by the Company's Board of Directors, has 
been prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement principles laid down in the Indian Accounting Standard 34, "Interim 
Financial Reporting" ("Ind AS 34") prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act,2013 as amended, read with relevant rules issued 
thereunder and other accounting principles generally accepted in India and in compliance with Regulation 33 of the Listing Regulations. Our 
responsibility is to express a conclusion on the Statement based on our review. 
 
3. We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagements (SRE) 2410 'Review of Interim 
Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the Entity' issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI). 
This standard requires that we plan and perform the review to obtain moderate assurance as to whether the Statement is free from material 
misstatement. A review of interim financial information consists of making inquiries, primarily of the Company's personnel responsible for 
financial and accounting matters and applying analytical and other review procedures. A review is substantially less in scope than an audit 
conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing specified under Section 143(10) of the Companies Act, 2013 and consequently does not 
enable us to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant matters that might be identified in an audit. Accordingly, we do 
not express an audit opinion. 
 
4. Based on our review conducted as stated above, nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe that the accompanying Statement, 
prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement principles laid down in the aforesaid Indian Accounting Standard ("Ind AS") 
specified under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 as amended, read with relevant rules issued thereunder and other accounting principles 
generally accepted in India, has not disclosed the information required to be disclosed in terms of Regulation 33 of the Listing Regulations, 
including the manner in which it is to be disclosed, or that it contains any material misstatement. 
 
 
5. Emphasis of Matter 
i. 
We did not review the interim financial results of two Jointly Controlled Operations whose interim unaudited financial results reflect 
(before consolidation adjustments) total assets of Rs. 492.37 million as at 30th September,2026 and total revenues of Rs. 491.25 million and 
Rs. 491.25 million, total net profit after tax of Rs. 0.27 million and Rs. 0.27 million and total comprehensive income of Rs. 0.27 million and 
Rs. 0.27 million for the quarter ended 30th September, 2026 and for the period from April 1, 2026 to 30th September, 2026 respectively. These 
interim financial results have been reviewed by other auditors whose reports have been furnished to us by the Management and our conclusion 
on the Statement, in so far as it relates to the amounts and disclosures included in respect of these Jointly Controlled Operations is based solely 
on the report of the other auditors and the procedures performed by us as stated in paragraph 3 above.  
 
Our conclusion on the statement is not modified in respect of the above matter.
