Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Puravankara Limited Q2 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call hosted by Dolat Capital. 
 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance 
during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touchtone 
phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Ms. Savita Singh from Dolat Capital. Thank you, and over to 
you, ma'am. 
Savita Singh: 
Thank you, Alriac. Good morning, everyone. I, Savita Singh, on behalf of Dolat Capital, 
welcome you all to the Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call of Puravankara Limited. I would 
like to thank the management for giving us this opportunity to host the call. 
 
Today from the management team, we have with us Mr. Ashish Puravankara, Managing 
Director; Mr. Mallanna Sasalu, CEO-South; Mr. Rajat Rastogi, CEO-West & Commercial 
Assets; and Mr. Neeraj Gautam, CFO. 
 
I now hand over the call to the management for their opening remarks. Over to you, sir. 
Neeraj Gautam: 
Thank you, Savita. Good morning, everyone. I'm Neeraj Gautam, Chief Financial Officer of 
Puravankara Limited. Thank you for joining us to discuss our second quarter and first half FY27 
performance. 
 
Our results and investor presentation are available on the stock exchanges and in our website. 
 
Please also refer to the forward-looking statement disclaimer in the presentation. The central 
message this quarter is that stronger sales are being accompanied by better collection, faster 
customer handovers and a meaningful reduction in net debt. 
 
These developments are important because for a real estate company, sustainable growth is not 
measured by booking alone, it must also be in execution, cash generation and strength of the 
balance sheet. Coming to our operating performance. This quarter, we recorded presales of 
INR2,762 crores, up by 109% year-on-year on sales volume of 2.38 million square feet. 
 
Average price realization rose 32% to INR11,607 per square feet and customer collections grew 
by 24% year-on-year to INR1,301 crores. For the first half of FY27, total revenue grew 60% 
year-on-year to INR1,928 crores. We reported a profit after tax of INR107 crores. Residential 
and commercial sales for the period stood at INR3,575 crores. In addition, we monetized 
approximately 5.46 lakh square feet of commercial office space at Purva Zentech for an asset 
value of INR626 crores, which is also reflected in this quarter's presales. 
 
Together these take our total sales achievement for the first half of year to INR4,200 crores or 
37.51% of our annual sales guidance of INR11,200 crores. Our growth is therefore supported by 
both our established South India base and increasingly meaningful contribution from the 
Western markets. Now coming to the collection and execution. Customer collection rose 24% 

  
 
Puravankara Limited 
 
 
November 03, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 14 
 
to INR1,301 crores in Q2 and reached INR2,500 crores for the first half year, up by 31%. These 
collections are important to sustaining construction progress and managing our funding 
requirements. 
 
We handed over 977 homes covering approximately 0.97 million square feet during the quarter, 
taking first half handover to 1,722 homes. Consistent delivery remains priority both for our 
customers and for the conversion of our development activity into recognizing earnings. 
 
Our priority is to preserve this connection between sales, construction, collection and delivery 
rather than treating any one metric as a full measure of performance. Coming to our financial 
performance. Revenue from operation rose to INR1,033 crores compared to INR644 crores a 
year earlier. 
 
Total income increased 59% to INR1,051 crores and EBITDA was INR289 crores, representing 
margin of 27%. Profit after tax was INR82 crores compared to the loss of INR42 crores in Q2 
FY26. For H1, total income grew 60% to INR1,928 crores and profit after tax was INR107 crores 
against a loss of INR111 crores a year ago. The quarter includes an exceptional gain of INR149 
crores, which we've distinguished from recurring operating performance, higher handover 
supported revenue integration, and our focus remains on improving the consistency of earnings 
over time. Coming to the cash flow and capital management. 
 
Our direct cash flow statement shows an operating surplus of INR596 crores for Q2 and INR413 
crores after net interest and tax. We also made meaningful progress on leverage. Gross debt 
declined by approximately INR180 crores to INR3,763 crores, while net debt reduced by 
INR470 crores to INR2,366 crores. 
 
Net debt-to-equity ratio to 1.26x and our weighted average cost of debt declined to 10.94%. In 
September, we completed the Purva Zentech-Exit at an enterprise value of approximately NR 
626 crores. This reflects our focus on recycling capital from mature assets to support future 
growth. The transition is reported separately from the regular project presales. 
 
Coming to the development pipeline and outlook for the rest of the half year. At the end of 
September, our ongoing portfolio comprised of 33.61 million square feet. We also had a planned 
launch program of 14.5 million square feet with estimated GDV of approximately INR22,600 
crores subject to approvals on launch readiness. 
 
During H1, we added development opportunity with an estimated GDV of INR14,100 crores 
across Bengaluru, Mumbai, Greater Noida, strengthening both our redevelopment portfolio and 
the geographic reach. Our FY27 sales guidance remains INR11,200 crores, including the 
Zentech transaction. 
 
First half sales asset monetization totaled approximately INR4,201 crores, equivalent to 37.5% 
of our guidance of this combined value basis. For the remainder of the year, our priorities are to 
execute planned launches, sustain collection, deliver homes on schedule and improve capital 
efficiency. We remain committed to pursuing growth responsibly and creating lasting value for 
our customers and shareholders.

Item No. 1: To approve appointment of Mr. Sunil Kumar Chugh (DIN: 08309168) as a Director 
of the Company: 
 
In accordance with the special rights granted to the promoters of the Company by the 
Shareholders through a Special Resolution passed by way of Postal Ballot on December 7, 2025, 
which entitles them to nominate up to two Non-Independent Directors each on the Board of 
the Company, the Company has received the letter dated October 12, 2026 from Canara Bank 
intimating about nominating Mr. Sunil Kumar Chugh (DIN: 08309168) on the Board of the 
Company.  
 
In terms of Sections 152, 160, 161 of the Companies Act, 2013 (“the Act”), the Board of 
Directors of the Company, based on the recommendation of the Nomination and 
Remuneration Committee had reviewed the candidature of Mr. Sunil Kumar Chugh  
(DIN: 08309168) and appointed him as an Additional Director (Non-Executive                                        
Non-Independent) with effect from October 27, 2026, liable to retire by rotation. In the opinion 
of the Board, Mr. Sunil Kumar Chugh (DIN: 08309168) meet the fit and proper criteria and is 
person of integrity, and have the necessary knowledge, experience and expertise for being 
appointed as a Director of the Company, liable to retire by rotation. 
 
Mr. Sunil Kumar Chugh (DIN: 08309168) is a Chartered Accountant and a Certified Associate 
of the Indian Institute of Bankers by qualification, has over 33 years of banking experience. 
Began the career in 1993 and risen through the ranks serving in five public sector banks such 
as Punjab National Bank, Oriental Bank of Commerce, Union Bank of India, Punjab & Sind Bank 
and Dena Bank, gaining deep expertise through diverse functional roles and leadership 
responsibilities. Over the years, led key business and operations verticals, including Corporate 
Credit, Retail, Agri & MSME (RAM) Credit, Financial Inclusion, Stressed Assets Management 
and Credit Monitoring. Headed Large Corporate Branches in Mumbai, Kolkata and 
Ahmedabad. Mr. Chugh’s role spanned Corporate Office, Administrative Offices and Branches, 
combining field-level exposure with strategic insights. He has served as Director on the Boards 
of PNB Cards & Services Limited and Swift India Domestic Services Private Limited. Currently, 
holding the position of Executive Director of Canara Bank effective from November 24, 2025. 
 
Mr. Sunil Kumar Chugh (DIN: 08309168) does not hold any shares in the Company. 
 
Mr. Sunil Kumar Chugh (DIN: 08309168) has furnished the necessary consent, declarations, 
and disclosures for his appointment as required under the Act, SEBI (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“Listing Regulations”), SEBI (Mutual Funds) 
Regulations, 2026 and other applicable statutory provisions.  
 
In terms of Section 160 of the Act, the Company has received a notice in writing from Canara 
Bank proposing the candidature of Mr. Sunil Kumar Chugh (DIN: 08309168) for the office of 
Director on the Board of the Company. 
 
Mr. Sunil Kumar Chugh (DIN: 08309168) is not related to any other Director and Key 
Managerial Personnel of the Company. However, Mr. Sunil Kumar Chugh (DIN: 08309168) and 
Mr. Santanu Kumar Majumdar (DIN: 08223415), Non-Executive Non-Independent Directors 
are associated with Canara Bank and are connected only by virtue of their affiliation with 
Canara Bank.

Institute of Company Secretaries of India is annexed to this Notice.

Began the career in 1993 and risen through the ranks serving in five public sector banks such 
as Punjab National Bank, Oriental Bank of Commerce, Union Bank of India, Punjab & Sind Bank 
and Dena Bank, gaining deep expertise through diverse functional roles and leadership 
responsibilities. Over the years, led key business and operations verticals, including Corporate 
Credit, Retail, Agri & MSME (RAM) Credit, Financial Inclusion, Stressed Assets Management 
and Credit Monitoring. Headed Large Corporate Branches in Mumbai, Kolkata and 
Ahmedabad. Mr. Chugh’s role spanned Corporate Office, Administrative Offices and Branches, 
combining field-level exposure with strategic insights. He has served as Director on the Boards 
of PNB Cards & Services Limited and Swift India Domestic Services Private Limited. Currently, 
holding the position of Executive Director of Canara Bank effective from November 24, 2025.

PRESS RELEASE 
GACL reports Highest-Ever Quarterly and Half Yearly Revenue in FY 
2026-27. 
Improved Sales Realizations, focus on improving operating performance, higher 
renewable energy 
integration 
and strategic 
growth 
projects 
reinforce 
the 
Company's long-term value creation roadmap. 
The Board of Directors, at its meeting held on 5th November, 2026 at 
Ahmedabad approved the Unaudited Financial Results for the 2nd quarter 
ended on 30th September, 206 on standalone as well as consolidated 
basis. 
Smt. Avantika Singh, IAS, Managing Director of the Company said "The 
Company's growth momentum continues during the 2nd quarter and the 
Company achieved the highest ever Quarterly as well as Half Yearly Sales 
revenue in the last two decades during financial Year 2026-27. For 2nd 
Quarter, Sales Revenue has increased by Rs.271.60 Crores (i.e. by 26°/o) 
to 
Rs.1,334.79 
Crores 
as 
compared 
to 
Rs.1,063.19 
Crores 
in 
the 
corrsponding quarter of previous year and for first Half Year, Sales 
Revenue has increased by Rs.422.99 Crores (i.e. by 20°/o) to Rs.2559.63 
Crores as compared to Rs.2,136.64 Crores in the corresponding period of 
previous year." 
She further shared that in spite of the ongoing geopolitical situation, the 
Company could achieve highest ever quarterly and half yearly revenue on 
account of better sales realizations by product mix optimization, increased 
share of renewable energy and expanding product footprint through new 
.· ... export markets. EBITDA for the quarter increased by Rs.88.67 Crores (i.e. 
by 67°/o) to Rs.221.86 Crores as compared to EBITDA of Rs.133.19 Crores 
in the corresponding quarter of previous year. 
Profit Before Tax for the 
quarter has ·increased by Rs.88.62 Crores (i.e. by 657°/o) to Rs.102.10 
Crores as compared to Profit Before Tax of Rs.13.48 Crores in the 
corresponding quarter of previous year. ' 
EBITDA for the first Half Year increased by Rs.192.91 Crores (i.e. by 75°/o) 
to Rs.451.19 Crores as compared to EBITDA of Rs.258.28 Crores in the 
corresponding period of previous year. Profit Before Tax for the first Half 
increased by Rs.189.11 Crores (i.e. by 821%) to Rs.212.14 Crores as 
compared to Rs.23.03 Crores in the corresponding period of the previous 
year. 
Energy has remained our continuous focused area and during the second 
quarter of FY 2026-27, the Company could reduce energy costs as 
compared to corresponding quarter of 
previous year on account of 
increased share of renewable power. During the second quarter of FY 2026-

•' 
27, the share of renewable energy has increased to 55°/o from 38°/o and 
during the first half the share of renewable energy has increased to 57°/o 
from 38°/o in corresponding period of the previous year. This aligns with the 
Board's directive to expand renewable power usage and supports India's 
net-zero carbon commitments. 
She further said "The Board of Directors also reviewed various ongoing 
projects worth rvRs.2100 Crores which were approved by the Board earlier 
which 
include, 
inter-alia, 
Phosphoric 
Acid 
Plant-II, 
E-g'rade 
H202, 
Investments in Renewable Energy SPVs etc. During FY26-27, the Company 
will complete project implementation of various projects viz. HCL Synthesis, 
Caustic Soda Flaking Unit, Upgradation of Electro/yzers and Chlorotoluene 
Downstream, which would add to the revenue growth, enhance operating 
efficiency and reduce overall cost of the Company. The rest of the projects 
will be completed during FY 27-:28 & FY 28-29. This would be in line with 
the Vision 2047 document in line with the Hon'ble Prime Minister's national 
vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. H 
The Company continues to drive efficiency through Project Ahvaan, 
focusing on enhancin9 operating efficiency, cost cutting across various 
functional 
areas, 
optimum 
capacity 
utilization 
of 
various 
plants, 
enhancement of green energy in overall power basket of the Company, 
working on organization structure including talent management, capability 
enhancement, digitization & usage of AI, etc. These initiatives are expected 
to contribute to improved operational efficiencies in the short to long term. 
***** 
About Gujarat Alkalies and Chemicals Limited 
Gujarat Alkalies and Chemicals Limited (GACL) was established in 1973 in Vadodara, 
Gujarat, to manufacture Caustic Soda and allied products. Promoted by the Government of 
Gujarat, GACL has emerged as one of the largest manufacturers of caustic soda, employing 
cutting-edge 
technology, 
groundbreaking 
research 
and 
development, 
and 
strategic 
.j·diversification. From an initial capacity of 37.425 TPA caustic soda, the organization has 
enhanced its capacity to 8,52,400 TP A, with manufacturing facilities spread over four 
complexes, two in Vadodara and two in Dahej. GACL now offers more than 35 products used 
as raw materials in various industries. By providing quality raw materials used in numerous 
applications, GACL contributes to the growth of the chemical industry in the country.
